- Console Tab

## Importing and Exporting Keyboard Shortcut Information

You can import and export your keyboard shortcut specifications so that your preferences are preserved across systems. This topic describes how to import and export the keyboard shortcut information.

To import or export keyboard shortcuts from a file:

1. In the Custom Compiler window, choose Window &gt; Keyboard Shortcuts .

The Keyboard Shortcuts dialog box opens.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

2. To import a file:
- a. Click Load .
- b. In the Open dialog box, locate the keyboard shortcuts file that you want to import, and click Open .

The imported keyboard shortcut information appears in the dialog box.

3. To export the keyboard shortcut information:
- a. Click Export .
- b. In the Save As dialog box, navigate to the target folder and type a name for the exported file.
- c. Click Save .

## Restricting Design Access to Read-Only

You can restrict design access to read-only so that users can open and view them, but they cannot modify the designs. Use one of the following methods to make designs readonly:

| Scope                                                          | Method                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|----------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Designs in all libraries (entire Custom Compiler session)      | When starting Custom Compiler, type the following at the Linux prompt: custom_compiler -readOnly true For more information, see custom_compiler Command Syntax and Arguments.                                                                       |
| Designs in a specific library (entire Custom Compiler session) | Add the following statement in the lib.defs file: ASSIGN <libName> libMode readOnly For more information about lib.defs files, see Controlling Library Availability.                                                                                |
| Specific design                                                | When opening a design using the Library Manager, right-click the design's view name, and then choose Open Read-Only . For details, see Opening Designs. If you have already opened a design and want to make it read-only, see Changing Edit Modes. |

By default, when libraries or designs are in the read-only mode, buttons and menu commands that let you modify the design are dimmed. If you want to hide the disabled buttons and menu commands, set the giHideAutoDisabled Tcl preference to true .

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Supplying Mapping Files for GDSII Stream and OASIS Format Translations

To successfully import and export design data in GDSII Stream format, you need to supply mapping files to permit name conversions for cells, fonts, labels, layers, objects, properties, and references.

- Layer Mapping Files
- Object Mapping Files
- Cell Mapping Files
- Font Mapping Files (GDSII Stream Only)
- Label Mapping Files (GDSII Stream Only)
- Property Mapping Files (GDSII Stream Only)
- Property Mapping Files (OASIS Only)
- Reference Mapping Files (GDSII Stream Only)
- Text Mapping Files

## Layer Mapping Files

The layer mapping file maps OpenAccess (OA) layer/purpose names to GDSII or OASIS layer number and data types. The file is used for both importing and exporting design data in the GDSII Stream and OASIS formats.

This section describes the following:

- Layer Mapping File Format and Contents
- OA, GDSII, and OASIS Mappings
- Mask Color and Color Lock Attributes
- Material and Mask Number Attributes
- Cut Size Attribute

- Mapping OpenAccess Objects in the Layer Mapping File
- Examples

For instructions on importing and exporting design data in the GDSII Stream format, see Importing Designs in GDSII Stream Format and Exporting Designs in GDSII Stream Format.

For instructions on importing and exporting design data in the OASIS format, see Importing Designs in OASIS Format and Exporting Designs in OASIS format .

## Layer Mapping File Format and Contents

All layer mapping files are in the ASCII format. The syntax for each line in the file is as follows:

oaLayerName oaPurposeName gdsLayer# gdsDataType# [color:colorName [colorLock]] [Material [maskNumber | cutSize]]

| Field           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|-----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| oaLayerName     | (Required) The name of the layer in the OA database. For more information, see OA, GDSII, and OASIS Mappings.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| oaPurposeName   | (Required) The purpose of the OA layer. For more information, see OA, GDSII, and OASIS Mappings.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| gdsLayer％       | (Required) The layer number in the GDS or OASIS. For more information, see OA, GDSII, and OASIS Mappings.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| gdsDataType％    | (Required) The data type number in the GDS or OASIS. The GDS or OASIS data type number can be a single number or a range of numbers. For example, the following are valid values for gdsDataType# : 1, 2, 5, or 0-255. For more information, see OA, GDSII, and OASIS Mappings.                                                                                                                                     |
| color:colorName | (Optional) A mask color. The colorName must be preceded by the keyword color, followed by a colon (for example, color:red). The color names you supply must be defined in the technology file, or they must have the value same . If no color information is supplied in the file, the translator assumes that the shape on the layer has no color. For more information, see Mask Color and Color Lock Attributes. |
| colorLock       | (Optional) The color lock status, which is only used if a colorName is specified, but it is not required. Valid values for colorLock are locked and unlocked . For more information, see Mask Color and Color Lock Attributes.                                                                                                                                                                                      |

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Field          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Material       | (Optional) The layer function name to map to or from the OA database. The layer function name is typically defined in the technology file. If you are importing a design to a library that does not have the information in its technology database, you can supply the information in the Material field of the layer mapping file. For more information, see Mask Color and Color Lock Attributes.                                   |
| maskNumber     | (Optional) The mask number that specifies the manufacturing order of the layers used in the design. If the Material value is cut , the maskNumber field is not used.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| cutSize        | (Optional) The dimensions of the rectangular cut, <dimension1>:<dimension2> . The dimension values must be preceded by the keyword CUTSIZE , followed by a colon (for example, CUTSIZE:0.032:0.032). The Material field can be used to specify different mappings for cut rectangles of different sizes. If the Material value is cut , the cut dimensions can follow in the same field. For more information, see Cut Size Attribute. |
| techLayerAlias | (Optional) The alias of the layers, as defined in the layerRules rule of the technology file. • For imported files,all source layer objects in a design changes to corresponding alias layer • For exported files, all alias layer objects in a design changes to corresponding source layer                                                                                                                                           |

The layer mapping file can contain the following optional lines:

- Comment lines that begin with the following character: ％. For example, a comment line can appear at the top of the file to label the fields.
- Blank lines. For example, you can add blank lines between sections of data. However, the translator ignores all blank lines in the file.

## OA, GDSII, and OASIS Mappings

Each line in the file specifies the following mappings:

- During import, shapes on the GDS or OASIS layer number and GDS or OASIS data type are written to the given OA layer name and OA layer purpose.
- During export, shapes on the OA layer name and OA layer purpose are written to the given GDS or OASIS layer number and GDS or OASIS data type.

<!-- image -->

Each line must contain a unique pair of GDS or OASIS layer number and GDS or OASIS data type number. However, an OA layer name and OA layer purpose pair can appear multiple times in the file for the following reasons:

- A shape on a particular OA layer can be written multiple times in the GDSII or OASIS database.
- Because mappings can include color and cut size information, an OA layer and purpose can appear multiple times. A line applies only to shapes that match the particular attributes.

In the following example, each of the two GDS layer number and GDS data type pairs is unique. However, the OA metal1 drawing layer is written two times in the GDS database.

<!-- image -->

## Mask Color and Color Lock Attributes

The optional mask color and color lock data is attributes of shapes that are on the layer described by each line. For any given color attribute, the color lock attribute is optional. In the following example, objects that are on the metal1 drawing layer have the color E1 . Because the line does not have a color lock value, the mapping applies to E1 -colored shapes on the metal1 drawing layer with either color lock status.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

A color attribute can have one of two color status: locked or unlocked . In the following example, if shapes that are on the metal1 drawing layer have the color E1 and the color is locked , they are mapped to GDS layer 1 and GDS data type 51 . If shapes that are on the metal1 drawing layer have the color E1 and the color is unlocked , they are mapped to GDS layer 1 and GDS data type 52 .

<!-- image -->

When exporting a design, you can choose which lines are used to map colored shapes:

- Use only the lines that contain the locked and unlocked keywords. Ignore the lines that do not contain the locked and unlocked keywords.
- Use only the lines that do not contain the locked and unlocked keywords. Ignore the lines that contain the locked and unlocked keywords.

You can make this selection using the Layer Map Colors check box in the Export Stream dialog box. For more information about the Export Stream dialog box, see Exporting Design Data in GDSII Stream Format and Exporting Design Data in OASIS Format.

The following formats are available when you import and export GDSII Stream:

```
· VIA1 drawing 1 0 cut CUTSIZE: 0.1: 0.1 mask1Color locked · VIA1 drawing 1 0 mask1Color locked cut CUTSIZE: 0.1: 0.1
```

## Note:

The values of the mask color and color lock attributes can be placed before or after the CUTSIZE column.

The following format is available when you import and export OASIS:

```
VIA1 drawing 1 0 mask1Color locked cut CUTSIZE: 0.1: 0.1
```

## Note:

The values of the mask color and color lock attributes must be placed before the CUTSIZE column.

## Material and Mask Number Attributes

The layer mapping file might contain Material and maskNumber data if you are importing a design to a library that does not have the information in its technology database. If you selected the AutoDetect Vias option in the Import Stream or Import OASIS dialog box, the translator uses these attributes to detect vias during the import process. Doing so stores vias as oaVias instead of oaInsts in the OA database, thus ensuring compactness and a more accurate representation.

For more information about the Import Stream dialog box, see the Importing Design Data in GDSII Stream Format. For more information about the Import OASIS dialog box, see the Importing Design Data in OASIS Format.

## Cut Size Attribute

If you are exporting a design, the Material field can contain cut size information in the following format:

cut CUTSIZE:&lt;dimension1&gt;:&lt;dimension2&gt;

where cut is the layer function name defined in the technology file.

The dimension values specify the dimensions of the rectangular cut, and the values should be floating numbers that specify the size in user units.

If the Material field contains cut information, the maskNumber field is not used.

## Note:

The cutSize attribute is ignored during import.

## Mapping OpenAccess Objects in the Layer Mapping File

PR Boundaries, Snap Boundaries, Area Blockages, and Layer Blockages objects can be exported to GDS and imported from GDS using the layer mapping file if the layer/purpose pairs shown in Table 10 are specified in the layer mapping file.

| OpenAccess Object   | Layer Name   | Purpose Name   | Keep Object Type with Property   |
|---------------------|--------------|----------------|----------------------------------|
| PR Boundary         | prBoundary   | boundary       | yes                              |
| Snap Boundary       | snap         | boundary       | yes                              |
| Area Blockage       | PinBorder    | blockage       | yes                              |

Table 10 Mapping OpenAccess Objects by Layer Purpose Pair

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Table 10 Mapping OpenAccess Objects by Layer Purpose Pair (Continued)

| OpenAccess Object   | Layer Name   | Purpose Name   | Keep Object Type with Property   |
|---------------------|--------------|----------------|----------------------------------|
| Layer Blockage      | Any OA layer | blockage       | yes                              |

## Note:

Object Mapping Files can work with this feature at the same time, but the object map has a higher priority than the layer mapping file.

## Examples

In the following example, color and color lock attributes are provided for the m1 layer. Red color-locked shapes on the m1 drawing layer are mapped using the first line. Blue colorunlocked shapes on the m1 drawing layer are mapped using the second line. E3 colorlocked shapes on the m1 drawing layer are mapped using the third line.

| # oaLayer ％   | oaPurpose   |   gds Layer# |   gdsData Type# | colorName   | colorLock   |
|---------------|-------------|--------------|-----------------|-------------|-------------|
| m1            | drawing     |            1 |              50 | color:red   | locked      |
| m1            | drawing     |            2 |              51 | color:blue  | unlocked    |
| m1            | drawing     |            3 |              52 | color:E3    | locked      |

In the following example, cut size attributes are provided for the v1 layer. Shapes that are 0.032 x 0.032 on the v1 layer are mapped using the first line. Shapes that are 0.064 x 0.064 on the v1 layer are mapped using the third line. Shapes that have other dimensions on the v1 layer are mapped using the second line.

| # oaLayer   | # oaPurpose   |   gds Layer# |   gdsData Type# | Material   | maskNumber          |
|-------------|---------------|--------------|-----------------|------------|---------------------|
| V1          | drawing       |           16 |               0 | cut        | CUTSIZE:0.032:0.032 |
| V1          | drawing       |           16 |               1 | cut        |                     |
| V1          | drawing       |           16 |              15 | cut        | CUTSIZE:0.064:0.064 |

## Object Mapping Files

This file specifies methods of mapping Boundaries and LayerBlockages between Stream shapes and OpenAccess databases.

This file is a text file that have a different number of fields for different initial keywords. Blank lines and lines starting with '％' are ignored. The first field is the object type name.

## For example, with industry-compatible keywords:

```
# Boundary    Subtype   GDS Layer     GDS Data Type Boundary      PR        27            4 Boundary      Snap      27            4 # Blockage    Subtype   oaLayer  GDS Layer GDS Data Type  Color layerBlockage routing   M1       191       31             color:red layerBlockage routing   M2       191       32             color:blue layerBlockage routing   M3       191       33             mask1color layerBlockage pin       M1       191       34             mask2color layerBlockage pin       M2       191       35 layerBlockage pin       M3       191       36
```

## For example, with first generation keywords (not supported for OASIS):

```
# Boundary      GDS Layer   GDS Data Type PRBoundary    27          4 # Blockage      oaLayer     GDS Layer   GDS Data Type LayerBlockage Metal5       52          2 LayerBlockage *            72          2
```

## Note:

Color can be specified as a layer mapping file for layerBlockage (with industry-compatible keywords only).

The tool supports to keep signal type in the object mapping file. The signal type can be mapped with the Term keyword. For example:

```
# Term    SigType  oaLayer  oaPurpose  GDS Layer GDS Data Type # Term    scan     m0       drawing    230       240 # Term    power    m1       drawing    230       241
```

## Cell Mapping Files

## Note:

For OASIS, cell mapping files are supported by the export process but not the import process.

The cell mapping file maps cell and port names during translation.

<!-- image -->

Chapter 3: Supplying Mapping Files for GDSII Stream and OASIS Format Translations Font Mapping Files (GDSII Stream Only)

<!-- image -->

The file can contain comment lines that begin with this character: ％.

The wildcard character (*) is allowed for GDSII Stream import and export for library names, OA cell names, and cell names when importing or exporting GDSII Stream files. A prefix and postfix can be combined with a wildcard for OA cell name and cell name. Only one wildcard is allowed for same library name, OA cell name, or cell name.

The system ignores blank lines.

Create an ASCII file formatted as follows:

```
<library name> <OA cell name > <view name> <cell name> For example: #lib name  OA cell name   view name   cell name Lib1  oa_cell1      layout      cell1 Lib2  oa_cell2      layout      cell2
```

## Font Mapping Files (GDSII Stream Only)

The font mapping file maps font IDs to OpenAccess font names.

The file can contain comment lines that begin with this character: ％.

The system ignores blank lines.

Create an ASCII file formatted as follows:

```
<font id> <OA font name>
```

## For example:

```
#stream ID  OA font name 0    EuroStyle 1    Roman 2    Gothic 3    Script
```

## Label Mapping Files (GDSII Stream Only)

The label mapping file is used by the translator to generate labels for OpenAccess objects.

The file also specifies which stream layers and data types should be used for the TEXT records that constitute each label.

The file is an ASCII files with either five or six white-space separated fields.

The file can contain comment lines that begin with this character: ％.

The system ignores blank lines.

## For example:

| # Object   | oaLayer   | oaPurpose   | GDS       |   GDS Data | Type   | oaSigType   |
|------------|-----------|-------------|-----------|------------|--------|-------------|
| Term       | Metal5    | drawing     | Layer 131 |          0 |        |             |
| Term       | Metal6    | drawing     | 132       |          0 |        |             |
| Net        | Metal6    | drawing     | 132       |          1 |        |             |
| Term       | Metal6    | drawing     | 132       |          2 |        | power       |
| Net        | Metal5    | drawing     | 131       |          3 |        | power       |

Label mapping provides support for multiple pinfigs or vias using the

dbExportStreamLabelMapWithMultiPinFig Tcl preference (false by default). By default, label mapping converts only one connected pinfig or via for the same term name or net name. When dbExportStreamLabelMapWithMultiPinFig is set to true, label mapping converts all connected pinfigs and vias for the same term name or net name. This preference corresponds to the option labelMapWithMultiPinFig in the exportStream binary. For example, assume there are three pins with same termName (a1), but on different layers (m1/drawing m2/drawing m3/pin), and the label mapping file defines "Term m2 drawing 10 0", "Term m1 drawing 8 0" and "Term m3 pin 12 0". The default label mapping generates only one label per shape because the three pins have the same termName (a1). If you use dbExportStreamLabelMapWithMultiPinFig true , label mapping generates three labels for three shapes.

## Property Mapping Files (GDSII Stream Only)

The property mapping file defines mappings between property names in the GDSII file and property IDs and object types in OpenAccess.

These object types are allowed: Dot, Line, Path, PathSeg Pin, Polygon, Rect, Text, ArrayInst and ScalarInst.

The file can contain comment lines that begin with this character: ％.

Create an ASCII file formatted as follows:

&lt;prop id&gt; &lt;object type&gt; &lt;OA prop name&gt;

## For example:

```
# stream ID    object         name 1            Rect         instP11 2            Polygon      poly1 3            Path         sigName 4            PathSeg      pathSegNet
```

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## The following is an example of using the Pin object type during export:

```
#stream ID        object            property name 4                  Pin              accessDir,pinName,termName,direction 5                  ScalarInst       instName
```

where accessDir , pinName , termName and direction are reserved keywords for the attributes of the oaPin object. You can define multiple keywords simultaneously using a property index, separating each name with a comma. They cannot be defined in duplicate in different lines. instName is a reserved keyword for the object types ScalarInst and ArrayInst for exporting the names of instances.

## Property Mapping Files (OASIS Only)

The property mapping file defines mappings between property names in the OASIS file and property IDs and object types in OpenAccess.

The following object types are allowed: Dot, Line, Path, PathSeg, Polygon, Rect, Text, ArrayInst, Pin and ScalarInst.

## Note:

Pin is used for exporting OASIS files only.

To export specific properties of object types in OpenAccess to OASIS properties, you must name the attributes of object properties in the mapping file as an &lt;id, value&gt; pair. &lt;id&gt; and &lt;value&gt; are string values.

The file can contain comment lines that begin with this character: ％.

Create an ASCII file formatted as follows:

```
<OA object type> <OA prop name>
```

## For example:

```
OA_object_type    OA_prop_name Rect            instP11 Polygon         poly1 Path            sigName Pin            accessDir,pinName,termName,direction ScalarInst     instName
```

## The following is an example of using the Pin object type during export:

```
#OA_object_type   OA_prop_name Pin                   accessDir,pinName,termName,direction ScalarInst            instName
```

where accessDir , pinName , termName and direction are reserved keywords for the attributes of the oaPin object. You can define multiple keywords simultaneously using a property index, separating each name with a comma. They cannot be defined in duplicate in different lines. instName is a reserved keyword for the object types ScalarInst and ArrayInst for exporting the names of instances.

<!-- image -->

## Reference Mapping Files (GDSII Stream Only)

The reference mapping file maps every structure the system writes to the stream file and to the source OpenAccess design. This includes PCell submasters, standard and custom vias, and PCell custom vias. PCells are identified by their override parameters. Vias include their viaDef name and standard vias include the values for any override viaParams.

## For example:

```
<!-- Created By exportStream G-2011.09 Started: Mon Mar 28 08:59:12 2012 (Hostname: Host1) --> <file-format version="1.0" name="synopsysExportStream"> <exportStream> <options lib="ADFULG" cell="AD4FUL" view="layout" gds=remote/us01home10/user11/bugs/gdsprb/chklibdef.gds hierDepth=2 noOutputBlockages text=cdba ver=3 /> <cellMappings> <mapping cellType="design" streamName="AD4FUL" lib="ADFULG" cell="AD4FUL" view="layout"/> <mapping cellType="design" streamName="p_4t_pcell_30136ea9a532e738c5494893f31a38a0" lib="generic90RF" cell="p_4t" view="layout"> <param name="nf" type="intParam">2</param> <param name="w" type="floatParam">0.00000058</param> <param name="tapBottom" type="stringParam"><![CDATA[all]]></param> <param name="drawWell" type="booleanParam">1</param> </mapping> <mapping cellType="stdvia" streamName="via12_stdvia_f67b15b30b330a6024d3f1bd9610d2c4" techLib="ADFULG" viaDef="via12"> <viaparams cutColumns="8" cutRows="2" layer1Enc="5.5,6.1"/> </mapping> <mapping cellType="customvia" streamName="via12_cust_pcell_8972b97befe9a7af324f4962de1704a0" lib="generic90RF" cell="via12_cust" view="layout" techLib="ADFULG" viaDef="via12"> <param name="columns" type="intParam">2</param> <param name="rows" type="intParam">8</param> </mapping> </cellMappings> </exportStream> </file-format>
```

## Text Mapping Files

A text mapping file is used to specify how to map text between an OASIS or a GDSII stream file and an OA database, and to process the text for conversion in an OA database.

A text mapping file maps individual characters and delimiters in text labels. For example, during the import process, you can map the text label IN[1] to IN&lt;1&gt; . You must prepare the text mapping file before you import your design.

## OASIS Text Mapping Files

The text mapping file syntax of each line for an OASIS file is as follows:

```
<cell-name> <layer-name> <layer-purpose> <text-mapping-string> <text-replacement-string>
```

| Field                   | Description                                                                                                   |
|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| cell-name               | The name of the cell in OASIS.                                                                                |
| layer-name              | The OASIS layer name.                                                                                         |
| layer-purpose           | The OASIS layer purpose.                                                                                      |
| text-mapping-string     | The current text match, that is, the text in OASIS that is replaced when it is imported into the OA database. |
| text-replacement-string | The text that replaces the OASIS text during the import process.                                              |

Each field can be a regular expression with support to recall the regular expression matches. Empty lines and lines that begin with the hash (％) character are ignored. The first match found in the text mapping file is used during conversion.

The following is an example of an OASIS text mapping file:

```
# cell-name layer-name layer-purpose text-mapping-string  text-replacement-string cell1     11         0             IMP<0>               IMP\[0\] cell2     .+         0            ([^<]+)<([^>]+)>      \1[\2] cell3     .+         .+           (^[^\[]+)\[([^\]]+)\] \L\1\E<\2>
```

## GDSII Stream Text Mapping Files

All text mapping files must be in the ASCII format. The syntax for each line is as follows:

```
<GDS cell name> <GDS layer #> <GDS data type> <Current text match> <Replacement text>
```

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Field              | Description                                                                |
|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| GDS cell name      | The name of the cell in GDS.                                               |
| GDS layer ％        | The GDS layer number.                                                      |
| GDS data type      | The GDS data type.                                                         |
| Current text match | The text in GDS that is replaced when it is imported into the OA database. |
| Replacement text   | The text that replaces the GDS text during the import process.             |

## In addition:

- The fields must appear in the order shown.
- All fields can contain string literals or regular expressions. When you provide a string literal, the software searches for the text that is identical to the one you provided. When you use regular expressions, you can search for text that match specific criteria. For example, you can use the regular expression [0-9]+ to look for any integer. For information about writing regular expressions, consult a regular expression reference.
- The fields must be delimited by a space character. A space character that appears after the last delimiter is considered a part of the last regular expression or string literal.

## In the following example:

NOR 230 65535 IN\[([0-9]+)\] IN&lt;\1&gt;

- NOR is the GDS cell name. The text mapping applies only to the text in the NOR cell.
- 230 is the GDS layer number. During the import process, the software looks for GDS layer 230.
- 65535 is the GDS data type. During the import process, the software looks for GDS data type 65535, which typically maps to the drawing layer purpose.
- IN\[([0-9]+)\] is the regular expression that looks for IN[ ] and remembers any integer encountered between the square brackets.
- IN&lt;\1&gt; is the regular expression that replaces the square brackets, [ and ] , found by the previous regular expression and replaces them with angle brackets, &lt; and &gt; . In addition, the expression recalls the integer that was stored by the previous expression and places it between the angle brackets.

Figure 1 shows the result of the example text mapping.

<!-- image -->

Figure 1 Mapping a Text Label from GDSII Stream to OA

<!-- image -->

## 4

## Import

This chapter describes how to import designs and library data from different platforms through the Custom Compiler Console. The supported formats include IC Compiler, GDSII Stream, OASIS, LEF, DEF, Verilog (netlist text), and EDIF 200.

This chapter contains the following topics:

- Importing Design Data in GDSII Stream Format
- Importing Design Data in OASIS Format
- Importing Design Data in Library Exchange Format
- Importing Design Data in Design Exchange Format
- Importing Design Netlist Data as Text Views
- Importing Design Netlist Data for Schematic Generation
- Importing Design Data in EDIF 200 Format

To import technology data instead of design data, use the Technology Manager Tool.

## Importing Design Data in GDSII Stream Format

Import design data in GDSII format by defining settings and options for the translation process to use.

Perform the import task after preparing mapping files. See Supplying Mapping Files for GDSII Stream and OASIS Format Translations.

For information about Tcl commands to import design data in GDSII Stream format, see the Custom Compiler Tcl Reference Manual for details.

<!-- image -->

To import design data in GDSII Stream format:

1. From the Home or Console tab, choose File &gt; Import &gt; Stream to open the Import Stream dialog box.

Figure 2 Import Stream Dialog Box: Main Tab

<!-- image -->

On the Main tab, enter settings as described in Table 11.

| Settings   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Input      | Run Directory Directory you browse to select, or a new directory you create by entering its name. Leaving this field blank uses the current working directory.                                                                                                                                    |
|            | Stream File Stream file you browse to select. Click the folder icon to open the Select Existing File(s) dialog box. In the dialog box, the Files of type field is filtered by default for formats .gds , .db , .strm , .Z , and .gz . Select * from the drop-down menu to see all existing files. |

Table 11 Import Stream Settings (Main Tab)

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Settings     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Output       | Top Cell Cell to create and use for the import process. Library Target library for the Stream import. If the library is defined in the lib.defs file, Custom Compiler imports GDSII to this library by overwriting the existing library. If the library is not in the lib.defs file, Custom Compiler creates a new library and imports GDSII to this new library. |

## 4. Click OK .

The translator creates multiple libraries for Stream files with large numbers of cells. This avoids performance problems with large Linux directories.

For normal FileSys libraries, the translator limits each output library to contain a maximum of 20,000 cells, and then creates additional libraries for the remaining cells. Additional libraries have the same name with \_n appended. For example, if the import is to the relLib library, then cells numbered 20,001 to 40,000 are created in a new library called relLib\_1.

In all cases where additional libraries are created on import, the new libraries are defined in the lib.defs file used by the import process. Any time the Stream file contains references to a cell that is placed in a different library, the instance in OpenAccess refers to the other library so that the design hierarchy remains intact.

The importStream command imports the design in GDSII Stream format.

## Syntax

```
importStream -lib library -gds files [-ascii] [-DMAttributes attrList] [-DMSystem sysName] [-libDefFile file] [-libPath path] [-shared] [-techDMAttributes attrList] [-techDMSystem sysName] [-techLib libName] [-techLibPath path] [-techRefs libList] [-autoMapObjects propNum] [-cell name] [-cellMap file] [-compress] [-compressLevel zLevel] -convertPathToPathSeg] [-convertTextBrackets angle|square][-dataModel version] [-dbuPerUU number] [-debugMsg] [-detectVias] [-disableLibLocking] [-dumpDesignTree] [-duplicateCell skip|rename|overwrite] [-filterAcutePaths] [-filterDots][-filterReentrantPgns] [-filterSelfIntersectingPgns] [-filterZeroWidth] [-fontMap file] [-hierDepth number] [-ignoreBoxes] [-lakerLicense layout] [-layerMap fileList] [-layerMapColorMode enableColor|disableColor] [-layerMapLog] [-layerMappingMode filter|map|off] [-logFile file] [-noInfo msgIds] [-noWarning msgIds] [-notCreateViaDefs] [-notInternalizeShapes] [-numCellsInLibLimit limit] [-objectMap file] [-outputBBoxInfo] [-overwrite] [-propMap file] [-propSeparator char] [-propertyInst number] [-propertyLogic number] [-propertyNet number] [-propertyWideAlignment number] [-ramDiskChunkSize] [-ramDiskUtilityPath] [-refLibList file] [-refLibs libList] [-refOtherLibsFirst] [-refViews viewList] [-resize scaleFactor] [-restorePcells] [-restoreVias] [-setColorShiftLayersToCells fileList useTech] [-si2ViaDetection] [-snapToMfgGrid] [-templateFile file] [-textHeight height] [-textMap fileList] [-toLower] [-toLowerLabel] [-toUpper] [-toUpperLabel] [-unmappedLayersUseStrmNums] [-useTechLayerMap] [-useTechObjectMap] [-viaMap fileList] [-view view] [-h | -help] [-v] [-version]
```

For details of the importStream command, type importStream -help .

## Note:

```
When -ascii is specified, the following arguments are not used for importStream: autoMapObjects, propMap, propSeparator, propertyInst, propertyLogic, propertyNet, propertyWideAlignment, restorePcells, restoreVias, viaMap The format of -ascii when supporting Rectangle, Polygon, Path, Text objects: # #Sample: Stream ASCII dump file # #openLib("libname",DBUPerUU,"UserUnit"); # openCell("cellName1"); #  addRect(layer,dtype,x1,y1,x2,y2); # closeCell("cellName1"); # openCell("cellName2"); #  addRect(layer,dtype,x1,y1,x2,y2); #  addPoly(layer,dtype,nPoints) #   (x1,y1) (x2,y2) (x3,y3) (x4,y4) #   (x5,y5) (x6,y6) ......; #  addPath(layer,dtype,width,style,nPoints,[bgnExt,endExt]) #   (x1,y1) (x2,y2) (x3,y3) (x4,y4) #   (x5,y5) (x6,y6) ......; # addText(layer,ttype,"textString",mag,x0,y0,orient,justify,fon t); #  addCellInst("masterName",x0,y0,angle,mirror,mag); # addArrayInst("masterName",x0,y0,angle,mirror,mag,rows,columns,r owSpacing,columnSpacing); # closeCell("cellName2"); #closeLib("libName"); # ##Notes: ## ## orient = 1:R0 2:R90  3:R180 4:R270 5:MY 6:MYR90 7:MX 8:MXR90
```

## Note:

When the OASIS file contains magnification factor, Import Oasis keeps the origin of the cell master, creates a new cell with magnification, and uses new cell for master of instance. The origin cell becomes as orphan cell. The new cell name is the origin name append with magnification, such as cell1\_0.25 (magnification is 0.25).

The onPostStreamExit callback is triggered at the end of the Import OASIS run.

The importOasis command imports the design in OASIS format.

## Syntax

```
importOasis -lib arg -oasis arg [-libDefFile arg] [-libPath arg] [-techLib arg] [-techRefs arg] [-cell arg] [-compress] [-compressLevel arg (=1)] [-dbuPerUU arg (=0)] [-debugMsg] [-duplicateCellQuery] [-restorePcells] [-restoreVias] [-detectVias] [-notCreateViaDefs] [-internalizeShapes] [-hierDepth arg (=256)] [-useTechLayerMap] [-layerMap arg] [-convertTextBrackets arg] [-logFile arg] [-noInfo arg] [-noWarning arg] [-useTechObjectMap] [-objectMap arg] [-overwrite] [-duplicateCell arg (=5)] [-dumpDesignTree] [-propertyInst arg] [-propertyNet arg] [-propertyLogic arg] [-refLibList arg] [-refLibs arg] [-refViews arg] [-refOtherLibsFirst] [-textHeight arg (=0)] [-textMap arg] [-view arg (=layout)] [-resize arg (=1)] [-toUpper] [-toLower] [-snapToMfgGrid] [-unmappedLayersUseOasisNums] [-layerMapColorMode arg (=1)] [-setColorShiftLayersToCells arg] [-ramDiskChunkSize arg] [-ramDiskUtilityPath arg] [-filterZeroWidth] [-filterAcutePaths] [-filterReentrantPgns] [-filterSelfIntersectingPgns] [-filterDots] [-disableLibLocking] [-version] [-help]
```

For details of the importOasis command, type importOasis -help .

## Settings

## Description

Use Specified Mapping allows you to specify manually the terminal names to be created as virtual.

Click Edit to open the Manage Virtual Term dialog box and enter terminal name to definition name mapping (the default net name mapping entries); for example, terminal name &gt; (connection definition, default net name). These are the parameters required for creating a connection definition for a terminal.

<!-- image -->

On import, the name of any terminal found in the subcircuit declaration is matched against the terminal names in the specified mapping table. If the mapping table has an entry for the terminal being looked up, it is created as virtual using the specified definition and default net name.

The table displays connection assignments and netSet CDF parameters. Clicking OK or Apply saves the modified definition name and default net as connection assignments.

The name matching is done according to the netlist type. If the netlist is case-insensitive, name matching is done case-insensitively and the connection definition is created with the specified parameter names in lowercase. If the netlist is case-sensitive, name matching is done case-sensitively and the connection definition is created as specified by the user.

Selecting the Save as netSet to CDF checkbox and clicking OK or Apply saves the modified definition name and default net as netSet parameter.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Reference  | Use Automatic Mapping if Unspecified allows for the automatic determination/recognition of the terminals to be created as virtual, using the specified reference view list. If this option is selected (and Use Specified Mapping is unselected), the subcircuit terminal names are compared with the terminal names in the Reference Views (the first view on the list is considered first and each successive view is checked only if the preceding view does not exist). If the netlist contains a terminal that is not found in the Reference Views text field, it is created as virtual using the terminal name followed by bang (!) as the connection definition and the default net name. For example, for terminal vdd that is on the netlist but not in the Reference Views , a connection definition is created using the default mapping (vdd!, vdd!). If both Use Specified Mapping and Use Automatic Mapping if Unspecified are selected, to determine whether or not to create a terminal as virtual, its name is first looked up in the user-specified mapping table. If it is not found, automatic mapping is tried next. Library Search List shows an ordered list of libraries for reference cells. By default all the existing libraries are considered, including the output library. |

Instances from the source text view get merged to a Vector Instance only under the following conditions:

The resulting Vector Instance bits order is controlled via the selected value.

- The Instance is a Vector Bit instance.
- The placed master should match for all bits.
- The base name should match for all bits.
- Instance properties should match for all bits.

Bit Format specifies the vector or bus bit notation format used in the source text. Target object's name is updated to match the tool's vector or bus bit notation. The name of objects (such as instances, terminals, and nets) from the source text matching to the specified bit format are placed.

For Verilog sources, this filed is disabled and the current value is ignored. The [\d] notation is forced to use for the specified value. It should either be enclosed in [ ] or &lt; &gt; brackets or as a suffix prepended by a delimiter, otherwise the value considered as invalid and ignored.

Valid values are &lt;\d&gt; , [\d] or any string ending by \d .

For example, a format #\d matches all names like Inst123#4 . The default is [\d] means any name like Inst123[4] is considered as a bit and changed to the tool's default bit notation. That is Inst123&lt;4&gt; .

Power recognizes the nets as power net.

Ground recognizes the nets as ground net.

## Generating Device Mapping File

To create appropriate instances for netlist devices, an XML formatted device mapping file is required. The device mapping file is used mainly for determining the master cellview that should be used for instances, order of ports, and the correct instance property names and values, according to the master's CDF data.

The $SUB syntax is now supported in the CDL format for import netlist flow.

<!-- image -->

To create a mapping file from a selected library, which can then be edited with additional required data:

1. On the Import Text dialog box, click generate to open the Generate Device Mapping File dialog box, as illustrated in the following figure.

<!-- image -->

(Clicking Generate on the Generate Schematic from Text dialog box also opens the same Generate Device Mapping File dialog box).

2. Browse to select the Reference Libraries and the Generated File Path where the file resides. Enter the View Search List from which to generate the mapping data (the default is symbol ), and the Cell Name , where cell name matching allows wildcard characters.
3. Specify which SimInfo section to be used for device mapping file template generation (the default is hspiceD ).
4. (Optional) Select Overwrite to overwrite any existing mapping file.
5. Click Generate to generate the file. See Device Mapping File Format.

## Device Mapping File Format

The device mapping file contains the following simple xml format:

```
<file-format version="1.0" name="synopsysDeviceMappingFile" > <deviceMappings><deviceMapping> <devType>devType</devType> <cellType>cellType</cellType> <models>modelname ...</models> <regModels>regModels</regModels> <portProp>portProp</portProp> <ports><{>p1<[portProp]> ...<}> <{>p2<[portProp]> ...<}> ...</ports> <portDefaultNets>pr1(n1) pr2(n2) ...</portDefaultNets > <propMatching>p1=v1 p2=v2 ...</propMatching> <lcv>libname/cellname/viewname</lcv>
```

<!-- image -->

```
<propMapping>p1<(v1, v2, ...)>=mp1<(mv1, mv2, ...)></propMapping> <stringParameters>p1[(p1v1, p2v2, ...)] p2(p2v1, p2v2, ...) ... <stringParameters> <appProps>appProps</appProps> </deviceMapping> ... </deviceMappings> </file-format>
```

Each deviceMapping record can contain the following tags:

- devType
- cellType
- models
- regModels
- portProp
- ports
- portDefaultNets
- propMatching
- lcv
- propMapping
- stringParameters
- appProps

All tags are optional except &lt;devType&gt; and &lt;lcv&gt; . Note that only the cell part of the lcv field is required; the library and view names can be absent, which indicate that the libSearchList and viewSearchList property values are used to search for a cellview with the given cell name.

The values of the following tags are examined for determining the correct lcv to be used for a device: devType , cellType , models , ports , and propMatching . All the other fields are used to correctly map the device/instance parameter names and to create correct instance connections.

To find a matching lcv , the values of these tags are examined in the following order: devType , cellType , models , ports , propMatching . Matching to a device/instance declaration is done in the following steps, where each step does its filtering among the records which have been filtered after the previous steps:

<!-- image -->

1. Find the records having the devType of the given device.
2. Find those records which contain in their models field the name of the model specified in the device declaration. If no model has been specified in the device declaration or no matching record has been found, searching for a record with an empty model field, which is considered as a default mapping for that device type, is done.
3. For active elements for which the N or P type has been recognized from the netlist file, using the model card information or checking the model name against the N or P type patterns and a record with an empty model name has been found only, check also that the found cell's cellType matches the model type.
4. Check among the found records for those which have a ports field with port number corresponding to the number of nets in the device declaration.
5. For each record matching the preceding conditions, as the final matched record is considered the first one having propMatching conditions to which the parameters in the device declaration match.

If no matching device mapping is found for the device declaration, the device is considered as unbound. For instances for which no mapping is found the module name specified in the instance declaration is considered as a name for a master cell.

If a matching mapping record is found for an instance or a device, that instance is created with a master cellview specified in the lcv field. Instance connections are done according to the ports and portDefaultNets fields' values and the instance properties' creation is done according to the propMapping field's value. The ports with names given in the ports field are by order connected to given in the device declaration nets. The remaining ports are connected according to the connections specified in the defaultPortNets field.

For correct instance property creation, the propMapping field's value is used in the following way: parameters given in the device declaration for which the mapping data exists in the propMapping field, are mapped according to the specified mapped name and values. Note that for CDL devices, the names of the parameters which are netlisted with a proceeding $ sign, should be specified in the device mapping file with $ sign as well, for example: a capacitor's $w parameter following data can be specified in the propMapping and propMatching tags correspondingly as $W=w and $w&gt;2u .

## devType

devType for devices is the device name prefix for SPICE (R, C, L, W, U, and so on) and is the primitive name for Verilog (tranif0, tranif1, nand, and so on). For module/ subckt instantiations, devType should be X for SPICE and module for Verilog. Subckt instantiations, which are actually subckt models, can be mapped using the X&lt;devType&gt; prefix, for example XM , XC , and so on. This allows to map the subckt model instantiations, with the X&lt;device\_prefix&gt; instance name prefix, the same way as the real device instantiations.

<!-- image -->

The devType tag can contain more than one device type, to support identical mapping for same type devices and subcircuit models, for example: M XM ' and R XR .

## cellType

cellType is used for specifying the cellType of the mapped device. For active elements, it should indicate whether the device is of N or P type. Valid values for active elements are NMOS and PMOS (for MOSFET devices), NJFET and PJFET (for JFET devices), and NPN and PNP (for BJT devices). For all other SPICE devices, the cellType should be the same as the devType .

The cellType tag is used mainly for schematic generation purposes. For active elements, cellType is used to correctly map the devices recognized to be of N or P type. The N or P type is recognized from the model card if it exists. Otherwise if no model card exists, or the device instantiated a subckt model, the N or P type is recognized by matching the model name with a pattern. The pattern checks for the first symbol of the model/subkct name to see if it is N or P , if it is not then checks which of the N and P symbols appears more times in the name.

## models

models contains the model names that can be specified in the device declarations. Note that this field can be empty indicating that the current lcv is the default one for the specified device type, and in case if no model name is specified in the device declaration or no lcv mapping is found for the specified model, the given default lcv is used.

For MOSFET, JFET, and BJT devices which can be of N or P type, different default mappings can be specified for N and P type elements. For this purpose, one of the following can be specified as the model name: nmos, pmos, njfet, pjfet, npn, pnp.

For module/subckt instantiations, models should contain the module/subckt name.

## Examples

&lt;deviceMapping&gt; &lt;devType&gt;M &lt;/devType&gt; &lt;models&gt;MM1 MM2&lt;/models&gt; &lt;lcv&gt;myLib/nmos/symbol&lt;/lcv&gt; &lt;deviceMapping&gt;

&lt;deviceMapping&gt; &lt;devType&gt;M&lt;/devType&gt; &lt;models&gt;pmos&lt;/models&gt; &lt;lcv&gt;myLib/pmos1/symbol&lt;/lcv&gt; &lt;deviceMapping&gt;

&lt;deviceMapping&gt;

```
<devType>M</devType> <models> </models> <lcv>myLib/nmos2/symbol</lcv> <deviceMapping> <deviceMapping> <devType>X</devType> <models>cell1</models> <lcv>myLib/mycell/symbol</lcv> <deviceMapping>
```

According to the previously mentioned device mapping records, the following device declarations are mapped to the following cells:

```
.model MM1 nmos .model MM3 pmos .model MM4 nmos M1 n1 n2 n3 MM1 1 2 // maps to myLib/nmos/symbol M3 n1 n2 n3 MM3 1 2 // myLib/pmos1/symbol M4 n1 n2 n3 MM4 1 2 // myLib/nmos2/symbol as there is no mapping declared for MM4 M5 n1 n2 n3 MM5 1 2 // myLib/nmos2/symbol as there is no mapping declared for MM5 X1 n1 n2 n3 cell1  // myLib/mycell/symbol X2 n1 n2 n3 cell2  // is not mapped, libSearchList and viewSearchList properties are used to find a cell with name cell2
```

## regModels

&lt;regModels&gt; is used for adding regular expressions to match model names. The regular expression matching has lower priority than the exact model name matching which is done by the &lt;models&gt; tag. If a model name parsed matched both &lt;models&gt; and &lt;regModels&gt; tags, the &lt;models&gt; tag is honored if the ports and parameters matched.

You can define multiple patterns in a &lt;regModels&gt; &lt;/regModels&gt; tag pair by separating each pattern using a space character. The regular expression pattern model matching is supported in both the legacy parser flow (TN library) and the new common parser flow (GNDB) for SPICE/CDL format. If a device mapping section in the device mapping file both have &lt;models&gt; and &lt;regModels&gt; tags, only the &lt;regModels&gt; tag is honored.

## portProp

portProp is the name of the property, which is used for the PCells with generated number of ports. For example, for W, U, and S devices, the number of ports is not fixed and if a PCell is used as the master, the ports are generated according to property value like portnumber . And because the device declaration contains no such parameter, its value should be calculated from the number of net names given in the device declaration and certain port list pattern given in ports .

<!-- image -->

## ports

ports contains the list of ports to which the nets given in the device declaration should be connected by order.

## Note that:

- The connected ports that should be connected to a net are given as a list. The port names in the i-th list are connected to the net which corresponds to the net on i-th position in the device declaration, for example, for PCells with a variable number of ports, if you want MOSFETs with 3 nodes to connect to a master with 4 terminals, specify the following port list meaning that the last net is connected both to ports S and B: G D {S B} .
- If the net given in some positions in the device declaration should not be connected to any net, an empty list can be specified instead of the port name, for example: for a MOSFET device, the list of ports can contain the following: {} G D S , meaning that the first name given in the device declaration should not be connected to any port, and the remaining 3 nets should be connected to G, D, and S ports correspondingly.
- Given port names can be either the names of existing ports in the cellview or the names of virtual terminals to which the nets from the device declaration should be connected. So any port name given in the list is considered as a terminal name, if such exists in the design, otherwise it is considered as a virtual terminal name to which the given net should be assigned. Use the teParseExtraTermsAsVirtual Tcl preference to decide whether extra port names should be considered as virtual terminals.
- For PCells, the ports of which are generated depending on property values (given in the portProp field), port names can be specified as a port name prefix followed by a bracket with the portProp name inside, for example, {in[n]} {refin} {out[n]} {refout} for w element. This indicates that the port names should be generated with the given prefix appended with indexes from 1 to n . Note that the value of n is actually calculated from the number of nets given in the device declarations. For example, for the preceding W element port pattern, the number of nets should be 2n+2 and if the device declaration contains 6 nets, n is calculated as 2, so the generated port names should be in1 in2 refin out1 out2 refout .
- If the ports field is empty, the portOrder/termOrder of the device is used for instterm connection. (If those properties are also empty, the instance remains unconnected).

## portDefaultNets

portDefaultNets defines the default connections for ports with the following format: pr1(n1) pr2(n2) , where pr i is the port name, and n i is the net that should connect to it if no other connection is specified for the port in the ports field.

For CDL netlists, this portDefaultNets tag can contain also port connections in the following format: pi($param) , which indicates that p i port should be connected to the net the name of which is given as a value of $param parameter. Note that port-to-parameter connections are considered as overriding for those made according to the ports field. This means that if the ports field contains p1 p2 p3 p4 for a BJT element, and the portDefaultNets field contains value p4($SUB) , port p4 is connected to the net the names of which is specified as a value of $SUB parameter in the BJT device declaration.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## propMatching

To have the specified in the device mapping record lcv to be used as the master for the given device, propMatching defines the conditions to which the parameter values in the instance declaration should match.

propMatching can contain a set of conditions on more than one parameter represented as expressions with equal ( == ), not equal ( != ), less ( &lt; ), greater ( &gt; ), less or equal ( &lt;= ), and greater or equal ( &gt;= ) operators. propMatching can also indicate matching by parameter existence or absence.

Note that more than one propMatching tag can be given in a device mapping record. To have matching with the case when a particular parameter is given in the device declaration, the parameter name should be specified in propMatching , and to indicate the opposite (the parameter is not given in the device declaration), a ! sign should be set before the parameter name. For example: w&lt;2u , l&gt;4u , or !CONVOLUTION ! FBASE !FMAX !RS which indicates that the specified master should be chosen only for linear transistors, which exclude the usage of this cellview as the master for frequency dependent and skin effect resistors.

## lcv

lcv contains the library, cell, and view names (separated by slashes) of the master cellview that should be used as a master for the device declaration which matches the data of all the previous fields. Note that if the library or view name is empty, libSearchList and viewSearchList values are used instead to search a given cell name in the listed libraries.

## propMapping

propMapping contains the mapping of hspice parameter names and their values to corresponding parameter names and values for the given cell's CDF data. For example:

- tranfun(SIN,PU)=srcType(SINE,PULSE) means that SPICE parameter tranfun is mapped to CDF parameter srcType and its values SIN and PU are mapped correspondingly to values SINE and PULSE .
- R=res means that the R value of the SPICE device is saved in RES parameter of the OA instance.

## stringParameters

stringParameters contains the mapped names of string and enumeration type parameters for a given device.

The stringParameters tag is used for correct replacing of identifier names representing parameter names with lineage("param\_name") expression in the instance parameter values. This is needed for correct schematic generation to make parameter evaluation look for the parameter value in upper levels of the hierarchy.

For string parameters, only the names should be listed, while for enumerated parameters, the tag can contain the parameter name followed by the supported enumeration values in brackets separated by commas, so that other string values passed to this parameter are considered as parameter names.

Also, non-string parameters that can have some string keyword values should be listed in this stringParameters tag. For example, keyword infinity for capacitor device's parameter C : C(infinity) .

## appProps

appProps contains the name of parameters which should be created in OA as instance properties if specified in the device declaration, even if they are not valid parameters according to the SPICE documentation, does not exist in the CDF and are not specified in the propMapping field.

## Device Mapping File Examples

The following lines show examples of deviceMapping records.

```
<deviceMappings> <!-mapping Sinusoidal voltage sources to the vsin cellview of analoglib . --> <deviceMapping> <devType> V </devType> <model> </model> <portProp></portProp> <ports> PLUS MINUS </ports> <propMatching> tranfun=sin </propMatching> <lcv> analogLib vsin symbol </lcv> <propMapping> tranfun(SIN)=srcType(Sine) dc=vdc acmag=acm acphase=acPhase vo=vo va=va td=td freq=freq q=q j=j </propMapping> <appProps>z</appProps> </deviceMapping> <!-mapping FET transistors (with 3 ports) with models named M1 and M2 to analoglib nmos (which is 3-port device with virtual terminal p_bulk),
```

```
and the model names M1 and M2 are mapped as nmos1 and nmos2. The bulk is connected to the same net as the source. --> <deviceMapping> <devType> M </devType> <model> M1 M2</model> <portProp></portProp> <ports> {G} {D} {S p_bulk} </ports> <propMatching> </propMatching> <lcv> analogLib nmos hspice </lcv> <propMapping>vds=Vds vgs=Vgs vbs=Vbs mname(M1,M2)=model(nmos1, nmos2) </propMapping> <appProps>a b</appProps> </deviceMapping> <!-mapping FET transistors (with 4 ports) with models named M3 and M4 to analoglib nmos (which is 3-port device and has a virtual terminal p_bulk), and the model names M3 and M4 are mapped as nmos3 and nmos4. The bulk is connected to the same net as the source. --> <deviceMapping> <devType> M </devType> <model> M3 M4</model> <portProp></portProp> <ports> {G} {D} {S} {p_bulk} </ports> <propMatching> </propMatching> <lcv> analogLib nmos hspice </lcv> <propMapping>vds=Vds vgs=Vgs vbs=Vbs l=l w=w mname(M3,M4)=model(nmos3, nmos4) </propMapping> <appProps>a b</appProps> </deviceMapping> <!-mapping High voltage FET transistors with models named HVP1 and HVP2 to analoglib nmos4v, and the model names HVP1 and HVP2 are mapped as nmos1 and nmos2. --> <deviceMapping> <devType> M </devType> <model> HVP1 HVP2</model> <portProp></portProp> <ports> {G} {D} {S} {B} </ports> <propMatching> </propMatching> <lcv> analogLib pmos4hv symbol </lcv> <propMapping>vds=Vds vgs=Vgs vbs=Vbs mname(HVP1, HVP2)=model(pmos1hv, pmos2hv) </propMapping> <appProps>a b</appProps> </deviceMapping> <!-mapping skin effect resistor to the myLib skin_effect_res symbol of myLib library,--> <deviceMapping> <devType> R </devType> <model> </model>

This is an example with the portProp usage, when the number of ports is variable. --> <deviceMapping> <devType> W </devType> <model> </model> <portProp>n</portProp>

## Importing Design Netlist Data for Schematic Generation

You can import design netlist data to generate schematics without creating text views. Available text netlist formats include SPICE, CDL, and Verilog. You can optionally generate symbol views while importing netlist text.

Compressed files that are supported by the Linux zcat command are supported by this flow. Compressed file support can also be enhanced using the db::showGenerateSchematicsFromText::decompressFiles procedure.

To import design data for schematic generation:

1. From the Home or Console tab, choose File &gt; Import &gt; Schematic from Netlist to open the Generate Schematics from Text dialog box.
2. On the Main tab, enter settings as described in Table 33.

|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Input          | Language is the behavioral modeling language you specify from the list: SPICE , CDL , Verilog , Verilog-A , Verilog-AMS , SystemVerilog , or VHDL . Netlist Files specifies the source netlist for this import process. Browse to select the file. Multiple files can also be selected. Top Cell Name works for CDL and SPICE formats only. Enter the name of a cell where top-level SPICE/CDL design data should be put. A name based off the imported file name is generated by default. Import Modules lets you list module names or specify the name pattern for the modules you wish to import. Match Type can be Exact , Reg Expr , or Wildcard . Exclude Modules lets you list module names or specify the name pattern for the modules you wish to exclude from the import when |
| Device Mapping | Device Map File works for SPICE, CDL, and Verilog formats only. You can click any of the following buttons: ◦ Device Mapping File for resolving instance masters to designate the required device mapping source (to resolve instance masters to reference libraries) from a file. ◦ Generate to create the device map file from a reference library. See Generating Device Mapping File. Click Edit Mapping File to open the selected mapping file in a text editor for adding or modifying the mapping information. Click Default to load the sample provided with the installation hierarchy. This file can also be copied and edited to address any missing information. The default mapping file maps all devices to analogLib library cells.                                      |
| Output         | Library specifies the destination library for this import operation, which you choose from the list. Click Create Library to open the New Library dialog box and create a new output library. View Name shows the view name of the schematic view that is generated. Overwrite specifies how the import process treats imported cellViews that conflict with existing cellViews. Never (the default) means that the existing cellView remains intact (no copy is created). Always means that existing cellViews are overwritten.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

Store Views by File Extension stores imported netlist with default view name specified with preference dbImportText&lt;Language&gt;ViewName . When this option is enabled, the View Name option is disabled. The tool recognizes file format by file extension defined with the preference dbImportText&lt;Langugage&gt;FileExtensions . ## Settings

## Description

Make Form-gate Hierarchy attempts to recognize common gate structures (such as inverters, and, nand gates). If found, it creates hierarchical cells of these gates.

Add Net Label to All Wire Segments adds net labels to each segment of a wire rather than just one segment.

Schematic Editor selects each island wire to create the net name label, so the generated results not only shows one net name on wire but each island has their net name label on the canvas.

Enabled by default.

Create Vector Ports controls whether to merge the bus bit terminals to a bus by selecting one of the following options: Off , by Ascending , or by Descending .

For example, A&lt;0&gt; and A&lt;1&gt; to A&lt;0:1&gt; . You can choose to sort bus bits in ascending or descending order.

Create Vector Instances controls whether to merge Vector Bit instances to a Vector instance by selecting one of the following options: Off , by Ascending , or by Descending .

Instances from the source text view get merged to a Vector Instance only under the following conditions:

The resulting Vector Instance bits order is controlled via the selected value.

- The Instance is a Vector Bit instance.
- The placed master should match for all bits.
- The base name should match for all bits.
- Instance properties should match for all bits.

Bit Format specifies the vector or bus bit notation format used in the source text. Target object's name is updated to match the tool's vector or bus bit notation. The name of objects (such as instances, terminals, and nets) from the source text matching to the specified bit format are placed.

For Verilog sources, this filed is disabled and the current value is ignored. The [\d] notation is forced to use for the specified value. It should either be enclosed in [ ] or &lt; &gt; brackets or as a suffix prepended by a delimiter, otherwise the value considered as invalid and ignored.

Valid values are &lt;\d&gt; , [\d] or any string ending by \d .

For example, a format #\d matches all names like Inst123#4 . The default is [\d] means any name like Inst123[4] is considered as a bit and changed to the tool's default bit notation. That is Inst123&lt;4&gt; .

## Settings

## Description

Use Specified Mapping allows you to specify manually the terminal names to be created as virtual.

Click Edit to open the Term Mapping dialog box and enter terminal name to definition name mapping (the default net name mapping entries); for example, terminal name &gt; (connection definition, default net name). These are the parameters required for creating a connection definition for a terminal.

<!-- image -->

On import, the name of any terminal found in the subcircuit declaration is matched against the terminal names in the specified mapping table. If the mapping table has an entry for the terminal being looked up, it is created as virtual using the specified definition and default net name.

The name matching is done according to the netlist type. If the netlist is case-insensitive, name matching is done case-insensitively and the connection definition is created with the specified parameter names in lower case. If the netlist is case-sensitive, name matching is done case-sensitively and the connection definition is created as specified by the user.

Use Automatic Mapping if Unspecified allows for the automatic determination/recognition of the terminals to be created as virtual, using the specified reference view list. If this option is selected (and Use Specified Mapping is unselected), the subcircuit terminal names are compared with the terminal names in the Reference Views (the first view on the list is considered first and each successive view is checked only if the preceding view does not exist). If the netlist contains a terminal that is not found in the Reference Views text field, it is created as virtual using the terminal name followed by bang (!) as the connection definition and the default net name. For example, for terminal vdd that is on the netlist but not in the Reference Views , a connection definition is created using the default mapping (vdd!, vdd!).

If both Use Specified Mapping and Use Automatic Mapping if Unspecified are selected, to determine whether or not to create a terminal as virtual, its name is first looked up in the user-specified mapping table. If it is not found, automatic mapping is tried next.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Settings      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|---------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Include Files | Specifies whether all include files should be parsed or ignored. The options are: ◦ Parse : Parses the include files and creates the cells for modules found in the include files. Include statements are not added to any module. For Verilog, effective directives are calculated and included for each module. ◦ Ignore : The include files are parsed, but the modules declared inside the include files are not created. Include statements are not added to the modules. For Verilog, effective directives are calculated and included for each module. For SPICE and CDL, you can use the Except rows to create multiple Parse / Ignore exceptions to the All files directive. Click to add an Except row under the current row, or to delete the current row. Match type for the exception can be Exact , Reg Expr , or Wildcard (the default). Exceptions are prioritized such that the lowermost condition is checked first; if there is no match, then the next condition up the list is checked, and so on. In other words, lower conditions have higher priority. Default exceptions are: ◦ Include files with extensions .dspf , .gz , .gzip , .enc and .spf . ◦ Ignore files with extensions .data , .ic , .lib , and .vec . |

## 5. Click OK .

The system imports the text and generates the schematic.

## Importing Design Data in EDIF 200 Format

EDIF is a common schematic format that is generated by many electronic CAD tools. Import design data as EDIF200 when you want to translate data files from an Electronic Design Interchange Format (EDIF) schematic to the Custom Compiler database.

## Using the Import EDIF200 Dialog Box

To import design data as EDIF200:

1. From the Home or Console tab, choose File &gt; Import &gt; EDIF200 to open the Import EDIF200 dialog box.
2. Enter settings as described in Table 36.

If the Output Library Name is specified, all cellviews are created in the specified library regardless of their libNames defined in the EDIF file. In the case of conflicting cell names (for example, if the library being used already has such a cell), the tool renames the cell name using the format <LibNameFromEDIF>_cellName. |

If Top Cell Name is not specified, both hierarchies (6 cells) are imported. If, however, Top Cell Name is specified as A1, only the A1 > B1 > C1 hierarchy is imported. If Top Cell Name is specified as a mid-level cell name, such as B, Custom Compiler imports only the hierarchy starting from that mid-level cell, such as B > C.                                                                                                                                             |
