## Export

This chapter describes how to export design and library data using the Custom Compiler Console. The data can be exported to IC Compiler, GDSII Stream, OASIS, LEF, DEF, Liberty File, and netlist formats. To protect the proprietary information stored in your Tcl scripts, you can export it in bytecode format.

- Exporting Design Data in GDSII Stream Format
- Exporting Design Data in OASIS Format
- Exporting Design Data in Library Exchange Format (LEF)
- Exporting Design Data in Design Exchange Format (DEF)
- Exporting Design Data in Liberty Library File Format
- Exporting Design Data in Netlist Format

## Note:

Exporting Designs and Libraries to the IC Compiler Tool is covered in the Custom Compiler and IC Compiler Co-Design Assistant User Guide .

To export technology data instead of design data, use the Technology Manager Tool.

## Exporting Design Data in GDSII Stream Format

To export design data in GDSII Stream format:

1. Perform any one of the following to open the Export Stream dialog box:
- From the Home tab, choose File &gt; Export &gt; Stream .
- From the toolbar in the Layout Editor, choose Design &gt; Export Stream

## Settings

## Description

Convert Pins to Texts specifies whether to convert pin's term name to text. Each shape connected to the pin is used for the location and layer/purpose pair (LPP) of the created text. Off by default.

Convert All Paths to Polygons imports two-point orthogonal and diagonal path records as pathSeg objects. Off by default.

Keep Half Width Paths specifies whether the translator should keep half-width paths and not convert them to polygons. Off by default.

Export Text Displays controls translation of textDisplay objects.

Map All Texts specifies whether the translator should attempt to name map oaTexts and oaTextDisplays that are not oaNames. Off by default.

Export Blockages controls export of blockage objects. Default is to export blockage objects (on).

Export Reference Library Cells controls translation and output of cells referenced from a library other than the one specified by the Library argument. Default is that these cells are translated.

Snap Vertices to Mfg Grid specifies whether the translator should snap the object vertices to manufacturing grid during export. Off by default.

Keep Vias specifies whether the translator should write via information into the .pcell file. On by default.

Flatten Standard Vias specifies if the exportStream translator should convert standard vias into their geometry. Off by default.

Keep Full Cell Name specifies whether to keep the full name of the cells. When turned off, cell names are shortened during export. Off by default.

Keep View Name specifies if the exportStream translator should keep the view name. If the view name is not a layout, the translator generates the view map with the -gdsFileName option to restore the view name. Off by default.

## Settings

## Description

Color Locks specifies which mapping lines in the layer mapping file are used to map shapes with a mask color attribute.

## Options for Color Locks are:

A color specification is present in the layer mapping file if the data type number is followed by the keyword color with a colon (:) and a color name. Optionally, this entry can be followed by one of the keywords locked or unlocked . locked refers to the anchor bit in the color value for the shape.

- Ignore : All colored shapes are mapped with the line that has neither keyword.
- Full : Mapping is compatible with Cadence® Virtuoso®, with the following behavior: The keyword colorAnnotate after the color specification in the layer map is used to ignore a whole line of layer mapping during GDSII Stream export and the same mapping line is handled during import.
- Strict : Anchor bit is used to select either locked or unlocked from the layer map.
- Honor : (default) Mapping is compatible with Cadence® Virtuoso®, with the following behavior: When the layer map does not have a color mapping rule in to match color shapes, the Custom Compiler tool tries to match the mapping rule without a color specified.

Example:

- DisableColor : Layer mapping lines with a color attribute in the layer mapping file are ignored. Any shape with color does not map those mapping lines with color attributes. Only mapping lines without a color attribute is used for layer mapping.

M1 drawing 3 0

M1 drawing 3 12 color:red unlocked

M1 drawing 3 11 color:red locked

When the DisableColor option is set, colored/colorless shapes on M1 are mapped to 3 0.

Lock Only is available only when you set the

- Lock Only : The shapes of the colored layer that are not colored or are not locked, are filtered out during export.

dbExportStreamShowLockOnly preference to true . The default setting is false .

PCell options control conversion of PCells into their geometry. The default is Keep .

The Flatten option flattens PCells, editable PCells, and MCells, obeying the hierarchy limit.

The None option means no conversion.

The Keep option preserves the information of PCells, editable PCells, MCells, and MPP in the GDS stream file, so that they can be restored during import using Import &gt; Stream &gt; Options &gt; Restore PCells . Abutment information is stored in a side file and can also be restored during import.

<!-- image -->

## Settings

## Description

Stream Version specifies the GDSII Stream format version for the translator to use. Rectangles are written as boundary regardless of which version is specified.

Name Space is the namespace mapping for text displays: cdba , native , lef , def , verilog , vhdl , spef , spice , or spf. Default is cdba .

Convert Names controls conversion of cell and instance names to either uppercase, lowercase, or no conversion. Default is no conversion.

Cell Name Prefix specifies the string prefixed to every structure name written in the Stream file. The GUI validates that the string entered is a legal CDBA scalar name, and that it also contains no spaces. If left empty, no option is used. Note that this option does not exist in oa2strm .

Cell Name Suffix specifies the string suffixed to every structure name written in the Stream file. The GUI validates that the string entered is a legal CDBA scalar name, and that it also contains no spaces. If left empty, no option is used. Note that this option does not exist in oa2strm .

Ignore Top Cells Prefix and Suffix Specifies whether top cells listed in Main &gt; Input &gt; Top Cell should be added with a prefix or suffix. Default is No.

Ignore Cells Prefix and Suffix Ignores the prefixes and suffixes of the cells listed in this field. Use blank space to separate cells.

Hierarchy Depth is the number of hierarchy levels to translate. Default is 256.

Text Depth specifies the depth to which the translator should export texts. Default is 256.

Label Depth specifies the depth to which the translator provides labels. Default is 1.

Convert Labels controls conversion of net and terminal names to either uppercase, lowercase, or no conversion. Default is no conversion.

Sides per Ellipse specifies the number of edges used for ellipse to polygon conversion. Default is 64.

Sides per Donut specifies the number of edges used for donut to polygon conversion. Default is 64.

<!-- image -->

| Settings   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Output     | Reference specifies the output reference mapping file. Specify a path to the file in the text box. This file is important when you export a GDSII file from Custom Compiler, run IC Validator DRC or LVS, and then cross-probe or highlight these violations to the Custom Compiler Layout Editor. In this flow, ICV reports violations with respect to the GDSII library/cell object context, but Custom Compiler must identify and probe the corresponding objects and coordinates in the OpenAccess lib/cell/view context. This reference mapping file stores the mapping relationship between the OpenAccess objects, (such as vias, PCells, lib/cell/view hierarchy, and so on) and their equivalent GDSII objects. Having this file ensures that you can cross-probe violations from a GDSII-based ICV run into Custom Compiler LE; this is the supported and recommended flow. Without this file, cross-probing might still be possible but is not guaranteed to work reliably. The browse icon is disabled if the current file path does not exist. |

## Settings

General

## Description

Apply Repetition exports repeated instances, shapes, and text in --repetition mode so that they occupy less disk space. Off by default.

Expand Arrays to Instances specifies whether to convert arrays to instances. Off by default.

Convert All Paths to Polygons exports paths as a polygon describing the complete shape boundary rather than as a path object. Off by default.

Convert Ellipses to Circles exports the conversion from circles to polygons. If this option is disabled, circles remain circles during export. Off by default.

Export Text Displays controls translation of textDisplay objects. On by default.

Export Blockages controls export of blockage objects. Default is to export blockage objects (on).

Export Reference Library Cells controls translation and output of cells referenced from a library other than the one specified by the Library argument. Default is that these cells are translated.

Snap Vertices to Mfg Grid specifies whether the translator should snap the object vertices to manufacturing grid during export. Off by default.

Keep Vias specifies whether the translator should write via information into the .pcell file. On by default.

Flatten Standard Vias specifies whether the translator should convert standard vias into their geometry. Off by default.

Keep Full Cell Name specifies whether to keep the full name of the cells. When turned off, cell names are shortened during export. Off by default.

|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|            | Duplicate Cell specifies what the translator should do during export: ◦ Append with Number : (default) Append the duplicate cell name with a sequence number. ◦ Append with Library Name : Append the duplicate cell name with a source library name. ◦ Skip Duplicate : Skips the duplicate cell name when the same cell name is found during export stream. After duplicating the cell name, the tool appends the suffix with the view name if the view name is not a layout. However, if the cell name still duplicates even after appending the suffix with the view name, the Duplicate Cell option specifies that the translator should append the duplicate cell name with a sequence number during export. |

## Settings

## Description

Color Locks specifies which mapping lines in the layer mapping file are used to map shapes with a mask color attribute.

## Options for Color Locks are:

A color specification is present in the layer mapping file if the data type number is followed by the keyword color with a colon (:) and a color name. Optionally, this entry can be followed by one of the keywords locked or unlocked . locked refers to the anchor bit in the color value for the shape.

- Ignore : All colored shapes are mapped with the line that has neither keyword.
- Full : Mapping is compatible with Cadence® Virtuoso®, with the following behavior: The keyword colorAnnotate after the color specification in the layer map is used to ignore a whole line of layer mapping during GDSII Stream export and the same mapping line is handled during import.
- Strict : Anchor bit is used to select either locked or unlocked from the layer map.
- Honor : (default) Mapping is compatible with Cadence® Virtuoso®, with the following behavior: When the layer map does not have a color mapping rule in to match color shapes, the Custom Compiler tool tries to match the mapping rule without a color specified.

## Example:

- DisableColor : Layer mapping lines with a color attribute in the layer mapping file are ignored. Any shape with color does not map those mapping lines with color attributes. Only mapping lines without a color attribute is used for layer mapping.

M1 drawing 3 0

M1 drawing 3 12 color:red unlocked

M1 drawing 3 11 color:red locked

When the DisableColor option is set, colored/colorless shapes on M1 are mapped to 3 0.

Lock Only is available only when you set the

- Lock Only : The shapes of the colored layer that are not colored or are not locked, are filtered out during export.

dbExportOasisShowLockOnly preference to true . The default setting is false .

The PCell options control the conversion of PCells into their geometry:

- Flatten flattens PCells.
- None means no conversion.
- Keep specifies whether the translator should output PCell information for a later import operation. On by default. Starting with the P-2019.06 release, Keep also specifies whether the translator should output abutment information provided the Tcl preference, dbExportOasisKeepAbutments , is set to true .

<!-- image -->

## Settings

## Description

Validation Scheme specifies the validation scheme to use. Valid values are None for no validation, CRC32 (default), or CHECKSUM32 .

Compression Level is the level of compression used when writing the file. 0 is the lowest and 9 is the highest level of compression. Default is 0.

Convert Names Specifies translator conversion of cell and instance name text to one of the following:

- Lower : Lowercase
- None : (default) Do not convert names
- Upper : Uppercase

Cell Name Prefix specifies a string that is prefixed to every structure name written in the stream file. The GUI validates that the string entered is a legal CDBA scalar name, and that it also contains no spaces. If left empty, no option is used. Note that this option does not exist in oa2strm .

Cell Name Suffix specifies a string that is suffixed to every cell name. The GUI validates that the string entered is a legal CDBA scalar name, and that it also contains no spaces. If left empty, no option is used.

Ignore Top Cells Prefix and Suffix Specifies whether top cells listed in Main &gt; Input &gt; Top Cell should be added with a prefix or suffix. Default is No.

Ignore Cells Prefix and Suffix Ignores the prefixes and suffixes of the cells listed in this field. Use blank space to separate cells.

Hierarchy Depth is the number of hierarchy levels to translate. Default is 20.

Sides per Ellipse specifies the number of edges used for ellipse to polygon conversion. Default is 64.

Note: If ellipses are not converted to polygons and the ellipses are circles and the diameters are even, they are exported as circles instead of polygons in the OASIS file. Cell/Layer Statistics show circles only if there are some circles in the OASIS file.

Sides per Donut specifies the number of edges used for donut to polygon conversion. Default is 64.

DBU per UU is an optional integer multiple or an integer divisor of the design's database units per user units that you specify for scaling while translating an OA database to OASIS without changing the source OA database. Default is empty. Preference: dbExportOasisDbuPerUU

## Exporting Design Data in Library Exchange Format (LEF)

Library Exchange Format (LEF) is an ASCII data format that describes standard cell libraries. LEF files typically include a technology section (rules, definitions, and capacitance), a site extension section, and a macros section (cell information, pins, blockages, and so on). LEF is used with the design exchange format (DEF), which describes netlists and circuits, to fully represent the physical layout of designs.

To export design data in Library Exchange Format (LEF):

1. From the Home or Console tab, choose File &gt; Export &gt; LEF to open the Export LEF dialog box.
2. On the Main tab, enter settings as described in Table 52.
3. Click the Options tab in the Export LEF dialog box (Figure 35).

Figure 34 Export LEF Dialog Box: Main Tab

<!-- image -->

Table 52 Export LEF Settings (Main Tab)

| Settings   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Input      | Library specifies the design designated for export. Cells specifies the cell(s) to export. Views specifies the view(s) to export. The default is an abstract view.                                    |
| Output     | Run Directory is the directory you browse to select, or a new directory you create by entering its name. The default is the current directory. LEF File is the LEF file you browse to select and use. |

<!-- image -->

Figure 35 Export LEF Dialog Box: Options Tab

<!-- image -->

Tcl preference: dbExportLefWriteTechnology Write pins alphabetically writes the pins from the abstract in alphabetical order. Version specifies the LEF file format version. You should select the latest version that is understood by the LEF readers in your flow. Default is 5.8. If you choose LEF version 5.8, mask number and DBU/UU information is included in the LEF file. Tcl preference: dbExportLefVersion DBU per UU overrides distance per database unit. Tcl preference: dbExportLefDBUPerUU Scale Factor scales cell coordinates. Tcl preference: |

Tcl preference: dbExportDefScaleFactor                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

## Exporting Design Data in Netlist Format

You can export design data in netlist format. You can do this without opening the design.

You can optionally perform flat netlisting with this procedure. The system flattens the design to a temporary cellView, optionally renames all instances and nets (except global and ported nets), and then netlists the flattened design.

To export design data in netlist format:

1. From the Home or Console tab, choose File &gt; Export &gt; Netlist to open the Export Netlist dialog box.
2. Enter settings on the Main tab.

<!-- image -->

(Optional) Use the dbExportNetlist preference to set the values in this dialog box. For information about using preferences, see Specifying Design Preferences.

The following table describes settings on this Main tab.

<!-- image -->

| Option           | Description                                                                                              |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Netlister Format | Choose a format from the list: CDL , HSPICE , Spectre , VHDL , Verilog , or VerilogICC . Tcl preference: |

Tcl preference: dbExportNetlistFormat

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Option            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|-------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Design to Netlist | Specify the Library and Cell , and specify or browse to choose a View for the design. You can accept the current Netlist File for overwriting, browse to a different file, or enter the name of a new file. You can browse to select a Netlist Directory . Open on Completion (on by default) opens a text viewer window showing the contents of the exported netlist. Tcl preferences: dbExportNetlistDir , dbExportNetlistFile , dbExportNetlistLCV |
| Hierarchy Options | View Search List searches these views. Accept, or enter new values. Tcl preference: dbExportNetlistViewSearchList View Stop List stops the search at these views. Accept, or enter new values. Tcl preference: dbExportNetlistViewStopList Flatten Design flattens a hierarchical design before netlisting it. Enabling this feature adds a Flattening Options tab to accept additional settings. Tcl preference: dbExportNetlistFlattenDesign        |

## Note:

- If a line in the Verilog netlist file exceeds 80 characters, ',' appears at the end of the line.
- For selecting multiple cellviews to export design in netlist format, see Selecting Multiple Cellviews

Port connection type and its default might vary according to the currently selected Netlist Format . This option is hidden by default for CDL but it is shown by default for Verilog and VerilogICC. This option controls the way the instance terminals connection to the nets are netlisted in the instance declartion. For CDL, ◦ When byOrder is set, the result looks like this: XVG2 s3 s2 gainV only the net names are declared ◦ When byName (works only for subcircuits) is set, the result looks like this: XVG2 gainV $ PINS Q=s3 D=s2 both terminal names and net names with '=' are declared, after keyword '$PINS' ◦ When byOrder is set, the result looks like this: res R5( net023 , net040 ); only the net names are declared ◦ When byName is set, the result looks like this: res R5( .MINUS ( net023 ), .PLUS ( net040 ) ); both terminal names with dot at start and net names in brackets are declared Tcl preferences: nlCDLPortConnectionType , nlVerilogICCPortConnectionType , nlVerilogPortConnectionType |

Ignore Properties is a list of property names for shorting. Ignore property names are netlister-specific and controlled by the preference nl<Simulator>ShortPropNames . Ignore properties are used to determine whether an instance or a master should be shorted. If a device is shorted, the netlister looks in nlShortExprPropNames to determine how to short a device. For example, a typical two-terminal shorting description is (short(PLUS MINUS)) , which tells the netlister to short the PLUS and MINUS terminals. |

When nlCDLIncludeCDLFile is set to false ( Copy CDL File Content is turned off), the netlister includes the cdl text view with an .include statement.

```
.subckt block1 XI142 net990 net991 net988 net989 block0 .ends block1 .include '/remote/project1/topLib/block0/cdl/netlist.cdl'
```

When nlCDLIncludeCDLFile is set to true ( Copy CDL File Content is turned on), the netlister copies the contents of the cdl text view directly into the final netlist.

.subckt block1 XI142 net990 net991 net988 net989 block0 .ends block1 # Copy the CDL file content into the final netlist .subckt block0 a b x y *.PININFO a:I b:I x:O y:O RR470 b y 1K $[RP] RR469 a x 1K $[RP] .ends block0

## Selecting Multiple Cellviews

To select multiple cellviews, set the dbExportNetlistMultipleLCV preference to true (default: false ). A new dialog box opens with the Multiple Cell Views panel in the Design to Netlist section instead of a single cellview selector, as shown in the following figure.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Select multiple Libraries , Cells , Views and click the Add Cell Views button to add all the selected cellviews to the Chosen Cell Views list, as shown in the following figure.

<!-- image -->

To remove some cellviews from the Chosen Cell Views list, select the cellviews in this list and click Remove Cell Views button.

The netlisting sessions for all chosen cellview are run in sequence and the corresponding message is shown in the Console.

<!-- image -->

The output folder is the same for all session, which is set in the Netlist Directory textbox in the Main tab, and the file name for each session is derived automatically according to the dbExportNetlistFileNameFormat preference.

Some design-related features are disabled in the multiple cellviews mode.

For example, Power panel for VerilogICC and temporary cellview selection for flatten netlist.

## General Designing

This chapter describes how to create, open, navigate, edit, save, and run processes on designs. You can also view design and component summaries, and save your work. At any time, you can print and plot designs, and export design images. Close designs to complete each session.

This chapter contains the following topics:

- Creating Designs
- Opening Designs
- Navigating the Design Hierarchy
- Viewing the Design
- Using Filter Boxes
- Changing Edit Modes
- Reverting to Last-Saved Edits
- Saving Your Designs
- Displaying Design Summary Information
- Printing and Plotting Designs
- Exporting Design Data
- Exporting Design Images
- Closing Designs
- Configuring Custom Cells

## Creating Designs

Create designs by creating cellViews from the OpenAccess database.

<!-- image -->

## To create a design:

1. From the Console tab or the Library Manager, choose File &gt; New &gt; CellView .

Alternatively, in the Layout Editor, choose Design &gt; New &gt; CellView .

## Note:

The Design &gt; New &gt; CellView command is hidden if the design library is read-only or if you are in a read-only session.

The New CellView dialog box opens.

<!-- image -->

2. In the Libraries list, choose the library to hold the cellView.

You can filter the list of libraries by typing the library name in the empty box above the Libraries list. The system treats empty spaces on both ends of a string as wildcards.

3. Provide the following information for the new cellView:

| CellView Information       | Description                                                                                                 |
|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Cell Name                  | Name of the new cellView that you are creating.                                                             |
| View Name                  | Representation of the cell. For example, a cell can have a schematic view, a layout view, or a symbol view. |
| Editor                     | Product to use to open the new cellView.                                                                    |
| Open on Create (check box) | Opens the new cellView when you click OK .                                                                  |

## 4. Click OK .

<!-- image -->

The new design cellView opens in the specified product.

Creating a design creates a set of oaDesign objects in OpenAccess to contain design netlists, schematics, layouts and other types of device representations. The oaDesign objects hold the connectivity, geometry, hierarchy, parasitics, and floorplanning information for a design.

## Opening Designs

Open a design cellView to view or edit it. Use the Open Design dialog box to also open DMFiles and associated application.

## Note:

To improve the rendering performance for very large designs, set the Tcl preferences, deEnableMouseMotionInterrupt to true and deRuntimeUpdateFrequency to 500 .

## These sections cover:

- From the Console Tab
- From an Editor Window
- From the Library Manager
- Opening a Bookmarked Design
- Responding to Warnings while Opening Designs
- Reopening Recently Opened Designs

## Caution:

When opening legacy designs created in third-party tools, the Layout Editor automatically disables connectivity of routes that are not well formed. You can manually inspect the routes that are not well formed and decide whether you want to keep the routes or delete them.

## Note:

If the design permission is set to read-only, some menu commands might be unavailable.

<!-- image -->

## From the Console Tab

To open a design from the Console tab:

1. Choose File &gt; Open Design .
2. Specify the names of the library, category (optional), cell, and view.

Entering text in an input field at the top of a column filters the set of names offered. To return to the full list, delete text in the input field.

The unique combination of library, cell, and view name describes a design.

<!-- image -->

3. Click Open .

Alternatively, you can double-click the view name, or right-click and choose Open .

The design opens in the editor for this view.

Preference options apply. Active cellView level option settings also apply and take precedence.

## From an Editor Window

To open a design from an editor:

1. Choose Design &gt; Open .
2. Specify the names of the library, category (optional), cell and view.

Entering text in an input field at the top of a column filters the set of names offered. To return to the full list, delete text in the input field.

<!-- image -->

## 3. Click Open .

Alternatively, you can double-click the view name, or right-click and choose Open .

The design opens in the editor for this view.

Preference options apply. Active cellView level preference settings also apply, and take precedence.

## From the Library Manager

To open a design from the Library Manager:

1. In the Library Manager, specify the names of the Libraries , Cell Categories (optional), Cells , and Views .

Entering text in an input field at the top of a column filters the set of names offered. To return to the full list, delete text in the input field.

2. In the Views area, right-click the view name and select one of the following:
- Open : Opens the design in the default view and in full-access mode. The default view is determined by the dmDefaultView Tcl preference setting.
- Open with Layout Editor : Opens the design in the Layout Editor.
- Open with SDL : Opens the design in SDL.
- Open Read-Only : Opens the design in read-only mode.

The design opens in the editor for this view.

Preference options apply. Active cellview-level preference settings also apply, and take precedence.

If the cellview has a lock icon ( ), the cellview is currently opened in an editor or had been edited by a process that terminated abnormally. Right-click the cellview name and choose Lock Information . In the CellView Lock Information dialog box, you can:

- Find out which user is currently editing the cellview.
- If the cellview had been edited by a process that terminated abnormally, click Check Lock to release the lock.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Opening Two Designs

1. In the Library Manager, choose File &gt; Open . The Open Design dialog box opens.
2. Select the names of two views.
3. Right-click on any one of the selected view names and select Open with .

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## The Open Design With dialog box opens:

<!-- image -->

4. Select the application of your choice in the Applications area from the list of the registered applications for the view type. The application in which the design is open is set as the default.
5. (Optional) Select the Open in Read-Only Mode option to open the designs in readonly mode.
6. (Optional) Select the Make it as Default Application option to set the selected application as the default.
7. Click Open to open the design in the selected application and to close the Open Design With dialog box.

## Responding to Warnings while Opening Designs

Respond to warnings while opening designs to correct problems the system detects when it scans the design before it opens.

To respond to warnings:

1. Begin by Opening Designs.

For schematic and symbol views, the system scans the entire placed hierarchy. For layouts, the system scans the placed hierarchy down to the view depth.

2. If the system detects problems, a warnings dialog box lists them.

Two types of warnings can occur:

- Missing references, in both schematics and layouts.

These are references from the design at the current view depth to instance and via objects not at located this view depth. The system sees these as unbound to the design. Their definitions are not found in the current technology file.

To address the underlying problem, check to make sure the design uses the correct technology library, or add the object to the current technology library.

Unbound instances occur when the corresponding OpenAccess instance header (oaInstHeader) points to a non-existent master design. Unbound vias occur when an OpenAccess via definition (oaViaDef) is not found, or the master design for an OpenAccess custom via definition (oaCustomViaDef) is not found.

<!-- image -->

- Out-of-date multi-part paths (MPPs) in layouts. An MPP definition differs between the design and the technology file.
3. Choose an option.
- For missing references, you can visually identify the affected objects by adding them to the selected set: Enable Select Missing References .
- For out-of-date MPPs, you can update them: Choose Update MPPs .
4. Click OK .

## Reopening Recently Opened Designs

Reopen a design by choosing it from the accumulated list of recently opened designs.

To reopen a design:

- In any design window, choose Design &gt; Open Recent , and select the design by its library, cell, and view.

## Navigating the Design Hierarchy

Navigate designs to descend to varying levels of device representation. You can descend one instance at a time, and you can navigate using alternate methods.

These sections cover:

- Navigating One Instance at a Time
- Navigating Using Alternate Methods

## Navigating One Instance at a Time

Navigate one instance at a time to descend directly into the design. For information on using the ide::descend Tcl command, see Design Editing Tcl in the Custom Compiler Tcl Reference Manual .

The navigation commands of the Layout Editor and Schematic Editor are cascaded in different menus, but they work similarly in different contexts.

| Layout Editor       | Schematic Editor or Symbol Editor   |
|---------------------|-------------------------------------|
| Hierarchy > Descend | Design > Hierarchy > Descend Edit   |
| -                   | Design > Hierarchy > Descend Read   |

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Layout Editor               | Schematic Editor or Symbol Editor           |
|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| -                           | Design > Hierarchy > Descend Out of Context |
| Hierarchy > Edit in Place   | Design > Hierarchy > Edit in Place          |
| Hierarchy > Edit in Group   | -                                           |
| Hierarchy > Return          | Design > Hierarchy > Return                 |
| Hierarchy > Return to Level | -                                           |
| Hierarchy > Return to Top   | Design > Hierarchy > Return to Top          |

To navigate a design one instance at a time:

1. To descend to the next level away from the root for editing, choose the Descend or Descend Edit command and then select an instance. The Descend toolbar appears.

## Note:

The Descend or Descend Edit command is hidden if the design library is read-only or if you are in a read-only session.

The Descend toolbar contains different options in the Layout Editor, Schematic Editor, and Symbol Editor.

The following figure illustrates the Descend toolbar for Layout Editor.

<!-- image -->

The toolbar contains the following options:

| Option          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|-----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| New Window      | Descends in a new window. Tcl preference: deDescendLayoutNewWindow                                                                                                                                       |
| Open Mode       | When Auto (default) is selected, determines the descend mode automatically. When Edit or Read-Only is selected, enables Edit or Read-Only mode for the descended instance. Tcl preference: deDescendMode |
| Descend Lineage | Specifies a lineage during descend if more than one choice is available. Tcl preference: deDescendLineage                                                                                                |

<!-- image -->

| Option   | Description                                                                                                          |
|----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Shadow   | Turns on Shadow mode to increase the contrast between the selected lineage and the remaining objects during descend. |

The following figure illustrates the Descend toolbar for Schematic Editor and Symbol Editor.

<!-- image -->

The toolbar contains the following options:

| Option          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|-----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Descend         | Specifies if the target descend type is Instance (default), Group (figure group), or Both . Tcl preference: deDescendObjectType                                                                          |
| Edit In Place   | Enables the Edit In Place mode. This option is ignored if New Window is selected because it takes precedence. Tcl preference: deDescendInPlace                                                           |
| New Window      | Descends in a new window. Mutually exclusive with Edit In Place . Tcl preference: deDescendNewWindow                                                                                                     |
| Open Mode       | When Auto (default) is selected, determines the descend mode automatically. When Edit or Read-Only is selected, enables Edit or Read-Only mode for the descended instance. Tcl preference: deDescendMode |
| Prompt for View | Prompts for view. Tcl preference: deDescendDialog                                                                                                                                                        |

2. (Schematic or symbol view only) To descend to the next level away from the root for reading in the schematic, choose Design &gt; Hierarchy &gt; Descend Read and select an instance.
3. (Schematic or symbol view only) To descend and also switch the view, choose Design &gt; Hierarchy &gt; Descend Out of Context , select an instance, and choose the view.
4. To edit the instance in the same window, choose Edit In Place from the appropriate menu. The Descend toolbar appears.

The Descend toolbar for layout views looks slightly different than the one previously described. From this toolbar, you can set the target descend type as Instance (default), Group (figure group), or Both . The Group option corresponds to the Hierarchy &gt; Edit In Group command.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

If the instance is in an instance array, complete the operation by additionally choosing a component instance.

For typical descent operations, the edit design and the view design are set to the new design context, which is the instance's switched master. For edit in place operations, only the edit design is modified and set to the instance's placed master.

5. To reverse the last descent, choose Return from the appropriate menu.
6. (Layout view only) To return to a specific level, choose Hierarchy &gt; Return to Level . The Return to Level dialog box appears.
7. To return to the design root level, choose Return to Top from the appropriate menu.

<!-- image -->

## Navigating Using Alternate Methods

Use alternate navigation methods to have additional control while navigating.

- If you want to see all instances or masters in a hierarchy and select the descent level from the list, use the Hierarchy Navigator. See Hierarchy Navigator Assistant.
- If you want to configure a custom hierarchy that reflects the design, use the Hierarchy Editor. See Hierarchy Editor Tool.
- If you want to navigate by net name, use the Design Navigator. See Design Navigator Assistant.

## Viewing the Design

When you edit a design, you can use canvas menu options to zoom to different scales, fit the image size to an area, pan across the design, redraw after making changes, overlay fill views, and switch viewports.

At any time, you can also bookmark a design data and viewport combination. See Adding a Bookmark.

- Zooming
- Magnifying
- Peeking
- Fitting
- Panning
- Redrawing Designs
- Switching to Previous or Next Viewports
- Interrupting Rendering and Layout Edits with Ctrl+C

## Zooming

You can zoom to magnify the design view, changing the viewport scale by the ratio of viewport pixels to database units (DBUs).

- To magnify a canvas area, choose View &gt; Zoom &gt; Area .

Then use the mouse to set one point and rotate the mouse wheel or drag the mouse to adjust the scale.

- To increase magnification of the canvas area, choose View &gt; Zoom &gt; In , and rotate the mouse wheel forward.
- To reduce current magnification of a canvas area, choose View &gt; Zoom &gt; Out , and rotate the mouse wheel in reverse.

Alternatively, you can zoom in or out of the canvas area using your mouse.

- To zoom in, right-click and drag the cursor over the canvas area you would like to magnify.
- To zoom out, hold Shift as you right-click and drag the cursor over the canvas area you would like to demagnify.

<!-- image -->

## Magnifying

The Magnify command allows you to magnify portions of a design without zooming in on them.

## To magnify a design:

1. In a design, choose View &gt; Magnify or click the Show magnified design button

.

<!-- image -->

2. Select the Size of the magnify window. Options are Small , Medium , and Large .
3. Choose whether to Zoom in on an area of the design in the magnify window or Fit the magnified area into the design window. Zoom options are 2x , 3x , 5x , and 10x . Fit options are 150 px/uu , 250 px/uu , 400 px/uu , and 600 px/uu .
4. To lock the placement of the peek window, check the Position option and choose Auto , Near Cursor , Top Left , Top Right , Bottom Left , or Bottom Right .
5. In the design, hover the cursor over a portion of the design to view its details in the magnify window. Click the canvas to view that portion of the design fitted or zoomed into the design window.
6. Click the Magnify button again to return to the original view of the design.
7. Press Esc to exit the command.

## Peeking

## Note:

Peek functionality is only available for schematic designs.

The Peek command allows you to visually descend into a design without actually navigating lower in the design's hierarchy.

## To peek into a design:

1. In a design, choose View &gt; Peek or click the Peek into master design button
2. Select the Size of the peek window. Options are Small , Medium , and Large .
3. To lock the placement of the peek window, check the Position option and choose Auto , Top Left , Top Right , Bottom Left , or Bottom Right .
4. In the design, hover the cursor over an instance to peek into its hierarchy.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

.

<!-- image -->

5. To cycle through all available views in the peek window, use the shortcut keys Alt+P (for previous) and Alt+N (for next).
6. Press Esc to exit the command.

Alternatively, you can activate the Peek command by hovering over an instance and pressing the T shortcut key. When using the shortcut key, your most recent settings determine the window size and position.

## Fitting

You can fit a design viewport to specified extents to magnify the image size.

- To fit the viewport to the extent of the design, choose:

View &gt; Fit View in a design schematic.

View &gt; Fit &gt; View in a design layout.

- To fit the viewport to the extent of an Edit-in-Group mode figure group, choose:

View &gt; Fit Edit in a design schematic.

View &gt; Fit &gt; Edit in a design layout.

- To fit the viewport to the set of selected objects, choose:

View &gt; Fit to Selected in a design schematic.

View &gt; Fit &gt; Selected in a design layout.

- In design layouts (only), to leave the center point unchanged and fit the viewport to the finest available grid, choose View &gt; Fit Grid .

## Panning

You can pan to move the viewport to a different position on the canvas without changing the scaling factor. Use panning to view parts of the image not visible in the current window view.

To pan a design:

1. In a design, choose View &gt; Pan . The Pan toolbar appears.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

You can use the coordinate inputs along with an optional zoom level to pan to coordinate. The Pan toolbar includes the following options:

| Settings   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Point X Y  | The point input is a space delimited point (2 floating-point number). You may enter any of the following formats: ◦ x y ◦ x,y ◦ (x y) ◦ (x,y) To aid cut/paste from a coordinate file, the value entered for panning removes the following characters when the point field focus loses focus: "{}():,                |
| Zoom       | When disabled (default), the zoom level is disabled. Apply requires both X and Y coordinates to be valid values in user units within the allowed coordinate space. When enabled, you can specify the zoom level on the toolbar, or you can still press and slide the cursor on the canvas. Tcl preference: dePanZoom |
| Apply      | Applies the changes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Defaults   | Resets all of the options to your Custom Compiler environment default values.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

2. Press and slide the cursor on the canvas, or use the arrow keys.

Alternatively, you can pan a design by holding Ctrl as you right-click and drag the cursor around the canvas.

## Redrawing Designs

You can redraw a design to show recent changes.

To redraw a design:

- In a design window, choose Edit &gt; Redraw .

## Switching to Previous or Next Viewports

You can switch viewports to move between design contexts.

The system saves the viewport for each open design in the context and restores former viewports upon ascending after descending into a hierarchy.

You can switch to the next and previous viewport.

- To switch context to the previous viewport, choose View &gt; Previous Viewport .
- To switch context to the next viewport, choose View &gt; Next Viewport .

## Interrupting Rendering and Layout Edits with Ctrl+C

You can use the shortcut key Ctrl+C to interrupt a rendering process or an active command taking a long time to execute. If the application is not in either of these states, the shortcut key Ctrl+C triggers the Copy to Clipboard command.

To interrupt a create instance array operation:

1. In any design layout view, choose Create &gt; Instance .

The Instance toolbar opens.

2. Press F3 to bring up the Create Instance dialog box.
3. Choose an instance from the required library, cell, and view, and then specify the number of columns and rows to create a 500x500 instance array.
4. (Optional) Pressing Ctrl+C now activates the Copy to Clipboard command.

Press Esc to end the Copy to Clipboard command and return to the Create Instance command to continue your work.

5. Move back to the canvas and click on the required location to place the instance array.
6. Use the shortcut key Ctrl+C to stop the operation if it takes too long to wait.

The Create Instance command exits after the interrupt event.

## Using Filter Boxes

Filter boxes are available in assistants and tools such as the Design Navigator, Object/ Layer Panel, and Library Manager. The filter box filters the list directly below the text box to find the closest match, thus you can organize lists and locate items quickly.

These sections cover:

- Filtering Lists
- Displaying Selections in Filter Boxes

<!-- image -->

## Filtering Lists

You can use filter boxes to specify which items are displayed in an item list.

To filter lists:

- In the filter box, enter the full or partial name of the item or object you want to select using a simple string match, a glob-style pattern, or a regular expression which is controlled by the Pattern Matching option in the General Options dialog box. For help on setting the Pattern Matching option for filter boxes, see Setting General Options.

When you enter a partial word, the list displays all the items that contain the partial word.

For example, to find all route-related objects in a list of object types in the Object/Layer Panel, first click the Objects tab, and then enter route in the filter box.

The tool treats empty spaces on both ends of any string as wildcard characters. All searches or auto fills are case insensitive by default. However, if at least one uppercase letter is included, case sensitivity appears.

To clear a filter box, click X as shown in the following figure.

<!-- image -->

## Displaying Selections in Filter Boxes

You can set the Library Manager filter boxes to display single-selected items from a list. This feature is controlled by the dmShowSelectedInFilter Tcl preference.

## Note:

Using this feature changes the behavior of the Library Manager filter boxes. While item names are displayed in the filter box, the item list remains unfiltered.

## To display selection in filter boxes:

- Set the dmShowSelectedInFilter Tcl preference to true , as shown in the following example:

```
db::setPrefValue dmShowSelectedInFilter -value 1
```

The tool displays single-selected objects in the Library Manager filter boxes.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Changing Edit Modes

Change the edit mode to switch the editing context between read-only and write-enabled.

To change the edit mode:

- In a design window, choose Design &gt; Make Read-Write or Design &gt; Make ReadOnly .

If the design is currently write-enabled, you can save recent changes before switching to read-only mode.

For other ways to restrict editing of designs, see Restricting Design Access to Read-Only.

## Reverting to Last-Saved Edits

Discard edits when you want to revert the design to the last saved state.

Complete this single step:

- In any design window, choose Design &gt; Discard Edits .

Alternatively, you can revert the design to any previous state in this session by using the Transaction History assistant. See Transaction History Assistant.

## Saving Designs

Save a design to retain edits made after the last save operation.

Complete this single step:

- Choose Design &gt; Save .

The system saves all design views opened from this context, committing all in-memory changes to disk, and storing a record of all undo operations performed after the last save operation.

## Saving Designs With Hierarchy

Save a design with hierarchy to retain edits made after the last save operation.

To save a design hierarchy:

- Choose Design &gt; Save Hierarchy .

The system saves all open cells down the hierarchy without prompting. This feature is available only in the layout view.

<!-- image -->

## Saving Designs With New Names

Save a design with a new name to create an additional version with the most recent changes.

To save a design with a new name:

1. In the design editor, choose Design &gt; Save As .
2. To save this design in a different library, or as a different cell or view, select options from the Library, Cell, and View lists.
3. Click Save .

## Saving Designs With Schematic and Config Views

Save a design with a new name to create an additional version with the most recent changes and also create a schematic view and a config view for SDL design.

<!-- image -->

To save a design with a schematic view and config view:

1. In the design editor, select Tools &gt; SDL .
2. In the design editor, choose Design &gt; Save As .
3. To save this design in a different library, or as a different cell or view, select options from the Library, Cell, and View lists. To save this design with config view and schematic view, select the Config or Schematic options. See lxSaveAsCopyConfig and lxSaveAsCopySchematic in Schematic Driven Layout Tcl in the Custom Compiler Tcl Reference Manual .
4. Click OK .

## Saving Hierarchical Design Layouts

The Save Designs dialog box lets you choose which designs to save in a modified hierarchy. To show the dialog box when saving, set the dePromptSaveHier preference to true .

<!-- image -->

To save hierarchical design layouts:

1. From the top-level design, choose Design &gt; Save .

The Save Designs dialog box opens if at least one lower-level design is modified.

<!-- image -->

2. Select the designs you want to save.
3. Click OK .

## Checking and Saving Individual Design Schematics

You can check and save a schematic to confirm its compliance with electrical and semantic rules.

To check and save a design:

- In the design schematic, choose Design &gt; Check and Save or click Check and Save on the Standard toolbar. When Check and Save is clicked, the ise::check and de:save commands are executed, which runs checks, creates markers, and ensures the design is saved. The Save icon without a tick ( )indicates that the design is saved.

If no errors are found, the Console reports information noting that no rule violations were found.

If errors are found, a dialog box opens listing the number of errors, and the Marker Browser tool opens to assist with locating them. You can choose to Save anyway, or you can click Cancel , and fix the errors before checking and saving again.

<!-- image -->

## Checking and Saving Designs Represented as Text

To check and save a design's HDL format:

- In the text editor, click Check and Save on the Standard toolbar to perform syntax checking and cross view checks before saving the design.

If no errors are found, the Console reports information noting that no warnings were found.

## Checking and Saving All Designs in Libraries

You can check and save all schematic designs in libraries to validate them for compliance with electrical and semantic rules. This operation completes by saving all designs in the library. It is useful after importing design libraries exported from other tools.

To check and save libraries:

1. Open the Library Manager.

From the Console tab or any design window, choose Tools &gt; Library Manager or click the Library Manager button.

2. Choose Edit &gt; Check and Save Libraries .
3. Specify check and save settings as described in Table 57.
4. Specify libraries. You can filter the list, and use the buttons to specify libraries.

Table 57 Library Check and Save Settings

| Settings           | Description                                                                                                                           |
|--------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Force Checks       | Controls whether a design will first be checked to see if the rules need to be executed.                                              |
| Check Only         | Checks designs, but does not save them.                                                                                               |
| Remove all Markers | Removes markers set by all tools.                                                                                                     |
| Prompt for Save    | Prompts to save the design when errors are found, and lists the number of errors. Otherwise, saves automatically.                     |
| Views              | To include specific views in the check and save operation, enter them here, and leave the Exclude check box unchecked.                |
| Exclude            | To exclude specific views from the check and save operation, choose the Exclude option, and enter the views by name in the Views box. |

<!-- image -->

- To select all listed libraries, click Check All .
- To deselect all libraries, click Check None .
- To hide the libraries you have not selected, click Hide Unchecked .
5. (Optional) To see a preview of the selected list of libraries and designs, click Preview . You can further filter the set of designs to check, and optionally click Run to run the check and save operation.
6. After settings are complete, click Run to run the library check and save operation.

## Saving Designs With Backup

You can save your designs and create multiple copies of your designs at different stages of the design.

During a particular session, you can specify the number of backup files for you to view. To enable the generation of backup files, use the deMaxBackupCount Tcl preference and specify the maximum number of backup files to be generated, as shown in the following example:

```
db::setPrefValue deMaxBackupCount -value 5
```

Each time you save your design, the tool saves the current updates in the cellView and generates a backup file of the previously saved design up to the maximum specified number. The default is 0, that is, no backup file is generated.

<!-- image -->

## To view the backup files:

1. From the Library Manager, right-click the selected view and choose Open Backup .
2. The backup files are displayed with their timestamps.

<!-- image -->

Click the selected backup file to open. To retain the contents of the backup file, you must save it. Backup files are not retained after the current session.

The backup file format is compatible with the Laker file format. You can also open these files in Laker.

## Automatically Saving Designs

You can automatically save your designs at specified intervals to minimize data loss caused by unforeseen events, such as, you might accidentally close your design without saving the updates.

To enable automatic saving, set the dePeriodicSaveInterval Tcl preference and specify the time interval between automatic save operations in minutes, as shown in the following example:

```
db::setPrefValue dePeriodicSaveInterval -value 1
```

The default is 0, that is, automatic saving is not enabled. The tool automatically saves your design at the specified time intervals, if the design is modified. The tool, however, retains only the latest automatically saved copy of the design.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

In case of any eventuality, you can retrieve the automatically saved design. See Retrieving Your Designs.

## Retrieving Your Designs

You can recover your designs in case of an unexpected termination of the tool, such as due to a power outage. When you start a new session after such an event, you can access the latest manually-saved file (regular), retrieve the latest automatically-saved file (autosave) or the latest unsaved file before the tool terminated (recovery).

To view and open the available regular, autosave, or recovery files:

1. Optionally set the Tcl preference deRecoveryFileType to regular , autosave , or recovery , as shown in the following example:
2. In the Library Manager, select the name of the Libraries , Cell Categories (optional), Cells , and Views .

```
db::setPrefValue deRecoveryFileType -value recovery
```

Right-click the selected view and choose Open Read-Only or double-click the selected view to directly open the Open Read-Only dialog box.

<!-- image -->

3. The Open Read-Only dialog box displays the available files with the latest timestamps. When you set the Tcl preference deRecoveryFileType to regular , autosave , or recovery , the Open Read-Only dialog box appears with the corresponding file

<!-- image -->

selected. To open a different file, click the corresponding radio button and choose Open .

<!-- image -->

The autosave and recovery files open in the read-only mode. You must save these to overwrite the regular design. The autosave and recovery file formats are compatible with the Laker file format. You can also open these files in Laker.

## About Cell Mapping File

The cell mapping file helps to evaluate values for columns of an instance. The file defines the following parameters:

- LCV Pattern is the master placed by the instance to match. When it matches, the instances used the specified expression. Patterns follow a top to bottom priority and uses the pattern that matches first. If none of them matches, the expression dependent column values for an instance display default empty values.

Patterns support wildcard syntax. Each pattern can consist of 3 sub patterns separated by / to use for library, cell, and view names accordingly. If a / separator is not found, the specified pattern applies to the cell name.

For example, a pattern INV* matches to all cellviews with cell name that start with INV , regardless of library and view names. A pattern stdLib*/INV*/* matches to all cellviews from libraries that start with stdLib and cell names that start with INV . Use either none or two / separators.

Sub expressions can be any string or empty values, like myLib/INV*/ or /cell*/ symbolN* ).

- Device Type is the hard-coded constant value with no evaluation. You use it as a type of device for the instance.
- Spice Model is a simple SEL expression that starts with [@ and ends by ] . It evaluates the value for space model name for an instance. Spice Model can also be a hardcoded value as a regular string.
- Extracted Parameters are optional in the mapping file. This part refers to a list of space separated parameter names to store values in the database. The

<!-- image -->

se::populateDesignSummary Tcl command creates a corresponding column in the table for each unique parameter name.

- Expression1, Expression2 , are the expressions to calculate custom value for the instance of specific master cell. The expression can be:
- A hard-coded value (a simple string convertible to a number).
- A SEL expression to evaluate for an instance.

For an instance matching to a pattern in cell mapping, only the specified extracted parameter values are filed and other parameter columns are left empty. A pattern item of CellMapping can have many sub items, in case if a cell is mapped to other different devices with values specified for them. The Extracted Parameters expression of sub items can have a list of pairs with parameter name and predefined values but can be left empty as well.

Consider the example of MOS device. Set the parameters as follows:

<!-- image -->

| Attributes               |                         | Value                     |
|--------------------------|-------------------------|---------------------------|
| Prompt Library Cell View | referencel0 pfin symbol | Library CellName ViewName |
| Name                     | M1                      |                           |
| Origin                   | (3.5625.2.9375)         |                           |
| Orientation              | RO                      |                           |
| Usage                    | Normal                  |                           |
| Physical Only            | 口                       |                           |
| Placement Status         | none                    |                           |

| Prompt                | Value   |            |
|-----------------------|---------|------------|
| Spicemodel            | P       | spiceModel |
| CDLmodel              | P       | cdiModel   |
| L(Gate length)        | 10nm    |            |
| Planar difusion width | 0.17um  |            |
| nfin(No.of Fins)      | 6       | nfin       |
| nf（No.of Fingers)     | 2       | nf         |
| M(Multiplicity)       | 1       | m          |
| IsDummy               |         |            |
| Max drn voltage       | None    |            |
| Max srcvoltage        | None    |            |
| Min dn voltage        | None    |            |
| Min src voltage       | None    |            |
| Mtotal                | 2       |            |
| Gate Pitch            | 66nm    |            |
| Planar fin width      | 10nm    |            |
| Finpitch              | 32nm    |            |
| Parasitics Mode       | value   |            |
| AD(Drain area）        | 1fm     |            |
| AS(Source area)       | 1.5f.m  |            |

Check for the following details in the corresponding map file:

Version: 1.0

## patterns:

- -LCVPattern: LCV Pattern
- Device Type: Any\_mark\_name\_as\_summary\_category
- Spice Model: [@cdf\_parameter of spice model]
- Extracted Params: cdf\_parameter\_list
- Expression1: Expression\_created\_by\_parameters
- Expression2: Expression\_created\_by\_parameters

The cell mapping file is an YAML formatted text file defining values for the pattern and corresponding expressions. For example:

```
Version: 1.0 patterns: - LCVPattern: pfin Device Type: pfin Spice Model: "[@spiceModel]" Extracted Params: spiceModel cdlModel m nf nfin Expression1: "[@m]" Expression2: "[@m] * [@nf]" - LCVPattern: nfin Device Type: nfin Spice Model: "[@spiceModel]" Extracted Params: spiceModel cdlModel m nf nfin Expression1: "[@m]" Expression2: "[@m] * [@nf]" - LCVPattern: nfincaphv Device Type: nfincaphv Spice Model: "[@spiceModel]" Extracted Params: spiceModel cdlModel m nf nfin Expression1: "[@m]" Expression2: "[@m] * [@nf]" - LCVPattern: rppwl Device Type: rppwl Spice Model: "[@spiceModel]" Extracted Params: spiceModel cdlModel m l w Expression1: "[@m]" Expression2: "[@m] * [@l] * [@w]"
```

<!-- image -->

## Printing and Plotting Designs

Print a design to view it on paper or as plotted output. You can choose to print or plot the design, export it as a PNG, JPEG, or BMP image (see Exporting Design Images), or create an Adobe PostScript, PDF, or PDF With Links file for later printing.

The Job Monitor tracks printing processes. See the Job Monitor Tool.

You can submit print requests, check the current print queue, and cancel print requests.

- Submitting a Print Request
- Checking the Print Queue
- Canceling a Print Request

To set up a printer, use the db::createPrinter Tcl command.

## Submitting a Print Request

Submit a print request to add it to the queue.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

1. From the Console tab or the Library Manager, choose File &gt; Print &gt; Submit .

<!-- image -->

From a design window, choose Design &gt; Print &gt; Submit . Use this option when you want to print or plot the contents of the current design viewport.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

2. Specify a source cellview.

If the Source option is not already selected, you can directly choose a library, optional category, cell, and view.

<!-- image -->

From the design view, by default, the cellview in the current viewport is selected. To choose a different cellview, deselect the Current Viewport option and specify the image by library, optional cell category, cell, and view.

From the Console tab, a current viewport cellview is not available. Specify the image by library, optional cell category, cell, and view.

3. Specify print options.

Table 58 lists basic print options.

## Checking the Print Queue

Check the print queue to view current print requests.

To check the print queue:

1. Begin by opening the queue window.

From the Console, choose File &gt; Print &gt; Queue .

From a design window, choose Design &gt; Print &gt; Queue .

2. Choose a printer.
3. View the queue.

You can sort print requests by rank, owner, job, file, or total size.

## Canceling a Print Request

Cancel a print request to delete it from the queue.

To cancel a print request:

1. Open the queue window:

From the Console, choose File &gt; Print &gt; Queue .

From a design window, choose Design &gt; Print &gt; Queue .

2. Select a print request.
3. Choose Edit &gt; Cancel Print Job .

## Closing Designs

Close a design to remove it from view in the current editing session, and to close all open files for the current context. To retain changes, save the design before closing it.

## To close a design:

1. In the Custom Compiler Home tab, choose File &gt; Close Designs . The Close Design dialog box opens and displays the list of all open designs. If a design is not the parent file within its cellview, the file name appears within parentheses next to the view name.
2. Select the designs you want to close.
3. To change the selected designs to the read-only mode, click Make Read-Only .
4. Click Close .

<!-- image -->

If any of the designs are currently open in an editor, follow the instructions in the prompt dialog box to save the changes.

## Configuring Custom Cells

This topic describes the custom cell configuration syntax used in the Custom Compiler tool.

The custom cell configuration is set on lxCustomCellsConfig , which is a library CDF parameter. The tool reloads the lxCustomCellsConfig setting every time after the CDF parameter changes. If the overlay library scheme is applied, the CDF parameter reads from the overlay library.

## Grouping Custom Cells by Tags

The Custom Cells Grouping feature allows you to categorize design instances into groups based on user-defined tags, such as lcv, or parameter names. This feature is useful for organizing and managing large designs by grouping similar instances together, which can simplify downstream processing, analysis, and reporting.

## Benefits:

- Flexible Grouping: Group instances by any combination of lcv, or parameter values.
- Customizable Criteria: Define multiple grouping criteria to suit your design requirements.
- Improved Organization: Easily manage and analyze grouped instances for design reviews or further processing.
- Automatic Handling: Instances not matching specified criteria can be grouped as 'others' or discarded, based on your configuration.

| Argument            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|---------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| CustomCellsGrouping | Specifies grouping criteria to categorize instances into different groups by tags. It supports multiple values to define different grouping criteria. If CustomCellsGrouping is not specified, instances are separated into individual groups by each instance. Instances which are discarded in the previous rule are moved to the next rule. |

<!-- image -->

## Argument

tags

category

## Example 3 Grouping Custom Cells

## Description

Specifies the attribute to use for grouping. You can select either lcv or a parameter name. The tool groups instances based on the order of tag definitions.

- Value type: list
- Required if CustomCellsGrouping is specified
- Valid values: lcv or parameter name.
- The tool does not issue warnings or errors if an instance does not have the specified parameter.

Defines how to group items based on tag values. Each tag value can be associated with a list of lists. Use the keyword others to group cells that do not match any specified tag value. If others is not specified, cells that do not match any tag value are excluded from all groups under this grouping criterion.

- Error: If the value type is not a list of lists or a list, the tool ignores the tag and does not group instances by it.
- Error: If a tag is not specified in the tags list but is specified in the category, the tool ignores that tag and does not group instances by it.
- Error: If a tag name is specified without a corresponding value (for example, specifying lcv without providing values), the tool reports an error.
- Warning: If only others is specified for a tag, the tool groups all instances into a single group for the tag.
- Warning: If others is specified along with other values (for example, [others, 3n]), the syntax is incorrect. The tool treats this as if only others is specified.
- Warning: If the value is empty, the tool ignores the tag and does not group instances by it.

```
CustomCellsGrouping: -tags: [lcv, Custom_Cell_Type, pnType, l] category: lcv: - ["*", custom_cell, "*"] - ["*", custom_cmos_cell, "*"] Custom_Cell_Type:
```

<!-- image -->

```
- ["*_130_*", "*_260_*"] - "*_280_*" - others l: - 3n -tags: [lcv] category: lcv: - ["*", cap_cell, "*"]
```

<!-- image -->

## Arranging Assistant Tabs

Assistants are displayed as tabs within the design editor window. By default, they are arranged horizontally. You have the option of displaying them vertically.

To change how the assistant tabs are arranged in the window:

1. In the design editor window, choose Options &gt; General .
2. In the General Options dialog box, select the Interface category.
3. In the Visual section, do one of the following:
- Clear the Arrange Assistant Tabs Vertically check box to arrange the tabs horizontally. This is the default setting.
- Select Arrange Assistant Tabs Vertically to arrange the tabs vertically.

ArrangeAssistantTabsVertically

## About Assistant Synchronization

To facilitate design tasks, the Custom Compiler environment automatically synchronizes many of the interactions between the assistants and the canvas. For example, when you select a net in the Design Navigator, the shapes that belong to that net are automatically selected on the canvas.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

- Show me an example of assistant synchronization in SDL.

To further facilitate your design tasks, you can enable Cross Selection on the Annotation Toolbar so that actions in one of the following are automatically synchronized across the others: 0

- Constraint Editor
- Design Navigator
- Schematic Assistant (in the Layout Editor)
- Layout canvas
- Placement Gallery

As the following example shows, selecting a net in the Design Navigator selects and highlights the corresponding component in the Schematic Assistant and the shapes on the layout canvas. The design-level constraint that is associated with the net is also selected in the Constraint Editor. In the example shown, the Shadow Mode is turned on, and the selection highlight color is white.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The Annotation toolbar also provides other functions to assist you with your design tasks. See Annotation Toolbar.

The Error Viewer can also be synchronized with the Design Navigator. For example, if you select a violation that is associated with a net, the net is simultaneously selected in the Design Navigator. If you select a violation that is associated with an instance, the instance is simultaneously selected in the Design Navigator. To set up the synchronization, see Error Viewer Assistant.

During any of the synchronizations, you can enable the Shadow mode to optimize the selection viewing. See Annotation Toolbar.

Click the arrow and move the slider to increase or decrease the contrast. The Shadow Mode control is also available in the Design Navigator Assistant. |
|          | Specifies the selection highlight color. Click the button to choose a highlight color. To turn off highlighting, choose .
