## Displaying the Clipboard Assistant

To display the Clipboard assistant:

1. In any layout, schematic, or symbol view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Clipboard . The Clipboard assistant pane appears on the left side of the window.

<!-- image -->

If you have already executed Clipboard commands, the clipboard contents are listed in the assistant. Otherwise, the assistant is empty and begins recording the command operations.

2. You can undock the Clipboard assistant pane using one of these methods:
- Click and drag it to a required location.
- Click Dock (next to Close ).

## Using the Clipboard Assistant

Clicking on a thumbnail starts the Paste command for the current editor. If the Paste command is already running, it switches to the specified clipboard.

If the Paste command is running, the clipboard being pasted is drawn with a purple outline, as shown in the following figure.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The thumbnail with the purple outline is always the same clipboard as that indicated by the toggle button on the Paste toolbar. Otherwise, no outline is drawn around any thumbnail.

## Selecting the Clipboard Library

By default, the Clipboard assistant saves the last 10 clips in a Recent clipboard library, which is saved under the &lt;install\_dir&gt;/synopsys\_custom/deClipboard/Recent directory. Recent clips are persistent across tool sessions.

<!-- image -->

## Opening and Closing the Clipboard Library

Instead of using the default Recent clipboard library, you can also paste the clipboard contents from different clipboard libraries to the current editor window.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Changing libraries does not affect the Paste command. To paste a clipboard from a different clipboard library, simply click in the clipboard in another library and move your cursor to the canvas to place the objects to a required location.

To open clipboard libraries:

1. Begin by opening the Clipboard assistant.
2. On the assistant pane, click the clipboard library list and then choose Open/Close to open the following dialog box.
3. Click Open library to choose the clipboard library you want to view.
4. Click Cancel to close the dialog box and return to the assistant pane.

<!-- image -->

The selected clipboard libraries (for example: synopsys\_custom and yank\_Base) are now shown in the clipboard library list.

<!-- image -->

To close a clipboard library:

1. Begin by opening the Clipboard assistant.
2. On the assistant pane, click the clipboard library list and then choose Open/Close to open the dialog box.

3. Click Close library to choose the clipboard library you want to close.
4. Click Cancel to close the dialog box and return to the assistant pane.

The selected clipboard library is now removed from the clipboard library list.

## Copying Selected Clipboards

To copy selected clipboards from an opened clipboard library to another:

1. Begin by opening the Clipboard assistant.
2. On the assistant pane, choose the Recent clipboard library and then click Edit to modify the clipboard contents.
3. Select the required clipboard and then click Copy .

(Optional) To select more than one clipboard in the pane, use Ctrl-click to select each clipboard individually. You can alternatively use Shift-click or drag-left to select clipboards in the pane.

4. Choose an opened clipboard library (for example: synopsys\_custom) from the following dialog box and then click OK .

<!-- image -->

The selected clipboard from the Recent clipboard library is now copied to the synopsys\_custom clipboard library.

<!-- image -->

## Deleting Selected Clipboards

To delete selected clipboards from an opened clipboard library:

1. Begin by opening the Clipboard assistant.
2. On the assistant pane, choose the Recent clipboard library and then click Edit to modify the clipboard contents.
3. Select the required clipboard and then click Delete .

(Optional) To select more than one clipboard in the pane, use Ctrl-click to select each clipboard individually. You can alternatively use Shift-click or drag-left to select clipboards in the pane.

## Reordering Selected Clipboards

Clipboards are shown in order from the recently copied to the least recently copied. The same order is also shown on the Paste toolbar in the Layout Editor, Schematic Editor, and Symbol Editor windows.

To reorder selected clipboards in an opened clipboard library:

1. Begin by opening the Clipboard assistant.
2. On the assistant pane, choose the Recent clipboard library and then click Edit to modify the clipboard contents.
3. Select the clipboard you want to move.

(Optional) To select more than one clipboard in the pane, use Ctrl-click to select each clipboard individually. You can alternatively use Shift-click or drag-left to select clipboards in the pane.

4. Drag and drop the selected clipboard to the required position.

The clipboard library and the associated Paste toolbar are updated immediately after reordering.

## Typing Tcl Commands and Canvas Coordinates

Just as in the Console Tab, you can type Tcl commands and canvas coordinates in the Console assistant.

To enter Tcl commands and canvas coordinates in the Console assistant:

1. Display the Console assistant.
2. Click and select TCL .
3. Type the Tcl commands at the &gt; prompt.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Some Tcl commands accept relative and absolute coordinates for drawing operations as arguments. Use the following guidelines when entering coordinates:

- For relative coordinates, the first coordinate defines a width and height without respect to the origin, and the second coordinate locates the shape at a point with respect to the origin. Enter relative coordinates following this convention: &lt;float&gt; &lt;float&gt;.
- For absolute coordinates, the first coordinate defines a point with respect to the origin, and the second coordinate determines the width and height with respect to the first point. Enter absolute coordinates following this convention: =&lt;float&gt; &lt;float&gt;.

For example, you can create a rectangle where the first point is absolute (such as, =4 5), and the second point is relative (such as, 2 3), and the system commits an oaRect with a bounding box of {4 5} {6 8}.

## See Also

- Console Tab
- Typing Python Commands

## Typing Python Commands

If you prefer to use Python commands in the Custom Compiler environment, you can do so in the Console assistant. To run supported Python commands, see Tcl Interface for Running Python Scripts, Blocks, and Expressions.

To enter Python commands in the Console assistant:

1. Display the Console assistant.
2. Click and select Python .

<!-- image -->

3. Type the Python commands at the Python &gt; prompt.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

For example, you can type the following in the Console to source a Python script file (layoutExample.py):

```
Python> exec(open('layoutExample.py').read())
```

## The layoutExample.py file contains the following:

```
# In Custom Compiler, the following command can be used to source a Python file in the Python Console #     exec(open('layoutExample.py').read()) import oa # Create a cell in the library lib        = oa.oaLib.find("TESTLIB") maskLayout = oa.oaViewType.get("maskLayout") design     = oa.oaDesign.open("TESTLIB", "cell1", "layout", maskLayout, "w") # Get the top block or create it topBlock   = design.getTopBlock() if topBlock == None: topBlock = oa.oaBlock.create(design) # Get technology information tech     = oa.oaTech.find(lib) mgrid    = tech.getDefaultManufacturingGrid() dbuPerUU = tech.getDBUPerUU( maskLayout ) um       = dbuPerUU # Add prBoundary pa = oa.oaPointArray(4) pa.append((0   , 0)) pa.append((1*um, 0)) pa.append((1*um, 1*um)) pa.append((0   , 1*um)) prBoundary=oa.oaPRBoundary.create(topBlock,pa) # Add an instance blockDomainVisibility = oa.oaBlockDomainVisibility("inheritFromTopBlock") inst = oa.oaScalarInst.create(topBlock, "reference10", "nfin", "layout", "W2", oa.oaTransform(), oa.oaParamArray(0), oa.oaBlockDomainVisibility("inheritFromTopBlock"), oa.oaPlacementStatus("placed"))
```

<!-- image -->

```
# Create nets net1 = oa.oaScalarNet.create(topBlock,"net1") net2 = oa.oaScalarNet.create(topBlock,"net2") # Create design terminal termType = oa.oaTermType("input") term     = oa.oaScalarTerm.create(net1, "net1", termType) # Add a net to an instTerm instTerm = oa.oaInstTerm.create(net1, inst, oa.oaName("D")) instTerm = oa.oaInstTerm.create(net2, inst, oa.oaName("S")) # Create a path truncate = oa.oaEndStyle("truncate") segStyle = oa.oaSegStyle(int(0.01*um), truncate, truncate, 0, 0) polyLayer      = oa.oaLayer.find(tech, oa.oaString("POLY")).getNumber() m1Layer        = oa.oaLayer.find(tech, oa.oaString("M1"  )).getNumber() m2Layer        = oa.oaLayer.find(tech, oa.oaString("M2"  )).getNumber() drawingPurpose = oa.oaPurpose.find(tech, oa.oaString("drawing")).getNumber() pathSeg        = oa.oaPathSeg.create(topBlock, polyLayer, drawingPurpose, (int(-0.5*um), 0), (int(-0.5*um), 1*um), segStyle) # Creata polygon pa = oa.oaPointArray(4) pa.append((0   , 0)) pa.append((1*um, 0)) pa.append((1*um, 1*um)) pa.append((0   , 1*um)) polygon=oa.oaPolygon.create(topBlock,m1Layer,drawingPurpose,pa) # Creata rectangle rect=oa.oaRect.create(topBlock,m2Layer,drawingPurpose,(int(2*um),int(2*um ),int(2.5*um),int(2.5*um))) oa.oaDesign.save(design)
```

## Constraint Editor Assistant

Constraints are rules that designs must follow to ensure correct layout fabrication and operation. The constraints are either global or design-specific. You use the Constraint Manager to view and manage the global constraints. You use the Constraint Editor to create and manage design-specific constraints.

This topic describes the Constraint Editor and covers the following:

- Constraint Types and Sources
- About the Constraint Editor
- Displaying the Constraint Editor
- Viewing Constraints
- Importing and Exporting Design-Specific Constraints
- Constraint Notes

For the descriptions of design-specific constraints, including how to create them, see the following:

- Placement constraints: See the Custom Compiler SDL and Visually Assisted Automation Guide and the Custom Compiler Schematic Editor and Text Editor User Guide .
- Routing constraints: See the Custom Compiler Custom Router User Guide and the Custom Compiler Schematic Editor and Text Editor User Guide .

For information about the Constraint Manager, see Constraint Manager Tool.

## Constraint Types and Sources

The Custom Compiler environment interacts with the following constraint types:

| Constraint Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Source              |
|-------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------|
| Process           | A set of global rules and constraints that all designs must follow during layout and routing, such as spacing rules and clearance rules. For information about the rules and constraints in the technology database, see the Custom Compiler Technology and Display Resource File Reference Manual . | Technology database |

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Constraint Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Source            |
|-------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| Design-specific   | Constraints that the Layout Editor, Schematic Editor, and Custom Router must follow instead of or in addition to the process rules in the technology database. The design-specific constraints further restrict process constraints. You cannot set design-specific constraints that violate process constraints. | Constraint Editor |

Figure 39 summarizes the concept of the different constraint sources and the input into the various Custom Compiler products.

Figure 39 Sources of Design Rules Used by Custom Compiler Tools

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The design-specific constraints that are created and managed using the Constraint Editor are in one of the following categories:

- Placement : Constraints that control the placement of objects. For example, you can specify how objects are aligned. Some Placement constraints are created or updated automatically. For example, when you use the Symbolic Editor to realize instances from layout or schematic in the Matching mode, any existing Instance Matching constraint is automatically updated. To set or modify Placement constraints, see the Custom Compiler SDL and Visually Assisted Automation Guide and the Custom Compiler Schematic Editor and Text Editor User Guide .
- Routing : Constraints that control routing operations and results. For example, you can specify valid routing layers, the minimum width of each routing layer, preferred direction for each layer, and shielding styles. To set or modify Routing constraints, see the Custom Compiler Custom Router User Guide and the Custom Compiler Schematic Editor and Text Editor User Guide .

## Constraint Notes

You can associate note objects to constraints using the Constraint Editor Assistant .

The association can be done either to a new intent during creation or to an existing intent. These operations are available only for Schematic view designs and when seUseConstraintCellView is false. If seUseConstraintCellView is true and the intent has an associated note object in the Schematic design, you can see the appropriate visual feedback in both Schematic and Layout views indicating the existence of the associated note object.

## Creating Intent With Notes

During intent creation, if there is a valid note object in the selection set, then the selected note object is associated with the newly created oaConstraint . The tool examines the selection set for existence of the itkNote object and associates with a constraint.

## Note:

Only one itkNote object can be associated with a constraint. However, you can also add the itkNoteShape object, which is optional. Thus, as a valid selection for note creation is considered to be either a single itkNote object or itkNote and itkNoteShape objects (in addition to intent member objects). This operation is controlled using the preference cmConstraintEditorAttachNotesOnCreate . If the value is false, then the operation is ignored. The intent is created in the usual way but note creation is skipped.

## Adding or Removing Notes

When the itkNote object without any intent association is selected in the Schematic design, the cmAddNote action is displayed in the Intent context-sensitive menu of the Constraint Editor . If the action is completed, the note object is attached to oaConstraint and the transaction is registered in Transaction History.

<!-- image -->

If the intent has an associated note object, then seRemoveNote is displayed in the Intent context-sensitive menu of the Constraint Editor . If the action is completed, the note object is detached from oaConstraint and the transaction is registered in Transaction History.

## Note:

This operation affects only the note and the association of the intent objects.

## Data Model

The association between itkNote(oaText) (and auxiliary itkNoteShape ) object and the related oaConstraint is implemented by creating an oaGroup . The group name is formatted using specific descriptive prefix appended with index to make it unique in edit design. When the note is detached from the intent, the corresponding oaGroup is destroyed. The described data model implies that a note object can be associated only with intent types that are represented with a single constraint. Evidently these intent types should be supported in the Schematic design.

## GUI Changes

The associated note objects are reflected in various ways. In the Constraint Editor , the Note column is displayed to indicate that the intent has a note object. Every intent associated with note objects has a corresponding icon to indicate the same. This column exists both in Schematic and Layout designs when preference seUseConstraintCellView is false.

Highlight Notes is added to the Constraint Editor toolbar to highlight all design note objects that have association with a constraint. This button is available only in Schematic View.

<!-- image -->

Cross selection related with note object behaves in a similar manner as with intent members, particularly when the intent is selected in Constraint Editor . The associated note is highlighted on a canvas along with intent members and viceversa. If the note object is selected on the canvas, then the associated intent is selected in Constraint Editor .

## SDL Flow and Layout Design

The note object association is also reflected in Layout Design . A constraint Boolean parameter intent\_note is maintained to indicate that owner constraint object has an associated note in Schematic Design .

<!-- image -->

During SDL flow, the transfer parameter is copied onto Layout Design. This parameter only maintains note association and does not affect parameter matching logic like reporting mismatch and so on.

The lxBrowserFitToNote action is displayed in the Constraint section of Design Navigator that can be used to fit schematic assistant to the associated note object of the constraint.

<!-- image -->

| Terms           |           | Displays the list of terminals in the design. To search for specific terminals by name, you can alternatively use the Search and Replace Tool.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Groups          |           | Displays the list of figure groups or synchronous groups in the design.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Reference Arrow |           | Switches by reference to the next tab and displays components connected to the selected component. To see the reference arrow, rest the cursor on any component name. To switch to the next tab, click the reference arrow that appears. For example, clicking the Nets tab displays the list of nets and their connected terminals. Clicking the reference arrow to the right of a terminal name switches your view to the Terminals tab and list for that net. You can navigate farther through the terminals using their reference arrows, or you can return to the list of nets by clicking the Nets tab again.                                                              |

3. (Optional) Filter the number of items initially shown in any list by entering unique characters in the Filter box.

For example, to find all ground nets in a list of nets, first click the Nets tab, and then enter VSS in the Filter box.

The tool treats all searches or auto fills as case insensitive, by default. However, if at least one uppercase letter is included, case sensitivity appears.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

To quickly delete the text in the Filter box, click the X button:

<!-- image -->

4. When you locate the list of components you want to work with, highlight the component names in the Design Navigator.

Use the keyboard and the mouse.

- To highlight one name, click the name.
- To highlight a contiguous group, Shift-select the starting and ending names.
- To highlight multiple individual names, Ctrl-select one at a time.
- Alternatively, you can select a shape or shapes in the design, which highlights the shape or shapes by name in the Design Navigator.
5. (Optional) Filter the list to show only the currently highlighted names by clicking the Show Only Selected Items button:
6. With the list of components you want to use now highlighted, and optionally filtered, select them in the design.

## Renaming Components

You can rename the following components in the Design Navigator:

- instances
- nets
- groups

To rename a component:

1. Double-click the instance, net, or group to rename.
2. Enter the new name.
3. Press Enter.

If the new name already exists in the design, the renaming is not allowed, and a message is displayed in the Console.

Prepare for this procedure by Locating Components.

## Placing Design Areas in Shadow

You can place design areas in shadow for additional visual contrast between selected nets, and the surrounding design. To increase contrast between selected objects and the surrounding design, set the leShadowSelection Tcl preference to true.

To place design areas in shadow:

1. Begin by opening the Design Navigator assistant. From any design layout, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Design Navigator .
2. Locate a net either in the list or by selecting it directly on the canvas.

For more information about locating nets, see Locating Components.

<!-- image -->

3. On the Design Navigator toolbar, click

(Shadow Mode).

Shadow mode increases the contrast between the nets, and the surrounding design, allowing for more targeted net viewing.

<!-- image -->

4. To adjust the contrast, click the arrow and move the slider up or down.

## Setting Flight Line Display Options

Flight lines identify missing connections between physical objects on the same net in analog designs. You can set the display options to show or hide the flight lines and assign colors to the flight lines.

Before you set the display options, make sure the leDisplayFlightlines Tcl preference is set to true .

<!-- image -->

To set the flight line display options:

1. In the Design Navigator, click the Nets tab.
2. Enable the Connectivity Engine as follows:
- a. Choose Options &gt; Design . The Layout Design Options dialog box opens.
- b. Click the Connectivity tab, and then select Connectivity Engine .
- c. Click OK to close the dialog box.

Notice that in the Design Navigator, the list of nets shows current flight line color settings.

3. In the Design Navigator Nets list, select the nets for which you want to apply the flight line display settings.

Alternatively, you can select nets by selecting shapes, vias, or instances (instance terminals). When you select objects on the canvas, the nets associated with the objects are selected.

<!-- image -->

4. On the Design Navigator toolbar, click Set Flight Line . The Flight Line menu appears. The menu contents depend on whether you selected the Show Manual or Show Selected option in the Layout Design Options dialog box.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

If the Connectivity Engine Mode in the Layout Design Options dialog box is Netlist , the leFlightlineSyncSelection Tcl preference is set to false , and all flight lines are hidden by default.

If a net's signal type is power or ground, the flight line is hidden by default.

5. From the Flight Line menu, choose the display setting and the color to assign to the selected nets.

For example, you can select a set of nets on the canvas, and then use the Flight Line menu to assign the orange color to those nets.

Nets for which flight lines are not enabled are shown in black.

## Showing and Hiding Flight Lines From the Canvas

To show or hide flight lines while working with shapes on the canvas:

1. Make sure you set the flight line display options in the Design Navigator. See Setting Flight Line Display Options.
2. Right-click the shapes, paths, or instances, and then choose either Show Flight Lines or Hide Flight Lines .

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

When flight lines are displayed, you can view flight lines that run between centers of instances that do not have pins.

## Working With Nets

You can work with nets by generating net detail and net resistance reports, creating objects with net names, creating net groups, and creating constraints.

- Before You Start
- Adding Nets to Net Groups

For information about using the Design Navigator to check and report wire resistance and electromigration, see the Custom Compiler Electrical Checking and Reporting User Guide . For information about creating net constraints for routing, see the Custom Compiler Custom Router User Guide .

## Before You Start

Net information is based on logical and physical connections between objects.

When working with nets in design layouts, be sure to turn on the Connectivity Engine. See Enabling the Connectivity Engine.

The Design Navigator shows the list of nets and the objects that are on the nets. You can assign nets to objects by:

- Adding Nets to Schematic Objects
- Adding Nets to Layout Objects

## See Also

- About Connectivity

## Adding Nets to Schematic Objects

Adding net names to schematic objects associates the objects with connections in the design.

You can add nets to the following schematic objects during schematic creation: wire, route, and by-name connector. For example, when using the Add Wire command, you can list one or more Nets on the Wire toolbar or in the Add Wire dialog box.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Adding Nets to Layout Objects

Adding net names to layout objects associates the objects with connections in the design.

You can add nets to layout objects (such as interconnect paths or path segments, topology objects, buses, paths, rectangles, polygons, and ellipses) during layout creation. For example, when using the Create Interconnect command, you can list one or more Nets on the Interconnect toolbar or in the Create Interconnect dialog box.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Instead of typing the net names manually, you can automatically add the nets selected in the Design Navigator to the Layout Editor command Nets box.

To automatically add Design Navigator net selections to the Layout Editor command Nets box:

1. Set the leAutoPickUpNamesFromDN Tcl preference to true.
2. In the Design Navigator, select the nets.
3. In the Layout Editor, run one of the following commands. The net selections in the Design Navigator automatically appear in the Nets box for the command.

- Create Bus
- Create Interconnect
- Create Pin

<!-- image -->

If you modify the net selection in the Design Navigator, you can synchronize the changes and update the list of Nets in the Layout Editor command:

<!-- image -->

1. On the command toolbar or dialog box, click Synchronize . The Nets list update to match the selections in the Design Navigator.
2. To change the order of the nets, click , and choose one of the following:
- Ascending Order : Sorts the net names in alphanumeric ascending order.
- Descending Order : Sorts the net names in alphanumeric descending order
- Selection Order : Keeps the order in which the nets were selected in the Design Navigator.

<!-- image -->

The net synchronization is available for the following Layout Editor commands:

- Create Ellipse
- Create Polygon
- Create Rectangle
- Create Pin (by Shape)

<!-- image -->

- Create Interconnect
- Create Pin
- Create Via (Auto mode)
- Reassign Net
- Create Plane Boundary

## Adding Nets to Net Groups

You can use the Design Navigator to add nets to existing net groups.

To add nets to net groups:

1. From any design schematic or layout, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Design Navigator .
2. Click the Nets tab to list the nets in the opened design.
3. In the Nets list, select the names nets you want to add to a group.
4. Right-click the selected nets and choose Add to Group .

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

5. In the Add to Group dialog box that opens, locate the group, using the Filter box, if necessary.
6. Select the group by its name.
7. Click Add to Group .

The dialog box closes. The selected nets are added to the specified group.

8. To confirm the new additions to the group, see Viewing Grouped Nets.

## Creating Net Groups

You can create net groups to organize them and to facilitate net selection during schematic and layout operations.

To create net groups:

1. From any design schematic or layout, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Design Navigator .
2. In the Design Navigator assistant, click the Nets tab to show the list of nets.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

You can navigate to the list of nets you want to group. To do this, see Locating Components.

3. In the Nets list, select the net or nets by name.
4. On the highlighted name or names, right-click and choose Add to Group .
5. In the Add to Group dialog box, click Click to Add and enter a name for the group. Press Enter .

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

6. Select the new net group and click the Add to Group button to close the dialog box.

## See Also

- Adding Nets to Net Groups

## Viewing Grouped Nets

The Design Navigator lets you filter the Nets list so that you can view only the grouped nets. These filtered views allow you to quickly locate nets of interest.

To view only grouped nets:

1. From any design schematic or layout, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Design Navigator .
2. Click the Nets tab to list the nets in the opened design.
3. On the Nets tab, choose Nets by Group .

The list of net groups appear.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

4. Expand the group name.

The name of the nets you added to the group appear in the list.

## Setting Signal Types

To facilitate the editing of net information, you can set or change the net signal type in the Design Navigator.

<!-- image -->

To set or change the net signal type:

- In the Design Navigator Nets tab, right-click the net name, and then choose Set Signal Type .

<!-- image -->

## Viewing Information About Nets

The Design Navigator provides visual indicators to notify you of unrouted nets and unconnected pins. Having visual indicators can help you quickly locate issues in the design.

<!-- image -->

The Design Navigator Nets tab provides the following visual indicators:

- Gray background behind a net name indicates that the net is not routed.
- For nets with a gray background, values next to the net name show the number of pins or instPins that are not connected. To display the number of unconnected pins, set the heDesignNavigatorShowExtendedFlightlineInfo Tcl preference to true.

<!-- image -->

## Viewing Open Nets

Open nets are nets that are not yet routed. You can display the list of open nets for targeted viewing and troubleshooting.

To display only the list of open nets:

1. In the Design Navigator, click the Nets tab, and then click the Opens: n/m tab.

The Nets tab refreshes and displays only open nets.

- The total number of opens and open nets are displayed next to the net name.
- Under each net name is the list of flight lines and associated Connectivity Islands.
- Under each island is the list of terminals or instance terminals.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

2. (Optional) To zoom in to the location of the open net, right-click the open-net name in the Design Navigator and choose Fit .

<!-- image -->

## See Also

- Error Viewer Assistant

## Viewing Shorted Nets

Shorted nets are nets that contain short circuits. You can display the list of shorted nets for targeted viewing and troubleshooting.

A short circuit occurs when path segments on the same layer but belonging to different nets touch, causing the nets to connect. You can view short circuits using one of the following methods:

| Method           | Description                                                               |
|------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Design Navigator | Provides a high-level and quick view of shorts by net, layer, and object. |

<!-- image -->

| Method       | Description                        |
|--------------|------------------------------------|
| Error Viewer | Provides details about each short. |

This topic describes how to use the Design Navigator to view shorts in design layouts. For detailed views of shorts, see Error Viewer.

To display the list of shorted nets:

1. In the Design Navigator, click the Nets tab, and then click Shorts .

The Nets tab refreshes and displays only shorted nets. The total number of shorts and shorted nets appear next to the net name. In the following example, the bln net has two shorts and two shorted nets.

<!-- image -->

2. Expand the shorted net name and view the details (layer, path shapes, and via shapes).

<!-- image -->

3. To zoom in to the location of the short, right-click the short in the Design Navigator and choose Fit .

<!-- image -->

To troubleshoot short circuits, see Reporting and Locating Short Circuits.

## See Also

- Error Viewer Assistant

## Reporting Information about Nets

You can report information about nets in a design to collect this information in one place. The system shows this report in the Console tab.

Use the Design Navigator to report information about nets.

To report information about nets in a design:

1. Begin by opening the Design Navigator assistant. From any design layout, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Design Navigator .
2. In the Design Navigator, locate the net.

For more information about locating nets, see Locating Components.

3. On the net name, right-click, and choose Report Nets .

4. In the Console Output tab, view the report details.

For more than 100 nets, the report is generated as a file in the CSV format instead of in the Console tab with the name, reportNets.csv, under the synopsys\_custom directory.

For a single net, the report lists:

- Routed net length
- Routed net length on each valid routing layer
- Manhattan net length
- Ratio of routed net length over Manhattan net length
- Evidence of the use of non-foundry rules for minWidth , minSpacing , validRoutingLayers , validRoutingVias , and minNumCut

For a collection of nets, the report lists the information for a single net plus this additional information:

- Via usage: the total number of vias, the number of vias between adjacent valid routing layers, redundant via rate
- Number of completely, and partially, routed nets, and unrouted nets
- Number of nets that use non-foundry rules, expressed as a percentage of all reported nets
- Optionally reported nets over a user-specified ratio of routed over Manhattan net length
- Optionally reported nets longer than a user-specified length threshold

## Working With Figure Groups

You can use the Design Navigator to work with figures (or shapes) that you have grouped.

You can also use the Design Navigator to work with figure groups you have cloned to create multiple identical figure groups. You can synchronize the cloned figure groups. When synchronized, edits to figures in one group automatically apply to figures in all peer groups of this cloned group, synchronizing design development.

You can maintain clone group synchronization to easily apply editing operations that would normally be repetitive, and you can also break synchronization when you want to work with a cloned figure group individually. Editing the elements of the cloned group in other tools will break synchronization. However, you can synchronize them again in the Layout Editor tool.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

To create figure groups and synchronous clone figure groups, use the Layout Editor. See Grouping Objects.

This topic describes the following:

- Displaying the List of Figure Groups
- Filtering the List of Figure Groups
- Selecting and Unselecting Figure Groups
- Operating on Figure Groups
- Showing Synchronous Clone Groups
- Adding Figure Groups to Synchronous Groups
- Breaking Synchronization of Cloned Groups
- Synchronizing Cloned Groups to Peers

## Displaying the List of Figure Groups

You can display the list of figure groups, including cloned figure groups, by name in the Design Navigator. After you display the list of figure groups, you can perform various operations by group.

To display the list of figure groups:

1. Display the Design Navigator. See Displaying the Design Navigator Assistant.
2. In the Design Navigator, click the Groups tab. The list of existing figure groups appear.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

3. (Optional) Click the Design Navigator toolbar and choose one of the following commands:
- Expand All : Expands all figure groups to show subgroups or underlying components.
- Collapse All : Hides the subgroups or underlying components from view.

## Filtering the List of Figure Groups

After displaying the existing figure groups in the design, you can filter the list to show only the groups of interest.

Use one of the following methods to filter the figure groups in the Design Navigator:

- Displaying Cloned Synchronous Figure Groups Only
- Filtering Figure Groups by Name
- Displaying Only Selected Figure Groups

## Displaying Cloned Synchronous Figure Groups Only

The Design Navigator Groups tab menu lets you display all groups or cloned synchronous figure groups only.

<!-- image -->

To use the Groups tab menu to filter the figure groups list:

- From the Groups tab menu, choose one of the following options:

| Option             | Description                                                                                                                |
|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| All Groups         | Lists all figure groups in the open design that are not components of custom elements such as MPPs and rulers.             |
| Synchronous Clones | Lists cloned, synchronized figure groups (only) in the open design. Additionally shows groups with broken synchronization. |

<!-- image -->

## Filtering Figure Groups by Name

If the names of the groups you want to list share one or more unique identifying characters (for example, they all begin with the letter U), you can use the Filter box to enter the common characters.

Before you start, specify the filtering method to use in the General Options dialog box. See Setting General Options.

To display the list of figure groups that have common characters in their names:

1. With the Groups tab displayed in the Design Navigator, type one or more characters in the Filter box.

As you start to type, the Groups tab updates and shows only the figure group names that match the filter (characters) you provided. The filter also searches lower-level group names.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

2. To scroll to the matching names in lower-level figure groups:
- Press Enter repeatedly to scroll to the next name in the list.
- Press Shift+Enter repeatedly to scroll to the previous name in the list.

## Displaying Only Selected Figure Groups

<!-- image -->

- (Optional) After Selecting and Unselecting Figure Groups, to display only the selected figure groups in the Design Navigator and hide all other groups, click Filter Selected .

<!-- image -->

Click Filter Selected again to restore the list and unhide the non-selected figure groups.

## Selecting and Unselecting Figure Groups

After you display the list of figure groups, you can select one or more groups for editing operations. You can also unselect figure groups.

This topic describes the following:

- Selecting Figure Groups
- Unselecting Figure Groups

<!-- image -->

## Selecting Figure Groups

To select one or more figure groups:

1. To select all figure groups in the list, click the Design Navigator toolbar and choose Select All .
2. To select individual figure groups in the list:
- To only select one group, click its name.
- To select a contiguous sequence, Shift-select the names of the starting, and ending, groups in the sequence.
- To select multiple individual groups, Ctrl-select each one by name.

<!-- image -->

The Design Navigator highlights the names of your selected groups in the list.

## Unselecting Figure Groups

To unselect all figure groups (regardless of how many you selected):

<!-- image -->

- On the Design Navigator toolbar, click and choose Deselect All .

## Operating on Figure Groups

## Showing Synchronous Clone Groups

You can show synchronous clone groups for an open design through the Design Navigator. Additionally, you can highlight group connectivity.

To create synchronous clone groups, see instructions on working with figure groups in the Custom Compiler Layout Editor User Guide for Creating and Editing Objects .

To show synchronous clone groups:

1. Begin by opening the Design Navigator. (From a design layout open for editing, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Design Navigator Assistant ).
2. In the Design Navigator with an open design containing synchronous clone groups, view the groups.

<!-- image -->

- a. In the Design Navigator toolbar, click the Groups button.

By default, the system shows all groups. This icon indicates a standard figure

- [ ] group:

- b. From the Groups button menu (to the right of the Groups button), choose Synchronous Clones .
3. In the list of synchronous clone groups, view status.

Synchronous clone groups appear as group icons with circling arrows:

Clones out of synchronization with their peer group show a red x :

<!-- image -->

To synchronize unsynchronized clone groups, see Synchronizing Cloned Groups to Peers.

4. Show in the design connectivity in a synchronous clone group:

In the toolbar, click the Highlight Peer Group button, and choose a highlight color to

apply from the drop-down menu. The color yellow has been chosen here.

<!-- image -->

The system applies the selected color to group names in the list of synchronous clones. The system also highlights connectivity within cloned groups on the canvas, using this color.

## Adding Figure Groups to Synchronous Groups

The two ways you can add a figure group to a synchronous group are:

- Using the Add to Sync Group Command
- Using the Make Sync Peers Command

## Caution:

The Add to Sync Group command and the Make Sync Peers command are available only if you choose Tools &gt; Enable Layout Advanced .

## Using the Add to Sync Group Command

In the Design Navigator, you can use the Add to Sync Group command to add selected figure groups to an existing or new synchronous group. If a figure group already belongs in a synchronous group, the command moves the figure group from the current synchronous group to the newly designated synchronous group.

<!-- image -->

To add figure groups to a synchronous group:

1. In the Design Navigator, display the list of figure groups. For instructions, see Displaying the List of Figure Groups.
2. Select the figure groups.
3. Right-click the selected groups, and then choose Add to Sync Group .

<!-- image -->

The Add to Sync Group dialog box opens.

<!-- image -->

4. Do one of the following:
- In the Name list, select an existing synchronous group.
- In the Name box, type a name for the synchronous group you want to create.
5. Click Add to Sync Group . The Design Navigator Groups tab refreshes and displays the new groupings.

<!-- image -->

## Using the Make Sync Peers Command

In the Design Navigator, you can use the Make Sync Peers command to break selected figure groups from an existing synchronous group and add them to a new synchronous group. The new synchronous group is assigned a default name.

To use the Make Sync Peers command:

1. In the Design Navigator, display the list of figure groups. For instructions, see Displaying the List of Figure Groups.
2. Select the figure groups.
3. Right-click the selected groups, and then choose Make Sync Peers .

<!-- image -->

The selected figure groups are moved to the newly created synchronization group, which appears in the Groups tab with a system-assigned default name.

## Breaking Synchronization of Cloned Groups

You can break figure group synchronization manually, or you can break the synchronization through editing of synchronized clone elements when you transfer the design to another tool, and back again.

You can break synchronization of cloned groups when you want to work with their figure groups individually.

<!-- image -->

To break synchronization in synchronous cloned groups:

1. In the Design Navigator, display the list of figure groups. For instructions, see Displaying the List of Figure Groups.
2. Display the list of synchronous clone groups. To do this:
- a. In the Design Navigator toolbar, click Groups .
- b. In the menu that appears, choose Synchronous Clones .
3. Select the name of the cloned group whose synchronization you want to break, rightclick, and choose Break Sync Clone .

You can now edit this group without automatically applying the edits to all clones of this group.

To synchronize the groups again, see Synchronizing Cloned Groups to Peers.

## Synchronizing Cloned Groups to Peers

You can synchronize cloned groups to their peers again after breaking the synchronization. This option is only available for figure groups that have been created by cloning.

To synchronize cloned groups to peers:

1. In the Design Navigator, display the list of figure groups. For instructions, see Displaying the List of Figure Groups.
2. Locate the cloned group that is no longer synchronized ( ).
3. Select the cloned group name, right-click, and choose Sync to Peers .

<!-- image -->

The system synchronizes this group to its cloned peers.

You can now edit this group, and automatically apply the edits to all clones of this group.

## Device Palette Assistant

You can use the Device Palette assistant to drag-and-drop commonly placed devices onto the design canvas. You can create, and categorize, sets of devices on the Device Palette. (Devices that do not require added parameters can be used). You can place these device instances directly from the palette to the design canvas.

<!-- image -->

These sections cover:

- Displaying the Device Palette Assistant
- Adding Favorite Devices to the Device Palette
- Placing Devices from the Palette
- Adjusting Device Palette Contents

## Displaying the Device Palette Assistant

To display the Device Palette assistant:

- In a layout or schematic view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Device Palette .

The assistant docks along the window edge. Undock it by clicking, and dragging it.

## Adding Favorite Devices to the Device Palette

You can add favorite devices to the palette to create a collection of devices and make them available directly from the palette.

Use the Device Palette assistant to add favorite devices to the palette.

To add a favorite device to the palette:

1. Begin by opening the Device Palette assistant. In a layout or schematic view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Device Palette .
2. On the device palette, click the + button on the toolbar. The Add Device dialog box appears.
3. Specify or browse to find the library, cell, and view.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The palette allows referencing of a master of any view type from either the layout or schematic editor. However, device favorites you add here appear in the device palette for this editor only.

4. (Optional) Accept the suggested alias, or enter a new alias.

Aliases provide an additional level of classification, after categories, for the devices in the palette.

5. From the list, choose a category or enter a new category for the palette to offer.

A new category you create here will include this favorite device.

6. (Optional) Parameters of the device is collapsed at startup. You can click the button to expand the Parameters table.
7. Click OK to close the Add Device dialog box.

## Editing Favorite Devices in the Device Palette

You can edit favorite devices in the palette.

To edit a favorite device to the palette:

1. Begin by opening the Device Palette assistant. In a layout or schematic view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Device Palette .
2. On the device palette, click the button on the toolbar. The Edit Device dialog box appears.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

3. Specify or browse to change the library, cell, and view as needed.
4. (Optional) Parameters of the device is collapsed at startup. You can click the button to expand the Parameters table.
5. Click OK to close the Edit Device dialog box.

<!-- image -->

## Placing Devices from the Palette

You can place a device from the device palette to quickly repeat the instance creation process for favorite devices. Use the Device Palette assistant to place commonly used devices in a design.

To place a device from the palette:

1. Begin by opening the Device Palette assistant. In a layout or schematic view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Device Palette .
2. From the Device Palette toolbar, choose the category.
3. From the palette list, use one of the three methods.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

- Select the device by name, and drag it onto the design canvas.
- Double-click the device name, fine tune instance creation options, and place the instance.
- Select the device by name, click Create Instance , fine tune instance creation options, and place the instance.

When the palette places a device instance, it also adds it to the Recently Placed category for additional quick access.

## Adjusting Device Palette Contents

You can adjust device palette contents by adding or deleting categories, deleting device favorites, and copying device favorites to new categories.

To adjust device palette contents:

1. Begin by opening the Device Palette assistant. In a layout or schematic view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Device Palette .
2. To the right of the Category list box, click the Browse button (...).
- Add a category by choosing &lt;Click to Add&gt; and entering the category name.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

- Delete a category or device favorite (by its alias) by selecting it and clicking the red x .

The Recently Placed and Uncategorized categories cannot be deleted. However, you can delete device favorites from any category where they are listed.

- Copy a favorite (by its alias) to another category by selecting it by name, and dragging it to the destination category.
3. Click OK .

## Using the Error Viewer Assistant in the Schematic Editor

Starting from W-2024.09 release, the Error Viewer assistant is the default error viewer in the Schematic Editor. Which means, the default of the seUseErrorViewer preference is true .

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

To run ERC or SRC checks on a read-only schematic design using the Error Viewer assistant to view the error markers, perform the following steps.

1. Disable the Create Violation Markers in Designs option in the Schematic Editor Check Options dialog box.
2. Choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer to open the assistant and use the features described in the following sections.

To use Marker Browser Assistant as the error viewer in the Schematic Editor, set the seUseErrorViewer preference as false by typing db::setPrefValue seUseErrorViewer -value false in the Console.

## Managing the Marker Tree

The marker tree shows marker categories along with the number of markers and the color used for categories and markers.

The marker tree consists of the following columns: Category, Count, and Color.

- In the Category column, markers can be classified by the following categories:

| Category     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Design       | Shows the name of the opened design. When the Hierarchy option is enabled, the design name in bold represents the current opened design while the design name in plain represents the design at other hierarchy levels. See Viewing Error Markers Hierarchically for more details.                          |
| Tool         | Shows the tool that verifies the violations. This information is derived from the oaMarker attributes.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Severity     | Shows the severity type of violations. This information is derived from the oaMarker attributes. Severity types are fixed values as defined by OpenAccess: ◦ Error ◦ Warning ◦ Signed Off Error ◦ Information ◦ Annotation ◦ Fatal Error ◦ Critical Error ◦ Acknowledge Warning ◦ Signed Off Critical Error |
| ShortMessage | Shows the short message of markers. The short message is set as the rule ID, for example: m1.s.1. If the rule is converted from a constraint, the constraint ID is used.                                                                                                                                    |

<!-- image -->

| Category   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Message    | Shows the long message of markers. The long message is set as the description of the rule set. For example, the minimum spacing rule description can be Minimum metal space in MINP direction (horizontal) . If such information is not found, the tool composes a name from the original content of the rule or constraint. If the violation marker relates to spacing or width, the Error Viewer shows an actual distance and a needed distance at the beginning of the message field, as shown in the following figure, to ease the effort required for violation fixing. |

- The Count column shows the number of markers in the corresponding category. The Error Viewer assistant shows the Count column by default. The Error Viewer displays the column title as Count(%d) where %d indicates the number of markers in the corresponding category. This column is not resizable.

For more information on how to show the column, see Manipulating Error Markers.

- The Color column shows the mapping highlight color for each category. The Error Viewer assistant hides the Color column by default. This column is not resizable.

This column is available only when the By Category option is enabled for highlight colors in the Error Viewer Options dialog box.

For information on how to assign colors to highlighted categories or markers, see Managing Highlight Colors.

For more information on how to show the column, see Manipulating Error Markers.

These sections cover:

- Displaying Category Levels in the Marker Tree
- Configuring the Marker Tree Contents
- Wildcard Matching in the Display Filter

## Displaying Category Levels in the Marker Tree

By default, markers are classified in the Category column by the following sequence of display levels: Design, Tool, ShortMessage, and Message.

To change the display level of categories:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. From the Category column, right-click the column header to show the category menu.
3. Click the drop-down list to the right of the categories to change the selected display levels.

<!-- image -->

Click OK to commit the change. The Category column is refreshed and the marker tree is collapsed.

The category level you defined in the marker tree affects the Filter Display dialog box contents. See Configuring the Marker Tree Contents for more information.

4. (Optional) Choose the arrow buttons next to the marker category to expand the current node's subtree and see the underlying markers in the category.

Double-click the marker category to expand or collapse specific levels.

For more information on showing or hiding category levels in the marker tree, see Manipulating Error Markers.

## Automatically Expanding Marker Levels in Error Viewer

The Error Viewer in Custom Compiler provides a centralized interface for reviewing and managing error markers generated by various tools, such as Via Checker. Automatically expanding marker levels after loading error data streamlines the review process, allowing you to quickly access relevant error categories without manual navigation.

You can control the default expansion level of the marker tree in the Error Viewer using the deErrorViewerAutoExpandMarkerLevel preference. This setting determines how many levels of the marker tree are expanded automatically when error markers are loaded. The default is 2.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Configuring the Marker Tree Contents

You can focus on the data that you want to focus on by using a display filter.

To configure the marker tree contents with single or multiple categories:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. Click the toolbar menu and choose Options . In the Error Viewer Options dialog box, set Filter Type as Multiple Category , and then click OK . See Setting Filter Type for Categories for more information. D
3. Click the toolbar menu and choose Filter Display .

<!-- image -->

The Filter Display dialog box appears.

<!-- image -->

Contents of the Filter Display dialog box vary when you change the category level in the marker tree, as shown in the following figure. See Displaying Category Levels in the Marker Tree for more information.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

By default, the tool uses a wildcard character * to show all of the violations in the marker tree.

4. (Optional) Click None to deselect all severity types. Choose any of the severity types you want to display.
5. Click OK to commit the change. The marker tree is refreshed and collapsed.
6. Click the toolbar menu and choose Options . In the Error Viewer Options dialog box, set Filter Type as Single Category , and then click OK . See Setting Filter Type for Categories for more information. D

<!-- image -->

Now you can only filter violations from one of the available categories: Design, Tool, ShortMessage (default), and Message.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

You may enter the required filter string in the filter text box, which corresponds to Filters and Case Sensitivity settings in the General Options dialog box. See Setting General Options for more information.

<!-- image -->

## Wildcard Matching in the Display Filter

You can use the wildcard character * when typing a filter string in the text box, for example: G*. Click Apply to refresh the contents of the marker tree.

| Characters   | Functions                                                                                                                                    | Examples                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| *            | Matches any sequence of zero or more characters.                                                                                             | t*t matches test or tonight but not tactic .                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ?            | Matches any single character. This is the same as "." in full regular expression (regrexps).                                                 | m?n matches man , men or min but not moon .                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [CHARS]      | Matches any character in square brackets. If CHARS contains a sequence of the form a-b, any character between a and b, inclusive, may match. | *a[ch] matches all strings that end with either ac or ah .                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| \            | Use the backslash character to escape a single character.                                                                                    | If string var equals to var="abcd\ef*g?h" • *\?* matches string that contains ? , so it matches var . • *[\]* matches string that contains \ , so it matches var . • *[12]* matches string that contain 1 or 2 , so it does not match var . |

The tool saves the filter history (Figure 41) so that you can easily choose from previously used filters.

<!-- image -->

## Viewing Marker Categories

You can view and highlight the categories of markers in the marker tree and the design.

To view and highlight the categories of markers:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. From the marker tree, choose the design and click Highlight Previous Category and Highlight Next Category on the toolbar to navigate to the previous or next marker category shown in the marker tree and also highlight the associated objects on the canvas.
3. (Optional) Click Clear Highlight to clear highlights of markers and their associated objects at the current design level.

## Viewing Error Markers

You can view and highlight error markers in the marker tree and the design, and also show more detailed messages associated with the highlighted markers.

To view and highlight error markers:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. From the marker tree, choose the design or any severity type of a category (for example: CriticalError).

(Optional) From the marker table pane, choose a marker of the selected design or category.

3. Click Highlight Previous Marker and Highlight Next Marker on the toolbar to navigate to the previous or next marker relative to the selected category and highlight the marker and its associated object on the canvas.
4. (Optional) Click Highlight Selected Marker to highlight the selected marker and its associated object on the canvas. You can find the longer message of the highlighted marker in the lower region of the Error Viewer.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

5. (Optional) To show more than one marker or a marker category, use Ctrl+click to select each marker individually.
6. (Optional) Click Clear All Highlight to clear highlights of markers and their associated objects at the current design level.

## Viewing Error Markers Hierarchically

By default (hierarchy disabled), the marker tree displays only the markers in the current edit design. When the Hierarchy option is on, you can view all markers from the top design hierarchy to the hierarchy that are visible down to the view depth.

To view error markers from the top design hierarchy to down:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. Click the toolbar menu and choose Hierarchy . For more information about toolbar menu options, see Manipulating Error Markers. D
3. Set the stop level on the Hierarchy toolbar to 1.

<!-- image -->

You can specify the start and stop levels from the Design Options dialog box (see Setting Layout Design Options) or from the Start Level and Stop Level boxes on the Hierarchy toolbar.

The Error Viewer updates the marker tree and shows the design name of the current opened design in bold text to distinguish it from designs (shown in plain text) at other hierarchy levels.

<!-- image -->

You can use the options available when you right-click selections from the list.

Table 70 describes the Error Viewer options menu in the marker tree for descending design levels.

<!-- image -->

Table 70 Error Viewer Options Menu in Marker Tree for Descending Design Levels

| Error Viewer Menu   | Description                                                                                           |
|---------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Descend             | Moves down to a lower hierarchy level to let you view and highlight the markers at the visible depth. |
| Unsort Tree         | Restores the marker tree order to its initial state.                                                  |
| Collapse            | Collapses the selected categories.                                                                    |
| Expand              | Expands the selected categories.                                                                      |
| Hide Count Column   | Hides the Count column from the marker tree.                                                          |
| Hide Color Column   | Hides the Color column from the marker tree.                                                          |

4. Right-click the design shown in plain text and choose Descend .

The Error Viewer updates the marker tree and shows the design name in bold.

Pushing and popping through the hierarchies causes the display of the marker tree to update, always showing the markers down to the visible depth.

5. Act on the markers selected in the marker tree or the marker table pane. For more information, see Manipulating Error Markers.
6. Click the Return button on the Hierarchy toolbar to return to the upper level of the design hierarchy.

(Optional) Click the Return to Top button on the Hierarchy toolbar to return to the top level.

<!-- image -->

## Manipulating Error Markers

You can manipulate error markers you have selected in the Error Viewer. The Error Viewer offers actions from the Error Viewer toolbar buttons and toolbar menu, and also through the options menu (the right-click selections).

To manipulate error markers in the marker tree:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. Act on the error markers selected in the marker tree.

You can use the toolbar buttons and toolbar menu. You can additionally use the options available when you right-click selections from the list.

- Table 71 describes actions you can perform using the Error Viewer toolbar buttons.

## Sorting Error Markers

You can sort error markers in descending (the default) or ascending order to easily access the ones you want to browse.

<!-- image -->

To sort error markers in the marker tree:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. From the Category column, click the column header to sort markers in the marker tree.

(Optional) Click the Tree View button menu and choose Unsort to restore the marker tree order to its initial state.

## Deleting Error Markers

You can delete more than one error marker in the marker tree and remove the highlight of the marker from the canvas.

To delete error markers:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. In the Error Viewer, choose the marker you want to delete.

(Optional) To select more than one marker or a marker category, use Ctrl+ click to select each marker individually.

(Optional) To select a range of markers or marker categories, use Shift-click or drag-left to quickly select them.

3. Click Delete Marker to remove the selected marker(s) from the hierarchical tree and the design.

The tool clears the highlight of markers on the canvas and also refreshes the marker tree.

## Customizing Marker Information to Display

You can now customize viewing the detailed information of the error markers that you have selected in the marker pane.

To customize the detailed information of a marker:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. In the Error Viewer, right-click the marker for which you want to customize the detailed information.
3. Check the information items to display from the menu, as shown in the following figure.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The selected marker displays detailed information for only the information items that you have selected.

## Showing Tooltips of Markers

You can show a tooltip containing the tool information, the severity type, and the short and long messages when hovering the pointer over a marker on the canvas.

To show the tooltip of a marker:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. Click the toolbar menu and make sure that Show Tip is on.
3. On the canvas, hover the pointer over the marker you want to check.

When there are overlapped error markers, the tooltip uses the format (num1/num2) where num1 indicates the index and num2 indicates the total number of markers.

<!-- image -->

Use shortcut keys 1 and 2 to cyclically show the tooltip of each marker.

<!-- image -->

## Customizing the Error Viewer Layout Style

Instead of displaying the Error Viewer with the default layout style, you can change the layout with an alternate style. The tool provides the following layout styles: Style 1 (the default), Style 2, and Style 3.

To apply another layout style:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. Click the toolbar menu and choose Layout Style &gt; Style 2 to apply Style 2 to the layout.

<!-- image -->

## Viewing Markers in Shadow

You can view design areas in shadow for additional visual contrast between selected markers and the surrounding design.

- To view design areas in shadow:

Click the Cross Shadow button from the design layout view to turn on the Shadow Mode. Click the arrow and move the slider to increase or decrease the contrast.

## Managing Highlight Colors

You can manage highlight colors of markers and their associated objects to control their visual display in a design, and also assign highlight colors for different categories.

<!-- image -->

## To set highlight colors:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. Click the toolbar menu and choose Options to open the Error Viewer Options dialog box.

<!-- image -->

By default, the tool assigns colors cyclically through a recurring sequence within predefined colors. Table 77 describes predefined colors and color packets to highlight markers and their associated objects. For more information on how to view or edit color packets, see Display Resource Editor Tool.

The tool draws the outline of highlighted markers with solid color lines, and also draws the outline of their highlighted objects with dashed color lines.
