3. (Optional) From the Error Viewer Options dialog box, choose Fixed and pick a color from the list. The tool highlights markers and their associated objects in the same color.
4. From the Error Viewer Options dialog box, choose By Category to set different colors for different categories.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

5. Click OK to commit the change. You can find the Color column showing in the marker tree pane.

By default, the tool only assigns colors to each lowest level of categories cyclically through a recurring sequence within predefined colors, described in Table 77.

6. From the Color column, double-click to choose a preferred color for the selected category.

<!-- image -->

Changing the color of any upper levels of categories disables the color of underlying markers in the hierarchical tree.

<!-- image -->

## Highlighting Markers When Selecting

You can highlight error markers and their associated objects on the canvas when selecting markers in the marker table pane.

To highlight markers and their associated objects on the canvas when selecting markers:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. Click the toolbar menu and choose Options to open the Error Viewer Options dialog box.
3. From the Error Viewer Options dialog box, turn on the Highlight Marker when Selecting option.
4. Click OK to save the changes.
5. In the marker table pane, choose the marker you want to highlight.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

(Optional) To select more than one marker, use Ctrl+click to select each marker individually.

(Optional) To select a range of markers, use Shift+click or drag-left to quickly select them.

## Highlighting With an X Symbol

You can highlight markers by placing an X symbol at the center of the marker's bounding box.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

To highlight markers with an X symbol:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. Click the toolbar menu and choose Options to open the Error Viewer Options dialog box.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

3. From the Error Viewer Options dialog box, turn on the Highlight X Symbol option.
4. Click OK to save the settings.

## Setting Zoom Mode after Highlighting

You can zoom to the newly highlighted objects after enabling the Zoom Mode after Highlighting option.

To set the option:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. Click the toolbar menu and choose Options to open the Error Viewer Options dialog box.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

3. From the Error Viewer Options dialog box, ensure that the Zoom Mode after Highlighting option is enabled so that you can set the following options:

When Pan is selected, you can pan to the newly highlighted objects without changing the zoom ratio of the canvas

When Zoom is selected, you can zoom to the newly highlighted objects with the specified zoom ratio. By default, the zoom ratio is 0.7.

4. Click OK to save the settings.

## Setting Highlight Actions

You can set the highlight actions to highlight markers, the associated objects of markers, fixing guides, or parent markers. ← ← ← 口 ←

<!-- image -->

## To set the option:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. Click the toolbar menu and choose Options to open the Error Viewer Options dialog box.
3. From the Error Viewer Options dialog box, go to the Set Highlight Action for section. By default, the tool highlights markers, the associated objects of markers, and fixing guides when Marker , Associated Objects , and Fixing Guides are enabled.

<!-- image -->

To highlight only markers, disable all the options and then enable Marker .

To highlight only the associated objects of markers, disable all the options and then enable Associated Objects .

To highlight only fixing guides, disable all the options and then enable Fixing Guides .

To highlight only parent markers, disable all the options and then enable Parent Markers .

4. Click OK to save the settings.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Specifying the Maximum Number of Markers to Display

You can specify how many markers you want to display in the marker table pane.

To set the maximum number of markers to display:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. Click the toolbar menu and choose Options to open the Error Viewer Options dialog box.
3. From the Error Viewer Options dialog box, turn on the Max Markers to Display option. By default, the maximum number is 10000.
4. Click OK to save the settings.

<!-- image -->

## Clearing All Highlights When Closing Error Viewer

To clear all highlights when closing the Error Viewer:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. Click the toolbar menu and choose Options to open the Error Viewer Options dialog box.
3. From the Error Viewer Options dialog box, turn on the Clear All Highlights when Closing Error Viewer option.
4. Click OK to save the settings.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Selecting First Item of Marker Table

To automatically select the first item of the marker table when you change the selection in the marker tree:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. Click the toolbar menu and choose Options to open the Error Viewer Options dialog box.
3. From the Error Viewer Options dialog box, turn on the Auto Select First Item of Marker Table option.

<!-- image -->

The associated Tcl preference is deErrorViewerAutoSelectMarkerTable .

4. Click OK to save the settings.

<!-- image -->

## Setting Filter Type for Categories

To set the category filter type:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. Click the toolbar menu and choose Options to open the Error Viewer Options dialog box.
3. From the Error Viewer Options dialog box, go to the Filter Type section, choose Single (default) to show single category, or choose Multiple to allow showing multiple categories by the Filter Display option.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The associated Tcl preference is deErrorViewerFilterType .

<!-- image -->

4. Click OK to save the settings.

## Note:

Filter Display is available in the toolbar menu only when you set Filter Type as Multiple Category in the Error Viewer Options dialog box. See Configuring the Marker Tree Contents for more information.

## Loading Calibre Result

## Note:

This feature is not available when using the Error Viewer assistant on an overlay design in the Schematic Editor.

To load a third-party result file into the Error Viewer:

1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design layout, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Error Viewer .
2. Click the toolbar menu and choose Load Result to open the Error Viewer Load Result dialog box. D
3. From the Error Viewer Load Result dialog box, specify necessary files with the options in the following table.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Option    | Description                                                                                                                                                                |
|-----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| ToolName  | When enabled, specifies the tool name of the result file. The tool name can be set to an oaMarker's tool name. When disabled (default), the default tool name is Calibre . |
| Rule File | When enabled, specifies the rule file of the result file. (Off by default).                                                                                                |

Table 78 Load Result Options

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Option                                | Description                                                                                                               |
|---------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Waive File                            | When enabled, specifies the waive file. (Off by default).                                                                 |
| Result File                           | Specifies the result file.                                                                                                |
| Create Markers to Current Edit Design | When enabled, creates markers to the current edit design. When disabled (default), creates markers to the overlay design. |
| Speed Mode                            | Used for loading large Calibre result files over 50MB.                                                                    |

4. Click OK to save the settings and load the result file.

After loading the result file, the tool creates markers in the current working cellview. The severity for each created marker is set as Error Severity . If the marker is from the waive file, the severity is set as AcknowledgedWarning .

The rule type in the result file is mapped as the marker's ShortMessage attribute.

The explanation strings in the result file are mapped as the marker's Message attribute if no rule file is specified or no corresponding rule information in the rule file. If a rule file is specified and there is a corresponding rule information of a rule type, the rule information of the rule type is mapped as the marker's Message attribute.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Loading RedHawk Result

The Error Viewer parses the result file and creates as oaMarkers in the current working cellview.

<!-- image -->

Table 79 Load Result Options

| Option           | Description                                                                                                                                                                |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| ToolName         | When enabled, specifies the tool name of the result file. The tool name can be set to an oaMarker's tool name. When disabled (default), the default tool name is RedHawk . |
| Short File       | When enabled, specifies a short file for short error information. (Off by default).                                                                                        |
| Open File (Wire) | When enabled, specifies open file for wire. (Off by default).                                                                                                              |
| Open File (Via)  | When enabled, specifies open file for via and net. (Off by default).                                                                                                       |
| EM File          | When enabled, reports the EM violations. (Off by default).                                                                                                                 |
| EM Threshold(%)  | Error marker information is displayed if this value is greater than the user-specified value. Valid range is 10%~1000% (Default is 100%.)                                  |
| Shrink           | If user specified, the coordinates are converted to Shrink rate. Valid range is 0.01~1.0 (Default is 1.0).                                                                 |

<!-- image -->

## Loading Generic Format File

The Error Viewer does not support export/import of a text file, but only supports the Save to view feature. However, this feature is disabled during co-design. To be able to share errors to debug and avoid accidental deletion of errors in the Error Viewer , the tool allows conversion of different error marker formats into a generic format so that the Error Viewer can import this text file.

When disabled (default), the default tool name is Generic .                                                                                                                                          |

It is in YAML format.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

When disabled (default), creates markers to the overlay design.                                                                                                                                                                                           |

The valid range is 10% ≦ x ≦ 1000%（Default is 100％). If this option is turned on, but error marker data is not em_ratio attribute, then error marker ignores to filter this error marker data. |

## Hierarchy Navigator Assistant

You can use the Hierarchy Navigator assistant to navigate and work in the hierarchy, by instance or master name.

- Displaying the Hierarchy Navigator Assistant

## Displaying the Hierarchy Navigator Assistant

To display the Hierarchy Navigator in a design layout or schematic view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Hierarchy Navigator .

The Hierarchy Navigator shows the hierarchy tree structure. The root of the hierarchical tree is the top library, cell, view (LCV). Each parent node contains the names of the child instances. Instances in the design are highlighted when they are selected in the Hierarchy Navigator.

Use the heNavigatorSortOrder Tcl preference to sort instances in alphabetical order or to place the cells with no hierarchy at the bottom of the hierarchy.

## Setting Navigation by Instance

You can set navigation by instance to work with instances only.

<!-- image -->

To set navigation by instance:

1. Open the Hierarchy Navigator assistant. In a design layout or schematic view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Hierarchy Navigator .
2. In the toolbar, click Hierarchy by Instance to see the hierarchy of each occurrence of an instance in the design. The Hierarchy Navigator also specifies the individual bit index into a vector instance to descend into when navigating by instance. The selected index is displayed in a second column as shown in the following figure:

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The following information is displayed in the second column based on the instances:

- The Design Editor descends into the selected index. The column shows the index, represented in angle brackets, of any vector instance in the descend path.
- Vector instances that are not in the descend path: Shows the current default or ellipses (…) if there is no current default index.
- Other instances: Shows no information in the index. The text in the left column spans both columns.

Click the index to show an in-line combination box with all indexes of the available vector instance. It is possible to select an index with the mouse or keyboard. You can type the number of the index for the cursor to automatically scroll and select the index from the list.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

To change the descend path in the Design Editor without prompting or redecorating the window, change the selected index in the descend path. The design is redrawn if the evaluation of any text objects depends on the descend path.

You can show and change the index of a vector instance that is not in the descend path after the column is displayed. The default index for the next descend operation changes (without descending into the instance) when the index of a vector instance that is not in the descend path changes. This index serves as the default for all descend operations, including the ide::descend preference, the de::descend preference, and by double-clicking within the Hierarchy Navigator .

3. Double-click the instance to descend into the selected instance. Right-click on an instance to show the following menu:

<!-- image -->

From this menu, select the following option to perform edits:

- Edit or view the designs in the hierarchy by choosing Descend Edit or Descend Read
- Edit the instance in place by choosing Edit in Place (available when the edit and the selected view designs match).
- Zoom to the selected master by choosing Fit . If the selected master does not exist within the edit design, Fit zooms to its parent master within the edit design.
- Set a design as the view design by choosing Set View Design (available when the edit and the selected view designs match).
- Select or deselect the instance in the canvas by choosing Select in Design or Deselect in Design .

## Setting Navigation by Master

You can set navigation by master to work with master instances only.

To navigate by master:

1. Open the Hierarchy Navigator assistant. In a design layout or schematic view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Hierarchy Navigator .
2. In the toolbar, click the Hierarchy by Master

<!-- image -->

.

To display the list of masters used in the design, and their hierarchy. The Hierarchy by Master mode shows the structure of the design.

When many instances of a single master are used in a design, only one row is shown in the tree, and the instance count is shown between brackets if the master is not root.

In the design hierarchy list, right-click on a master to show the following menu:

<!-- image -->

From this menu, select the following option to perform edits:

- Open the master in the Hierarchy Editor or Design Editor option by choosing Open or Open Read Only .
- Zoom to the selected master by choosing Fit . If the selected master does not exist within the edit design, Fit zooms to its parent master within the edit design.
- Select or deselect the master in the canvas by choosing Select in Design or Deselect in Design . If the selected master does not exist within the edit design, it selects or deselects the parent master within the edit design.

The PCell submasters are not displayed as separate masters in the Hierarchy by Master display mode.

While in the Hierarchy by Master mode, you can open the design in a new editor window by double-clicking a master. However, it is not possible to change the design editor's context from the Hierarchy by Master display mode.

## Exporting Design Hierarchy

You can export the design hierarchy structure to a text file.

<!-- image -->

To export the design hierarchy:

1. Begin by opening the Hierarchy Navigator assistant. In a design layout or schematic view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Hierarchy Navigator .
2. In the toolbar, click Export Hierarchy .

<!-- image -->

This opens the Export Hierarchy dialog box.

<!-- image -->

To select the type of hierarchy structure to export use the drop-down list with Type .

In the text file with the exported hierarchy, the default delimiter between the instance names and their paths is a single space. To use any other delimiter, such as an underscore (\_), specify it in the Delimiter tab. To view the file with the exported hierarchy structure in the Text Viewer tool, select Open in Text Editor . Click OK to open the file.

## Resolving Context Issues

There are three types of context issues that can occur while working with designs.

You can use the Hierarchy Navigator to resolve the following issues.

- Invalid Contexts: If the context of the current edit or view design becomes invalid (due to change in the parent lineage), the Hierarchy Navigator prunes all the submodules of invalid instances from the tree except instances in the lineage of the current edit context.
- Out of context lineages: Instances can be pushed out-of-context while working with the design. The Hierarchy Navigator indicates the out-of-context instances by a red color font.
- Invalid Placed/Switched Masters: If the placed or switched master does not exist, the instance/master is displayed in a red color font. If the master name is visible, the placed master is displayed instead of the switched master.

<!-- image -->

To find instances in the design hierarchy:

1. Begin by opening the Hierarchy Navigator assistant. In a design layout or schematic view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Hierarchy Navigator .
2. In the toolbar, click Show Search Line , which shows or hides the Find text field.

<!-- image -->

Type an initial of the instance name you want to locate, for example:

Filtering adheres to the Find preference setting of the General Options dialog box for partial match, wildcard, regular expression, and match start. See Setting General Options.

## Showing Quick Access Menu

The Hierarchy Navigator allows you to access frequently used commands when you rightclick an instance.

To show the menu:

1. Open the Hierarchy Navigator assistant. In a design layout or schematic view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Hierarchy Navigator .
2. In the design hierarchy list, right-click on an instance to show the following menu:

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

- Open the selected instance in another window by choosing Open or Open Read Only .
- Edit the selected instance directly in the same window by choosing Edit in Place .
- Zoom to the selected instance by choosing Fit . If the selected instance does not exist within the edit design, Fit zooms to its parent instance within the edit design.
- Select or deselect the instance in the canvas by choosing Select in Design or Deselect in Design .

## Object Filter Assistant

You can use the Object Filter assistant to control the way the system responds to the selection of specific object types. The Object Filter works with schematic and symbol views.

If you are working in an area of a schematic where you cannot select a wire due to the interference of bounding boxes, you can use the Object Filter to turn off bounding box object selection, and more easily allow wire selection.

You can also use the Object Filter during area selection, for example, in situations where you might want to select a group of instances, and exclude wires, and other objects, from the selection set.

This topic describes the following:

- Opening the Object Filter Assistant
- Filtering Schematic Objects
- Filtering Symbol Objects

## Opening the Object Filter Assistant

Open the Object Filter to work with object selection settings in schematics and symbols.

To open the Object Filter:

- In the schematic or symbol, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Schematic Object Filter or Symbol Object Filter .

The assistant docks along the window edge. Undock it by clicking and dragging it.

To filter schematic objects:

2. Choose an option:

To enable or disable individual selectability for an object, click its check box.

To enable or disable selectability for all objects, click the buttons ( ) at the top. 回 回

Each design has an Object/Layer Panel. Settings you make apply immediately, and are stored in the technology database.

## Locating LPPs, Layers, and Objects

Using the Object/Layer Panel, you can use the filter box to locate LPPs, layers, and objects in the LPPs , Layers , and Objects tabs separately. The filter applies to the current tab. When switching tabs, the filter applies to the new tab.

<!-- image -->

To locate LPPs, layers, and objects:

1. Begin by opening the Object/Layer Panel assistant. In a design layout view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Object/Layer Panel .
2. In the Object/Layer Panel, click one of the following tabs:
- LPPs tab that displays the list of LPPs in the design
- Layers tab that displays the list of layers in the design
- Objects tab that displays the list of objects in the design

When switching the LPPs , Layers , and Objects tabs, the filter applies to the tab you are currently in.

3. (Optional) To view more LPPs at once, you can resize the Object/Layer Panel by adjusting its width so that the LPPs are listed in several visible columns.
4. (Optional) From the toolbar menu , make sure that the Show LPP Filter option is on.

<!-- image -->

The Object/Layer Panel shows the filter box by default. You can deselect Show LPP Filter to hide the filter.

5. In the filter box, type the full or partial text or an expression to search for the items of interest. See Using Filter Boxes for help using this filter.

When locating LPPs or layers, use a space to apply filtering to the layer name and purpose name, for example: m* dr* matches LPP metal1 drawing (which is the closest match), and other LPPs starting with layer name m and purpose dr .

When finding route related objects in a list of object types, first click the Objects tab, and then type route in the filter box.

6. With the list of components you want to use now optionally filtered, select them in the Object/Layer Panel.
7. Use the Object/Layer Panel to act on the selected components.

When you are ready to act on the selected components, see the following sections:

- Working With LPPs
- Working With Layers
- Working With Objects

## Displaying Presets

You can display or hide the Presets toolbar.

A preset is a named collection of state information in the Object/Layer Panel which can be restored en masse. A preset contains:

- Selected LPP sets and their relationship
- LPP visibility, selectability, and fill status
- Object filter visibility and selectability status

A preset can be created from the current design state using the de::createOLPPreset Tcl command. It is not possible to create one programmatically outside of manipulating the design and then capturing its state.

To display a preset status information:

1. Begin by opening the Object/Layer Panel assistant. In a design layout view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Object/Layer Panel .
2. Click the toolbar menu choose Show Presets to show the Presets toolbar at the top of the Object/Layer Panel. D

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

On the Presets toolbar, D stands for Default, and it is the default setting of LPP list (or selected LPPs) in the design that is opened. The preset number are user-saved LPP selection settings that apply globally. Click the button to add more preset number. +

<!-- image -->

3. You can set your own LPP selection settings and then right-click one of the numbered preset buttons to save the settings.

Right-clicking preset button shows a Save button to save the user-defined LPP selection settings.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

You can remove or rename an existing user-saved LPP selection settings preset by right-clicking the numbered button for the user-saved preset.

<!-- image -->

You can activate multiple presets at a time by saving multiple numbered buttons. You can merge an active preset with the current LPP settings by clicking the corresponding numbered button while pressing the Shift key. To delete or subtract this preset setting from the current LPP settings, click the corresponding numbered button while pressing the Ctrl key. You must click the least-numbered button to merge or delete.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Presets in the Object tab are saved and loaded through the application state interface defined by deOLPPresets.xml . You will be prompted to save the preset settings with the Object/Layer Panel Presets option when closing the software.

<!-- image -->

## Working With LPPs

In the LPPs tab, you can:

LPP sets are sorted alphanumerically. LPP sets with no default LPP are shown first, followed by a small separator, and then the LPP sets which have default LPPs. The LPP sets with default LPPs are sorted in mask order of the default LPPs.

- Show or hide LPPs with specified purposes

- Control the visibility and selectability of boundary objects

The LPPs tab consists of two panes. The upper pane shows the built-in LPP sets and the user-defined LPP sets. The lower pane shows the contained LPPs of a selected LPP set.

## Creating User-Defined LPP Sets

You can create your own LPP sets in the LPPs tab.

To create a user-defined LPP set:

1. Begin by opening the Object/Layer Panel assistant. In a design layout view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Object/Layer Panel .
2. Choose an existing LPP set, for example: M1 .
3. Click the LPPs tab menu and choose New Set .

The New LPP Sets dialog box appears.

4. Enter myLPPset in the Name box, and then enable the Include current LPPs option to include the currently valid LPPs; otherwise, the new LPP set is empty. In this case, the new LPP set includes the valid LPPs from the M1 set.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Other than the built-in LPP sets, current sets are listed in the Name list so that they can be replaced if needed.

5. Click Create to create the new LPP set, myLPPset .

If the LPP set already exists, the tool shows an Overwrite LPP Set dialog box to confirm overwriting it.

<!-- image -->

New user-defined LPP sets are saved to the ./synopsys\_custom/lppSets.tcl file if you choose to save the Object/Layer Panel state when exiting the Custom Compiler tool. The system automatically loads the file on next session.

<!-- image -->

You can start editing the newly created LPP set in the LPP pane if needed.

## Editing User-defined LPP Sets

You can edit user-defined LPP sets in the LPPs tab.

To edit a user-defined LPP set:

1. Begin by opening the Object/Layer Panel assistant. In a design layout view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Object/Layer Panel .
2. Choose the user-defined LPP set you want to edit, for example: myLPPset .
3. Click the LPPs tab menu and choose Edit &lt;setName&gt; .

The tool replaces &lt;setName&gt; with myLPPSet and displays its contained LPPs in a new pane.

<!-- image -->

4. Select a built-in LPP set or another user-defined LPP set, and then drag and drop the required LPPs from the selected set to myLPPset .

(Optional) To select or deselect more than one LPP set, use Ctrl-click to select or deselect each LPP individually.

(Optional) To select multiple LPPs, use Shift+click or drag-left to quickly select them.

5. Click the close button after editing. This updates the myLPPSet contents.

## Removing User-defined LPP Sets

You can remove user-defined LPP sets from the LPPs tab.

To remove a user-defined LPP set:

1. Begin by opening the Object/Layer Panel assistant. In a design layout view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Object/Layer Panel .
2. Choose the user-defined LPP set you want to remove, for example: myLPPset .
3. Click the LPPs tab menu and choose Remove &lt;setName&gt; .

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The tool replaces &lt;setName&gt; with myLPPset and displays its contained LPPs in the lower pane.

The Remove LPP Set dialog box appears.

4. Click Remove to confirm removing the selected LPP set.

## Setting the Active Layer Purpose Pair

You can set the active layer purpose pair (LPP) to make it the target for layout operations.

The active LPP is indicated by name at the top of the Object/Layer Panel. Click the arrow next to the active LPP indicator and choose from a list of the last ten active LPPs.

<!-- image -->

To set the active LPP:

1. Begin by opening the Object/Layer Panel assistant. In a design layout view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Object/Layer Panel .
2. Click the LPPs tab.

(Optional) To view more LPPs at once, you can resize the Object/Layer Panel by adjusting its width so that the LPPs are listed in several visible columns.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

3. Scroll the list to locate the LPP, or filter the list by entering characters in the Filter box. See Locating LPPs, Layers, and Objects for help locating the LPP.
4. (Optional) From the toolbar menu , make sure that Auto Redraw is enabled. This option automatically redraw the canvas objects when changes are made within the Object/Layer Panel.
5. Select the LPP by name.

<!-- image -->

This sets the active LPP and makes it visible and selectable. There is always only one active LPP.

## Note:

The active layer purpose pair (LPP) must be visible as you create objects. For more information about using active LPP on creation, see Using Active Layer Purpose Pair in the Custom Compiler Layout Editor User Guide for Creating and Editing Objects .

(Optional) To select or deselect more than one LPP, use Ctrl-click to select or deselect each LPP individually.

(Optional) To select multiple LPPs, use Shift-click or drag-left to quickly select them.

6. From the toolbar menu, choose any of the following options:
- Make Visible LPPs Selectable : Makes all currently visible LPPs selectable.
- Keep Active LPP Selectable : Makes the active LPP selectable.
- Keep Active LPP Visible : Makes the active LPP visible.

(Optional) Use Shift+right-click to make an LPP under the cursor position visible and other LPPs invisible. Next click makes the LPP invisible and other LPPs visible.

(Optional) Use Ctrl+middle-click to toggle the stipple visibility of an active LPP.

<!-- image -->

The Object/Layer Panel shows each LPP with an icon and indicates the visibility and selectability settings of each LPP as follows:

<!-- image -->

- Gray background indicates that the LPP is set to be unselectable
- LPP icon disappears if the LPP is set to be invisible (and also unselectable)

## Making LPP Sets Visible and Selectable

You can make LPP sets visible and selectable to facilitate the design process. You can also enable and disable LPP fill patterns.

By default, the PR boundary, snap boundary, and global wide alignment grids are listed in the Objects tab when you select the Design LPP set. To control the visibility and selectability of these boundary objects along with the LPPs, see Controlling the Visibility and Selectability of Boundary Objects.

To control the visibility and selectability of LPP sets:

1. Begin by opening the Object/Layer Panel assistant. In a design layout view, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Object/Layer Panel .
2. Click the LPPs tab.

(Optional) To view more LPP sets at once, you can resize the Object/Layer Panel by adjusting its width so that the LPP sets are listed in several visible columns.

<!-- image -->

3. (Optional) From the toolbar menu , make sure that Auto Redraw is enabled. This option automatically redraw the canvas after making changes.
4. Select the LPP set, either a built-in LPP set or a user-defined LPP set, you want to apply.

## Note:

The active layer purpose pair (LPP) must be visible as you create objects. For more information about using active LPP on creation, see Using Active Layer Purpose Pair in the Custom Compiler Layout Editor User Guide .

(Optional) To select or deselect more than one LPP set or LPP, use Ctrl+click to select or deselect each LPP set or LPP individually.

(Optional) To select multiple LPP sets or LPPs, use Shift+click or drag-left to quickly select them.

5. Right-click and apply the operation of your choice to the selected LPP set:
- Set the selected LPP set(s) to be visible or invisible.
- Enable or disable fill. Disabling fill ignores the fill style defined in the associated packet, and renders the packet with a color outline, but no fill pattern. This action does not change the resource definition for the packet.
- Set the selected LPP set(s) to be selectable or unselectable.
- Remove (deselect) the currently selected LPP set(s).

The Object/Layer Panel shows each LPP set with an icon constructed from the packets of the first four LPPs within the LPP set (Figure 44), and indicates the visibility and selectability settings of each LPP set as follows:

Figure 44 LPP Set Icons and Visibility/Selectability Status

<!-- image -->

- LPP Set icon depicts the packets of the first four LPPs within the LPP set whose purpose is one of these defined in the leOLPDefaultPurposeList preference. If fewer than four LPPs remain, they are repeated until the circle is complete. Fill style, outline, and fill colors are all depicted in the pie slice (Figure 44).

Full LPP Set icon indicates that all the LPPs within the LPP set are fully visible.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Partial LPP Set icon indicates that the LPP set contains invisible LPPs.

LPP Set icon disappears if all the LPPs within the LPP set are completely invisible.

- LPP sets depict the selectable state with an alternate background color.

White background indicates that all the LPPs within the LPP set are selectable.

Light gray background indicates that the LPP set contains unselectable LPPs.

Dark gray background indicates that all the LPPs within the LPP set are completely unselectable.

## Showing Abbreviations and Stream Layer Numbers

3. Hover over an LPP. The tool shows a tooltip that contains the full layer name and purpose name (abbreviated or unabbreviated), the layer and purpose numbers, and the layer and purpose descriptions.

## Controlling the Visibility and Selectability of Boundary Objects

You can sort all LPPs to easily access the ones you need frequently.

To view and select the boundary objects in the LPPs tab:

2. Click the LPPs tab.
3. When the preference is set, the Object/Layer Panel assistant lists the following objects in the LPPs tab when you select the Design LPP set:

## System LPPs

A system layer-purpose pair (LPP) is a layer-purpose pair that is owned by the system, not by the design or technology.

System LPPs have the following characteristics:

- Do not appear on the Object/Layer Panel .
- Not listed on the Layer-Purpose Pair Selector.
- Not returned by the de::getLPPs command unless you specify -includeSystem is true .
- Cannot be modified by any user interface control for layer-purpose pairs, including Set All Visible and Set All Selectable .
- Cannot be set as active using commands such as de::setActiveLPP .

To designate a layer-purpose pair as a system LPP, you need to set the system attribute on the deLPP object.

The deLPP object represents a layer purpose pair (LPP) in a design. You can use this object to modify the validity, selectability, and visibility attributes as shown in the Object/ Layer Panel . You can obtain a deLPP object using the de::getLPPs command.

<!-- image -->

## Note:

You cannot destroy a deLPP object.

For more information, see the following Tcl commands:

- de::createLPPSet

- de::getlpps

- de::setActiveLPP

## Sharing OLP Settings

By turning on the Share OLP Settings option, the Object/Layer Panel automatically synchronizes the filters of LPPs and object types between designs which share a common technology.

Design Settings are defined as an ordered list of LPPs with their validity, selectability, visibility, and fill settings, together with a set of object types with their visibility and selectability settings and the active LPP. One design setting exists for each design opened by the design editor.

<!-- image -->

Interactive commands may further restrict the selection filters by providing additional per-type, per-LPP, and per-object selection filters that are applied in addition to the design's selectability registry. Thus, before selecting an object, both the design and active interactive command's filter set must be queried. Inactive commands in the command stack do not affect the selectability.

When a design is opened, the technology may be modified. Typically this happens when an LPP is encountered in the design which does not exist within the technology. In this case, the LPP is added to the technology by the technology manager with some default settings. The Object/Layer Panel is not responsible for updating the technology but it is responsible for showing LPPs added with this method.

By default, modifications made within the Object/Layer Panel are reflected back in only the settings for the edit design. However, by turning on the Share OLP Settings option or by setting the deShareOLPSettings preference to true , these changes are automatically applied to all designs which share a common technology.

By turning off the Share OLP Settings option, you can modify multiple design settings when the designs are explicitly linked with a linked design context.

To enable synchronization to other design contexts, the linked design context must have the leSyncOLP capability applied. This capability indicates to the Object/Layer Panel that the edit design of the linked design context should be modified at the same time as the edit design is modified.

## Note:

This is a one-way synchronization.

This does not require that the two designs share the exact same technology. The Object/Layer Panel attempts to apply changes to the same-named LPPs in the opposite design and ignores any errors.

The leOLPAutoRedraw preference is supported for redrawing all affected design contexts.

When a design is opened, depending on the deShareOLPSettings preference value, the design's OLP settings are read from either another design or the design's referenced technology or the appropriate Technology Settings (if deShareOLPSettings preference value is true ). When using Design Settings and descending into a design which was not formerly open from another design with the same technology, the parent's OLP settings are copied to the newly opened design. These settings are not copied back to the parent on return, but only used as defaults for the newly opened design.

Commands that modify the selection can cause members to become desynchronized. To maintain synchronization, you must edit in group when making modifications.

## Probe Assistant

You can use the Probe assistant to view probes in the design or in a currently selected set of objects. This assistant displays probes visually through object highlighting. You can use the Probe assistant to find and cycle through probed objects, to sort the list of probed objects, and to view text details for each one.

This topic describes the following:

- Opening the Probe Assistant
- Cycling Through Probed Objects
- Deleting Probes
- Viewing Probes in Shadow
- Viewing Probed Object Details

## Opening the Probe Assistant

Open the Probe assistant to find and cycle through probes and their objects in any probed design context.

## To open the Probe assistant:

- In any design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Probe Assistant .

<!-- image -->

Probes attach to objects both when designers add them manually and when design analysis processes add them automatically.

The assistant docks along the window edge. Undock it by clicking and dragging it.

## Cycling Through Probed Objects

You can cycle through probed objects in a design to view them individually.

To cycle through probed objects:

1. Begin by opening the Probe assistant. In any design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Probe Assistant .
2. In the list of probes in the Probe assistant, select a probe by name.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The assistant browses to see the selected probe. If the Zoom option is checked in the toolbar menu, the assistant also zooms in to where it is.

3. To cycle through all probed objects in the design or selected set, click the toolbar arrows.

<!-- image -->

## Deleting Probes

You can select probes and then remove them from your design.

To delete probes from the design canvas:

1. Begin by opening the Probe assistant in the design context with probes you want to view. In any design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Probe Assistant .
2. In the list of probes in the Probe assistant, select the probe by name.
3. In the Probe assistant toolbar, click the Delete button below or press the Delete key.

<!-- image -->

## Viewing Probes in Shadow

You can view design areas in shadow for additional visual contrast between selected probes and the surrounding design.

1. To view design areas in shadow:

Click the Shadow button on the Probe assistant toolbar. Click the arrow and move the slider to increase or decrease the contrast.

<!-- image -->

2. (Optional) Set the deProbeHighlightShadow Tcl preference with the following value for probing operations:
- true : Turns on the Shadow mode to increase the contrast between the objects you are probing and the remaining objects.
- net : Turns on the Shadow mode to increase the contrast between the nets you are probing and the remaining nets.
- false : Turns off the Shadow mode.

## Viewing Probed Object Details

You can view probed object details to obtain information about object names, packet colors, and short descriptions entered when the probes were created.

To view probed object details:

1. Begin by opening the Probe assistant in the design context with probes you want to view. In any design, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Probe Assistant .
2. In the list of probes in the Probe assistant, select a probe by name.

The system browses to the design where the probed object is, and displays details about this probe. If the Zoom option is checked in the toolbar menu, the assistant also zooms to fit the object.

The Probe assistant shows the lineage path to the probed object, the tool associated with this probe (signifying how the probe was created), and the purpose, and long description, entered when this probe was created.

3. To sort by object, packet, or description, select the column titles.
4. Click the toolbar menu to see the available viewing options.

| Tools       | Filters the probe list by tool. Tcl preference: deProbeAssistantTools                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Help        | Opens the online help documentation for this topic.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

## Property Editor Assistant

You can use the Property Editor assistant to create and edit properties, parameters, and attribute values of selected objects. You can also view connection assignments, instance terminal connectivity, and attributes for colored shapes in advanced node designs.

- About the Property Editor
- Setting Editor Annotation Options
- Displaying the Property Editor
- Opening the Properties Dialog Box
- Viewing Design Object Properties
- Editing and Deleting Design Properties
- Creating New Design Properties
- Enabling Zoom Operations
- Adjusting Parameters in the Selected Set
- Resetting to Default Parameter Values
- Instance Terminal Region
- Property Editor Toolbar

## About the Property Editor

You can use the Property Editor to:

- Display the properties of selected objects.
- Edit the properties and parameters of selected objects.
- Create new properties to be associated with the selected objects.

<!-- image -->

The Property Editor consists of the following:

<!-- image -->

The contents of the Property Editor depends on the objects you select in the design. For example, if you select an instance, the properties of the instance are displayed. If you select a path segment, the properties of the path segment are displayed.

<!-- image -->

## Instance

## Path Segment

<!-- image -->

For more information, see Viewing Design Object Properties. For the descriptions of the toolbar buttons, see Property Editor Toolbar.

## Setting Editor Annotation Options

The attributes, parameters, and properties in the Property Editor can have different font colors and styles to indicate the following:

| Font Color/Style   | Description                                                                                                   |
|--------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Gray               | The value is read-only.                                                                                       |
| Italic             | The value is inherited. For example, PCell instances might have inherited values defined by the PCell master. |
| Bold               | The value was modified but not yet applied.                                                                   |

To turn on visual indicators for inherited and modified values:

1. In the design editor, choose Options &gt; General .
2. In the General Options dialog box that opens, click Editors .

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

3. In the Editor Annotations section, select the visual indicator options that you want to turn on.

| Option             | Description                                                                                 |
|--------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Modified: Bold     | Displays modified values in bold font. Tcl preference: dbPropertyEditorAnnotateModified     |
| Inherited: Italics | Displays inherited values in italic font. Tcl preference: dbPropertyEditorAnnotateInherited |
| Row Color          | Displays rows in alternating colors (white and gray). Tcl preference: dbShowParamRowColors  |

<!-- image -->

## Displaying the Property Editor

You can view the object properties using either the Property Editor or the Properties dialog box. The Property Editor and the Properties dialog box contain the same information. The main differences are:

- The Property Editor presents information in the same pane.
- The Design Properties dialog box presents information in different tabs. See Opening the Properties Dialog Box.

To display the Property Editor:

- In any design window, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Property Editor .

The Property Editor appears on the right side of the Layout Editor. You can undock it by dragging it to a different location.

Notice that the text above the Attributes section indicates the object you selected. In the following example, the text above the Attributes section indicates that a path segment is selected in the design.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Opening the Properties Dialog Box

You can view the object properties using either the Property Editor or the Properties dialog box. The Property Editor and the Properties dialog box contain the same information. The main differences are:

- The Properties dialog box presents information in different tabs in an independent dialog box.
- The Property Editor presents information in the same pane. By default, the pane appears on the right side of the Layout Editor. See Displaying the Property Editor.

To open the Properties dialog box on a one-time basis:

1. In the Layout Editor, choose Window &gt; Console .
2. In the Console pane, type the following at the prompt:

```
> de::showProperties
```

The Properties dialog box opens. Notice that the text in the title bar indicates the object you selected. In the following example, the title bar indicates that a path segment is selected in the design.

If you click Show Multiple Item View ( ), the Common text appears next to the selected objects on the title bar.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

To configure the Layout Editor so that the Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Property Editor command opens the Properties dialog box instead of the Property Editor by default:

1. Use a text editor to open the ~/.synopsys\_custom.tcl file.
2. Add the following line in the file:

gi::createBinding -event q -command de::showProperties -windowType leLayout

Instead of leLayout , you can specify seSchematic or seSymbol .

## Viewing Design Object Properties

You can view the properties of selected design objects. While viewing the properties, you can edit, delete, or create new properties. See Editing and Deleting Design Properties.

Before you start, set the editor annotations if you want visual indicators for the source or status of the property values. See Setting Editor Annotation Options.

<!-- image -->

The video demonstrates how to select multiple schematic instances and edit their attributes in the Property Editor in the Custom Compiler environment.

[To view object properties:](https://spdocs.synopsys.com/dow_retrieve/latest/training/dg/custom_compiler/CC_Edit_multiple_insts_in_PE.mp4)

1. [Begin by Displaying the Property Editor or Opening the Properties Dialog Box.](https://spdocs.synopsys.com/dow_retrieve/latest/training/dg/custom_compiler/CC_Edit_multiple_insts_in_PE.mp4)
2. Select one or more objects on the canvas. To see properties for the design itself, click anywhere on the canvas.

If you select pre-colored shapes, the Property Editor lists their color attributes and indicates whether the color is a color anchor or has been propagated from another shape.

3. In the Property Editor, review details available for the currently selected set.
- If you selected one object, information about that object is displayed. To see additional details about that object's properties (or, for example, its parameters or attributes if that information is available), expand each section.
- For some objects that are associated with layers, you can filter and search for the layer of interest.

- choose Column Visibility .
- If you selected a group of objects, you can cycle through them using the Show Previous Object and Show Next Object arrows on the assistant's toolbar. The assistant shows details for one object at a time, and simultaneously delineates the object's shape on the canvas.
- If you selected a group of objects, and you want to use tabs for quicker access to details about each one, click Show Multiple Item View ( )on the assistant's toolbar.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

If the dePropertyEditorShowCommonAllRefs Tcl preference is set to true , then the Property Editor will display the selected PMOS and NMOS instance parameters and properties in the All Instances or All Vias tab. You can make changes to these instances in the same tab instead of in different tabs.

- If you want to expand the scope of the selected set to include additional items of this object type, choose an expanded scope from the black double-arrow button menu on the assistant's toolbar.

The assistant shows the currently applied scope below the assistant toolbar, lists the number of objects in the selected set, and shows the current object's position in the set's order.

<!-- image -->

4. (Optional) Display or hide details about the selected set. To do this, click , and then

<!-- image -->

In the Column Visibility dialog box that appears, select the information you want to display in the Property Editor.

## Editing and Deleting Design Properties

Before you start, set the editor annotations if you want visual indicators for the source or status of the property values. See Setting Editor Annotation Options.

To edit and delete design properties:

1. Begin by Displaying the Property Editor or Opening the Properties Dialog Box.
2. On the canvas, select the object whose properties you want to edit or delete.

Values that are in gray text are read-only. You cannot edit them. In the following example, the Library Name, Cell Name, and View Name are read-only, so the names are gray.

<!-- image -->

If the Editor Annotation is turned on, Attributes and Parameters that are italicized are inherited values. In the following example, Inst M2 has inherited several Parameters values from its master cell, such as Spice Model, LVS Model, and so on.

<!-- image -->

3. Edit the attribute or parameter values. For assistance in showing properties, see Viewing Design Object Properties.
- To edit a value, type the value or text, select from the menu, or change the check box selection. To move to and edit the next value, press Tab. To edit parameter definitions, see Adjusting Parameters in the Selected Set.

If the Editor Annotation is turned on, after you edit the values, attributes, and parameters, the property names appear in bold font to indicate that they have been modified but not yet applied. In the following example, the LPP selection was modified and not yet applied.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

- To delete a property, select its row, right-click, and choose Remove .

The tool draws a line striking through the entry. When you apply the changes, the tool removes this listing altogether.

<!-- image -->

- To add new properties now, see Creating New Design Properties.

4. (Optional) Adjust edits before saving the final changes:
- To return all values to the default, on the Property Editor toolbar click Reset to Defaults .
- To discard the last change, move the cursor to the design window, and choose Edit &gt; Undo .
- To discard all changes, on the Property Editor toolbar click Discard Changes .
5. Click Apply Changes ( ) when you are done.

The tool validates the entries, and reports any errors it finds, by outlining the text boxes with a red border. Move the cursor over an invalid entry to see a tool tip for correcting the error. Adjust entries to create a valid property.

6. (Optional) Discard these applied changes by moving the cursor to the design window, and choosing Edit &gt; Undo .

## Creating New Design Properties

You can create new design properties to automatically associate them with objects in a selected set.

To create a new design property:

1. Begin by Displaying the Property Editor or Opening the Properties Dialog Box.
2. In the Property Editor, expand the Properties region of the assistant using the small arrow button.
3. Create the property.
- To create only one property, and its value, single-click the Click-to-Add text box. Enter the name and the value. Click the Apply Changes button (a green check mark ) at the top of the assistant.

<!-- image -->

This completes the procedure to create a property.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

- To create a property with additional details, double-click the Click-to-Add text box, which opens a dialog box. (Alternatively, you can right-click this text box, and choose Add to open the same dialog box).
4. Define the property you are creating as described in Table 90.

<!-- image -->

Table 90 Create Property

| Definition   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Name         | Name for this new property that does not conflict with an existing property name                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Type         | One of these property types: application, Boolean, double, enumeration, float, hierarchical, integer, string, or time                                                                                                                                        |
| Visibility   | Choose On to show this property in the Property Editor.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Value        | Initial value for this property. You can edit values later. (See Editing and Deleting Design Properties).                                                                                                                                                    |
| Range        | For double, float, integer, and time property types, optionally set a range by choosing the range option, and defining the minimum and maximum values for the range. For the enumeration property type, optionally set a range by entering a list of values. |

## 5. Click OK .

The tool validates the entries, and reports any errors it finds, by outlining the text boxes with a red border. Move the cursor over the invalid entry to see a tool tip for correcting the error. Adjust entries to create a valid property.

## Enabling Zoom Operations

You can enable zoom operations to conveniently scale the selected set.

To enable zoom operations:

1. Begin by Displaying the Property Editor or Opening the Properties Dialog Box.
2. From the Property Editor toolbar menu, choose the Zoom option.

<!-- image -->

For zoom operation details, see Zooming.

3. (Optional) Cycle through the selected set.

The tool zooms to magnify each object.

For more information about viewing properties in the design, see Viewing Design Object Properties.

4. (Optional) Disable automatic zooming by deselecting the Zoom option in the Property Editor toolbar menu.

## Adjusting Parameters in the Selected Set

You can navigate from the Property Editor assistant to the Parameter Editor and adjust parameters for the currently selected set.

To adjust parameters in the currently selected set:

1. Begin by Displaying the Property Editor or Opening the Properties Dialog Box.
2. In the design, select one or more objects.
3. From the Property Editor toolbar menu, choose Parameter Definitions .

The Parameter Definition Editor opens.

For more information, see Parameter Definition Editor Tool.

<!-- image -->

## Resetting to Default Parameter Values

To reset the parameters to their default values:

- On the Property Editor toolbar, click Reset to Defaults .

<!-- image -->

You can customize Reset to Defaults so that specific parameters do not revert to their default values. Use the following CDF parameter to specify the parameters that should not be reverted when resetting to default values in the Property Editor:

| CDF Parameter         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| dbResetParamsToIgnore | (String) List of parameters that should not revert to their default values, but their callback procedures will run after the reset operation. The order of the callback is determined by the order the parameters appear in the list. |

The default values for vias and multi-part paths (MPPs) are from the StdViaDef and leMPP definitions, respectively and not from any corresponding CDF parameter default. The default values for instances and custom vias are from the CDF parameters first, and if no such parameter exists then the default is obtained from the OA database (SuperMaster oaParamArray).

## Instance Terminal Region

The Instance Terminal editing region has a table for editing (layouts only) and viewing the instance terminals of an instance. The default configuration only presents the only the Term Name and Net Name columns. Additionally, only for layouts, the default configuration also presents the Current column. A context-sensitive menu allows hiding and showing the Term Name, Net Name, Term Type, Anchor , and Current columns for instance terminals

| Column    | Description                                                            |
|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Term Name | Displays the instance terminal names.                                  |
| Net Name  | Displays the name of the net connected to the named instance terminal. |
| Term Type | Displays the terminal type.                                            |

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Column   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Anchor   | (Layout only) Displays the anchor value, which associated with instance terminal. If there is no associated net with a terminal, this column with check box is visible, empty, and dimmed. Only when a net is entered in the Net Name column, the check box in the Anchor column becomes editable. |
| Current  | (Layout only) Displays the Average DC , Average AC , Peak , and AC RMS as the four sub columns of the Current column with each cell having the same behavior as the Current widget's cells.                                                                                                        |

4. Select the objects in the table.

.

## About the Track Pattern Assistant

You can use the Track Pattern assistant to enable correct-by-construction layout design for advanced process nodes, such as those containing FinFETs. Using track patterns can reduce design time.

When you design with active track patterns, objects snap to the nearest track during create, copy, move, and stretch operations. In addition, the Layout Editor displays only relevant candidate tracks as you create, copy, move, or stretch objects, even if Visibility is turned off for those tracks.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

You need to define track patterns before you can use the Track Pattern assistant to apply them. A track pattern definition is a set of horizontal or vertical tracks that indicate available routing resources, that is, both the positions and the number of routing tracks.

To define track patterns for your designs, you can use one of the following methods:

- Use the Track Pattern assistant.

See Creating and Editing Track Pattern Definitions.

- Add track pattern definitions directly to the technology file.

See the section about trackPatternDefs in the Custom Compiler Technology File and Display Resource Reference Manual .

To import an updated technology file after adding track pattern definitions, see Importing Technology Data.

Contact your Synopsys Support representative for additional assistance.

- Use Tcl to add track pattern definitions.

See the section covering the le::createTrackPatternDef command in the Custom Compiler Tcl Reference Manual .

Contact your Synopsys Support representative for additional assistance.

## Displaying the Track Pattern Assistant

To display the Track Pattern assistant:

- In the Layout Editor window, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Track Pattern Assistant . The Track Pattern assistant pane appears on the left side of the window. You can undock the pane by dragging it to a required location.

The Track Pattern assistant shows a list of track patterns for the current design, in alphabetical order by associated layer name, preferred sub-node direction (vertical or horizontal), visibility, and active state. If a layer does not have an associated track pattern, the system does not list the layer.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Viewing Track Patterns

You can view track patterns that are set up and defined for your designs. You can set them to be visible or invisible, and active or inactive, either individually or all at once. In addition, if your design's technology contains mask color definitions, you have the option of displaying the track patterns' assigned colors.

To view track patterns:

1. In a design layout, display the Track Pattern assistant. In the Layout Editor window, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Track Pattern Assistant .
2. To limit the list of tracks displayed in the Track Pattern assistant, type characters in the Filter box. Any name that matches the characters you typed will be displayed.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

If the Filter box is not displayed, click , and then choose Show Filter .

3. To show individual track patterns, select Visibility for those track patterns. To hide the track patterns, clear the Visibility check box.

## Note:

The Layout Editor displays relevant candidate tracks as you create, copy, move, or stretch objects, even if Visibility is turned off for those tracks. To turn off the automatic display of candidate tracks, set the leDisplayInCommandTrackPatterns Tcl preference to false .

<!-- image -->

In the following example, the m2 layer vertical red tracks are set to be displayed on the canvas. Note that the tracks' assigned color is not displayed.

<!-- image -->

4. To display a track pattern's assigned color, on the Track Pattern toolbar, click Toggle track color rendering . The tracks' assigned color displays. (To display the assigned color, the track pattern must be visible. See step 3).

In the following example, Toggle track color rendering is turned on for the m2 layer vertical red tracks. Notice that the tracks are colored Red.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

5. To show or hide all track patterns in the list, click one of the following Track Pattern toolbar buttons, respectively: .
6. To make a track pattern active, select Activity . To make a track pattern inactive, clear the Activity check box. +

## Caution:

## Renaming and Deleting Track Patterns

You can rename existing track patterns. You can also delete track patterns from the set available for this design.

To rename or delete track patterns:

1. Open the Track Pattern assistant. In the Layout Editor window, choose Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Track Pattern Assistant .
2. From the list of track patterns, select one by name.

Choosing Edit &gt; Undo reverses either of these operations.

## [About Track Regions](https://solvnet.synopsys.com/dow_retrieve/latest/kb/custom_compiler/videos/CC_Track_Region_Assistant.mp4)

Tracks ensure that interconnects and routes in advanced node designs, such as those containing FinFETs, are properly placed and correct by construction. You can create multiple track regions to accommodate different requirements within the same design. Each track region consists of one or more tiles. Each tile consists of a set of tracks.

<!-- image -->

A complete region consists of an integer number of tiles. An incomplete region consists of one or more incomplete tiles. In the following example, the incomplete region has an incomplete tile in the Y direction (tile 1 is incomplete in the Y direction).

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Within a region, you can specify that alternating tiles flip along the X or Y direction. In the following example, the second tile is flipped vertically (in the Y direction).

<!-- image -->

## Note:

If you create track regions, the Layout Editor will ignore existing track patterns in the design.

<!-- image -->

When you design with active track regions, shapes and objects snap to the nearest track during create, copy, move, and stretch operations. In addition, the Layout Editor displays only relevant candidate tracks as you place interconnects and routes, even if Visibility is turned off for those tracks. 60

## Grouping Track Grids and Grid Groups

You can group track grids and grid groups that share the same color and width to a single track group.

Using this option, you can:

- Define grids with the same color and width in grids()
- Define tracks with the same color and width in tracks()
- Group those tracks in a single group in groups()

This group applies to a single trackGroup , and all tracks/grids in the group share the specified color and width.

<!-- image -->

This approach allows you to logically group together tracks (and their associated grids) that have matching visual and physical properties, and have them apply to a single trackGroup .

In the TRA, the track grids are displayed as separate rows at the same level as group definitions. Grid groups appear at the same level as individual grids and use the same icon. Grid groups are expandable; expanding a grid group displays its underlying grids, which can be managed together. In the TRA, grid groups are positioned between group definitions and individual grids.

## Exclusive Track Grids

In the TRA, for exclusive track grids, only one grid can be active or visible at a time.

<!-- image -->

Figure 52 Exclusive Track Grids

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

When you enable one grid, all other grids in the exclusive group are automatically disabled.

The active and visible states are managed separately and operate independently.

When you open a design or create a region, the active and visible states of exclusive grids are initialized based on their definitions. The exclusivity logic is enforced only when you change grid states using the TRA. If you change the visible or active state of a grid using Tcl commands, it does not affect the states of other grids in the same exclusive group.

## Hidden Tracks and Group Definitions

An object is not displayed in the TRA if the hidden attribute of a track or group definition is set to true, which cannot be controlled from the assistant. The Set all tracks visible/active command does not affect hidden objects.

You can access these objects using the Tcl commands.

## Before You Start

Some required and optional tasks should be completed before you start to create and edit track regions in the Track Region Assistant.

Make sure that the technology database has one or more track region definitions specified in the trackDefs Layer Rules section. For information about modifying the technology database, see the Custom Compiler Technology and Display Resource File Reference Manual.

The track region definitions that are available for global and local track region creation are filtered by the leTrackRegionAllowedDefNames Tcl preference. If you do not see the definition when creating track regions, check the Tcl preference setting.

If you defined grids to specify permissible starting (low) and ending (high) locations for interconnects and routes, you can optionally set the leTrackRegionAssistantShowTrackGrids Tcl preference to show (true) or hide (false) the grid information in the Track Region Assistant. To change how the grids are displayed on the layout canvas (line or arrow), set the leRenderTrackGridsMethod Tcl preference. When leRenderTrackGridsMethod is line , you can specify the line style, such as the color or thickness, by editing the trackGridLines display packet. See Creating and Editing Display Packets and Packet Aliases.

If you want to use design- or project-based preset track regions instead of track regions defined in the PDK or foundry technology, see Defining Track Presets.

## Defining Track Presets

Some designs or projects require that you use tracks from different track regions. To address the requirement, you can define a group of tracks (track presets) that are in different track regions. Doing so lets you access and use the tracks in the different regions without having to enable each region individually.

To define a track preset:

1. Create a preset file named deTRAPresets.txt. The file should be in the ASCII format and should contain the following information for each track preset:

```
presetName1 { {regionDef1/grouDef1/track1 <visibleState> <activeState>} .... {regionDefN/grouDefN/trackN1 <visibleState> <activeState>} }
```

## For example:

```
preset1 { {r1/g1/t1 0 1}
```

<!-- image -->

```
{r1/g1/t2 1 0} {r1/g2/t1 1 1} {r3/g2/t2 0 0} } preset2 { {r1/*        true   false} {r2/*/t2     false  1} {r3/g4/t2    1      1} }
```

2. Set the leTrackPresetsFilePath Tcl preference to specify the path to the preset file. The default value is:
3. (Optional) Set the leTrackDefaultSet Tcl preference to specify the default preset, the preset that is applied when the design is opened.
4. (Optional) To select a non-default track preset, open the Track Region Assistant and select from the Preset list.

```
$SYNOPSYS_CUSTOM_LOCAL/deTRAPresets.txt
```

<!-- image -->

Alternatively, select the preset from the Layout Editor Advanced toolbar.

<!-- image -->

## Creating Track Region PCells

A track region PCell is an editable PCell that contains a set of track tiles. See About Track Region PCells.

You can create track region PCells using one of the following methods:

- Create &gt; Rectangle command, which requires that you use the Object/Layer Panel to select a track boundary LPP, such as the system-reserved border track LPP.
- Track Region Assistant Create Region PCell command, which automatically detects and uses the available track boundary LPPs.

This topic describes how to use the Track Region Assistant Create Region PCell command. For instructions on using the Create &gt; Rectangle command, see Creating and Editing Track Region PCells.

To create a new track region PCell using presets, see Defining Track Presets and Creating Track Region PCells Using Presets.

To use the Track Region Assistant to create track region PCells:

1. (To use presets) In the Track Region Assistant, click , and choose Track Presets .
2. In the Track Region Assistant, click , and choose Create Region PCell .

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Note:

The names appear in the Preset list so that you can reuse the track region PCell definitions later. See Creating Track Region PCells Using Presets.

4. Click Edit Tracks . The Edit Tracks dialog box appears.

At the top of the dialog box are general options that apply to the entire track region PCell. Below the general parameters are tabs that contain data for tracks. Each tab represents a track group. Within each tab are data for individual tracks.

| Draw Shape   | Draws physical shapes inside the PCell master to represent the tracks. Tcl Preference: leTrackPcellDrawShape                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

The set of tracks have the same track width and spacing. In the example shown, one row (or one track definition) results in the set of four uniform tracks in the tile. In the non-uniform mode, each row in a tab defines a single track. In the example shown, three rows in the same tab results in three tracks with different widths and spacing. |-----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

If the preference is set to false , the track operates like a default track, and wires of any width can route on the tracks. When the preference is set to true , only wires with non-default-rule nets can route on the tracks, and the wires must match the width of the reserved tracks.
