## Controlling Library Availability

You can control the libraries that are availability for design sessions. You can specify availability for libraries created using the Custom Compiler environment, and you can adjust availability for libraries whose data was imported.

To control library availability, use library definition files ( lib.defs ).

This section describes the following for controlling availability for reference libraries used by integrated tools.

- Specifying Library Availability
- Combining Libraries
- Hiding Libraries
- Loading Libraries Automatically

## Specifying Library Availability

Specify general library availability by editing the library definition file. You can use this file to add, change, and remove library availability.

You can use the library definition file to directly define paths to libraries. Additionally, you can also use it to indirectly define paths by including references to additional library definition files.

## After

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The default version of this file is named lib.defs . However, different names are allowed. (To specify a library definition file with a different name at session start, use the -libDefsFile command line option, and the filePath to the library location).

To edit a library definition file:

1. Display the Library Definitions Editor. See Editing Library Definitions.
2. Edit the file using valid definition statements in Table 101. For editing instructions, see Editing Library Definitions.

Table 101 Library Definition File Statements

| Statement                                                    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|--------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| ASSIGN <library_name> <attribute_name> <attribute_value>     | Assigns one of the following attributes such as libMode or dbOverlayPath to a listed library. For example, create an overlay CDF (Component Description Format) using a statement such as: ASSIGN libName dbOverlayPath overlay/path                                                                             |
| DEFINE <library_logical_name_or_label> <path_to_the_library> | Defines a library, and its library path. The library's logical name is in the Linux name space, therefore, it might appear differently in the Cdba name space that the Custom Compiler environment uses to display the name. The path is not name-mapped, and appears just as it would in a Linux shell command. |
| INCLUDE <path_to_library_definition_ file>                   | Includes in this library definition file the libraries listed in another library definition file. Add this statement for each library definition file whose library definitions you want to include. When this statement is used, and the file is not found, the system generates an error.                      |
| SOFTINCLUDE <path_to_the_included_file>                      | Adds other library definitions. When this statement is used, and the file is not found, the system ignores it.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| UNASSIGN <libraryName> <attribute_name>                      | Removes this attribute.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| UNDEFINE <libraryName>                                       | Removes a previously defined library.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

## Note:

The SOFTINCLUDE , UNASSIGN , and UNDEFINE statements are Synopsys extensions to the OpenAccess standard library definition syntax. Files that use these statements are not guaranteed to work with non-Synopsys OpenAccess based tools when they are run outside of this environment. When translators and integrated tools run from within the Custom Compiler environment, the system uses a temporary copy of the library definition file that replaces these statements.

<!-- image -->

When library names include characters other than letters and numbers, note that these can appear differently in the definition file and the Library Manager. This is due to name mapping, which enables these names to be recognized by multiple environment features. When this occurs, use the Library Manager to both create the library and automatically add its access instead of adding access manually.

3. Save the file.

## Combining Libraries

To combine the contents of two or more libraries, use the COMBINE attribute with the ASSIGN command. In the following example, the contents of libA and libB are listed under libC in the Library Manager. The instances still belong to their original libraries.

ASSIGN libC COMBINE libA libB

The following limitations apply to the COMBINE attribute:

- You cannot use the attribute with Fusion Compiler or IC Compiler II libraries.
- If a cell exists in more than one of the libraries, the cell listed in the combined library represents only the first occurrence of this cell.
- The Copy &gt; Cell and Move &gt; Cell commands do not permit groups of cells in different physical libraries.
- A cell that is copied into a combined library will be placed in the top-level library ( libC in the example shown).
- You cannot copy or move cells in libraries that are members of the combined library.

## Hiding Libraries

After you combine libraries, you might want to hide the libraries so that the cells do not appear in more than one place in the Library Manager.

To hide libraries such that they do not appear in the Library Manager, use the INVISIBLE attribute with the ASSIGN command. The following example hides mylib so that it does not appear in the Library Manager:

ASSIGN mylib INVISIBLE

## Loading Libraries Automatically

Libraries can have an autoload file to automatically load the libraries at startup. You can also disable the autoload file before sourcing a particular library by assigning the loadAutoLoadFile attribute to false . To disable loading of the autoload file for a library defined in the lib.defs file:

ASSIGN &lt;libName&gt; loadAutoLoadFile false

## Note:

The attribute only affects one library and not its hierarchy. If you need to disable autoLoad.file for its technology library too, then each library must have a separate ASSIGN statement.

## Compressing and Uncompressing Libraries

The Library Manager tool uses the oaZip method to compress libraries. This type of compressing the libraries allows you to save the disk space and to view or edit designs in the compressed library.

## Note:

Supports compressing of OpenAccess filesys (oaDMFileSys) and OpenAccess turbo (oaDMTurbo) libraries only and does not support compressing of NDM and IC Compiler libraries.

The Edit Library Compression dialog box allows you to compress, uncompress, or check the current compression state of a library.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

To compress or uncompress the library:

- In the Edit Library Compression dialog box,
- Select the Enable Compression check box and click either OK or Apply to compress the selected library.
- Do not select the Enable Compression check box and click either OK or Apply to uncompress the selected library.
- Click the Check button to check the current compression state of the selected library. The Check button is independent from the Enable Compression check box selection.

## Defining Compression Level

You can define the compression level to compress the library with the dmLibraryCompressionLevel preference. The default is 1 . Valid values are 1-9.

You can compress the library using the Edit Library Compression action under the Library CSM and Edit menu. The action is enabled only if a library is selected.

## Preparing Libraries for Compressing

While preparing the library for compressing, various dialog boxes might appear. This helps you to take action, if needed, when prompted. Listing a few checks that occur while preparing for compressing, and you might not see all of them based on your environment:

- Designs in read mode are closed without notification.
- Checking for the locked libraries using the library lock.

<!-- image -->

If the library is locked, the Compress Library dialog box appears for 5 seconds. Then, interrupts the compression process if the library is not unlocked in the other session.

- Checking data.dm file for the lock state.
- Checking for locks in all cellviews under the library.
- Checking the file permissions for data.dm and cellviews.

If the library is managed by a version control system and has checked in data.dm or any cellviews, it performs necessary checks. If anything should be checked out for compressing the library, the Check Out Library dialog box appears.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Click the Check Out button to check out the data.dm file of the library, which also checks out all the checked in cellviews in the library. If check out process fails, the library is not compressed. If you click Cancel , the compression operation is not performed.

- Checking for open designs and prompts to save and close.

<!-- image -->

If the library contains open designs, the Close Designs dialog box appears. If you click Cancel Uncompress , compressing of the library is interrupted.

- Compressing and uncompressing the library. The following dialog boxes appear to show the progress.

## Modifying Component Description Format (CDF) Overlays

You can use the library definition file ( lib.def file) to modify PDK CDF definitions and netlisting behavior for a library without changing the original or base PDK. This method might be useful when the library is read-only (for example, foundry supplied PDKs) or if you do not want to directly modify the library.

To modify CDF overlays, add ASSIGN statements with the following attribute or keyword in the lib.def file:

| ASSIGN Attribute or Keyword   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|-------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| dbOverlayPath                 | Attribute that specifies one or more CDF overlays. When specifying more than one CDF overlay: • Add quotation marks to enclose the overlay names. • Use space delimiters. The modifications are applied based on the order in which the overlay names are specified. The last overlay listed has the highest priority and is the default. Parameter reordering is based on the overlay with the highest priority. If that overlay does not contain all the parameters, the parameter reorder information in the base overlay is used. |
| dbOverlayPath:append          | Keyword for appending to existing overlays.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

The Custom Compiler tool automatically synchronizes the CDF overlay modifications with the Parameter Definition Editor and saves the changes to the overlay library.

The library does not need to exist. If the specified path does not exist, the library is automatically created.

## Example of modifying a single CDF overlay:

ASSIGN foundryPDK dbOverlayPath ./path/to/foundryPDKOverlay

<!-- image -->

## Example of modifying a multiple CDF overlays:

ASSIGN myLib dbOverlayPath "myLibOverlay3 myLibOverlay2 myLibOverlay1"

In the multiple CDF overlay example, myLibOverlay1 has the highest priority, and myLibOverlay3 has the lowest priority.

For information on how to view multiple overlays and edit the parameters in Parameter Definition Editor, see Viewing CDF Overlay Parameters and Editing CDF Overlay Parameters.

## Managing Individual Libraries

You can manage individual libraries by copying, moving, and deleting them. After making changes, update library name references to allow recognition of changes from referenced libraries.

This topic describes the following:

- Copying Libraries
- Moving Libraries
- Deleting Libraries
- Updating Library Name References
- Updating Library References

## Copying Libraries

You can copy a library to create a new library with identical contents.

To copy a library:

1. In the Library Manager, specify the library to copy using one of these methods:
- From the Libraries list, select the library name, right-click, and choose Copy .
- From the Edit menu, choose Copy &gt; Library , and filter the list to select the library.
- Make sure the library name is selected in the Libraries list. From the Toolbar , click Copy .

<!-- image -->

The Copy Library dialog box opens.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

2. In the Source section, choose the source library to copy. Filter the list to specify the source library or directly select the library name.
3. In the Destination section:
- a. Type the Name to assign to the copied library.
- b. Specify the Directory of the copied library. Accept the default, or browse to select a directory.

<!-- image -->

- c. Select Cache pcells from the destination library to save evaluated PCells in a cache directory for use in later sessions. If you choose this option, browse to select the Cache Directory location.
- d. Select Overlay the destination library to specify that an overlay directory can be used to overlay CDF parameters for cells in the destination library. If you choose this option, accept the default, or browse to select an Overlay Directory .

## 4. In the Options section:

- Select Update References to update the designs in the copied library so that all design references to copied cellviews point to the new location. You can specify the scope of the updates: Copied Library or All Writable Libraries . See Updating Library Name References to modify external references. See also Updating Library References.
- Select Skip Updates for Pcell Instances to skip PCell evaluation after the update process.

Because PCell evaluation is a time-consuming operation, you can use this option to skip it, especially for hierarchical copy operations. If you skip the evaluation, the PCells might not be displayed correctly when you first open the designs.

- Select Copy Hierarchical References to copy the hierarchy underneath each cell in the library by descending the hierarchy, and copying the master of each instance.

To control where the descent stops, enter a list of library names in the Exclude Libraries text box. (Descent stops at a reference to any cellview within any of these libraries). To facilitate data entry, click Exclude All But Source Library , and keep or the list that populates the text box.

To copy only certain views, enter them in the Views text box. To exclude the specified view, select Exclude .

To copy cellview based on the view type name, select the cellview view type name from the View Types list. T o exclude the specified cell view type name, select Exclude . The default is Select All . The view type filtering applies to the copied library and to the cellview references from the copied hierarchy.

<!-- image -->

- Select Rename All Cells to use new names for the copied cells in the library. Specify the new name for the cells in the box.

<!-- image -->

You can use name patterns to rename the cells in the library. The name patterns you can use include %L (original library name), %C (original cell name), %N (a unique number in the system), and %% (the % character).

For example, %C\_a uses the original cell name ( %C ) and adds the \_a suffix.

## 5. Click OK .

If the source library contains a technology database, the copy also receives it. If the source library points to an external technology library, the copy points to the same technology library, and the system generates this notice: &lt;library name&gt; references an external technology file that exists in &lt;library name&gt; .

If conflicts occur, the Cell Conflicts dialog box opens and lets you decide how to resolve the conflicts.

## See Also

- Managing Duplicate Name Conflicts
- Copying Library, Cell, and Cellview Names
- Copying Library, Cell, and Cellview Paths

## Moving Libraries

You can move a library to a different location to provide a different point of access to its contents.

To move a library:

1. In the Library Manager, specify the library to move using one of these methods:
- From the Libraries list, select the library name, right-click the mouse, and choose Move .
- From the Edit menu, choose Move &gt; Library , and filter the list to select the library.
- Make sure the library name is selected in the Libraries list. From the Toolbar , click the Move button.

2. In the Move Library dialog box that opens, specify the following settings:

<!-- image -->

## Settings Description

Source The source library to move. Filter the list to specify the source library or directly select the library name.

Destination Name The name for the moved library. This is a required field.

To use the original library name, type %L. You can add prefixes and suffixes to the original library name. For example, to add a suffix to the original library name, type %L\_&lt;suffix&gt; .

Directory The directory to contain the moved library. Accept or browse to select a directory.

Cache pcells from the destination library saves evaluated PCells in a cache directory for use in later sessions. If you choose this option, browse to select the Cache Directory location. This option is not available for Fusion Compiler or IC Compiler libraries.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Settings   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|            | Overlay the destination library overlays the destination library with the contents of the source library. If you choose this option, accept or browse to select an Overlay Directory .                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Options    | ◦ Update References : Updates the designs in the moved library so that all design references to moved cellViews point to the new location. Only the references within the moved library are updated. External references from other libraries are not modified. See Updating Library Name References to modify external references. See also Updating Library References. ◦ Skip Updates for PCell Instances : Does not update PCell instances during the move process. ◦ Rename All Cells : Renames the moved cells to the specified name. You can add prefixes and suffixes to the original cell names. For example, to add a prefix to the original cell name, type <prefix>_%C . Copy Hierarchical References copies the hierarchy underneath each cell in the library by descending the hierarchy and copying the master of each instance. To control where descent stops, enter a list of library names in the Exclude Libraries text box. (Descent will stop at a reference to any cellView within any of these libraries). To copy only certain views, enter them in the Include Views text box. |

## 3. Click OK .

If you have open designs with unsaved modifications in the source library, the system prompts you to save those designs. After you save the designs, the system closes any designs that remain open in the source library.

## Deleting Libraries

You can delete a library to completely remove it from the disk. The operation also removes the library listing from the library definition file.

To delete Fusion Compiler libraries, see Deleting Fusion Compiler Libraries. To delete IC Compiler II libraries, see Deleting IC Compiler II Libraries.

## Caution:

You cannot undo this operation.

To delete a library:

1. In the Library Manager, from the Libraries list, select the library.
2. Delete the selected library using one of these methods.

- Right-click the mouse, and choose Delete .
- From the Edit menu, choose Delete .
- Make sure the library name is selected in the Libraries list. From the Toolbar , click Delete .
3. Click Delete to complete the operation.

## Updating Library Name References

You can update library name references to change all the references from a library to name a different library. This is useful after you replace or rename a library.

Copying or moving libraries updates internal references for designs. However, the system does not update external references. External references are those that are in other libraries. This operation updates these external references.

To update library name references:

1. In the Library Manager, choose Edit &gt; Update Library Name .
2. Enter the name of the old library whose references should be replaced.
3. From the list, choose the new library to supply new references.
4. Select any additional libraries to search to find additional references to change.
5. Click Update .

This update process updates instances in OpenAccess designs whose master has the old library name, and also updates custom vias in a technology database that is local to a searched library. Where the master of the custom via uses the old library name, it also updates the reference to use the technology database in the old library.

## Updating Library References

After you rename, replace, or move a library, you can update references to the library so that associations remain intact.

Use one of the following methods to update the library reference:

- Select the Update References option when you are in the Copy Library or Move Library dialog box. For information, see Copying Libraries and Moving Libraries.
- Choose Edit &gt; Update References command in the Library Manager. The command lets you update references without having to copy or move the library. You can also set up multiple reference library updates, and then run the multiple updates simultaneously.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

To update the library reference using the Edit &gt; Update References command:

1. In the Library Manager, choose Edit &gt; Update References . The Find and Update References dialog box opens.
2. In the Designs to Update section:
- a. Choose one or more libraries from the Library list. You can further filter the set of designs by specifying the Cell , View , and view Type .
- b. Select Search Mutual References if you want to include only reference libraries that are common among the selected designs.

<!-- image -->

Tcl preference: dmSearchMutualReferences

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

- c. Click Search .
3. In the Existing and New Reference section, choose a New reference library to replace the Existing reference library.

As soon as you choose a new reference library, the change appears in the Change List section. This allows you to review the changes you set up before you update the reference. Any new change you make to the same design library reference replaces the existing change in the Change List .

You can further filter the references to be updated by specifying the Cell and View .

4. Select Update only to existing designs to update the library reference only if the same names exist in the new library. If the names do not exist in the new library, the cells will retain their original references.

Tcl preference: dmUpdateOnlyToExisting

5. Repeat steps 3 through 4 to specify additional library reference changes.

For each design library, you can set up multiple reference library changes, and then update all of them simultaneously.

6. In the Change List section, review all the changes you have set up so far.

If necessary, you can correct updated references. To do this, in the New column, select the new reference library. The Update command will apply the newly assigned reference instead.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

To skip a change, select the blank line in the New column.

<!-- image -->

To start over, click Clear Changes to remove all changes from the Change List and Existing and New Reference sections. The original search results are retained.

7. Repeat steps 2 through 6 to change the references of other design libraries.

All the changes you set up are displayed in the Change List section. You can review them, and then update them all simultaneously.

8. Click Update . The update operation starts.

If there are open designs, the Save Designs dialog box appears. Like other Library Manager operations (copy and move), related designs that are open in the read mode are closed implicitly before the update operation starts.

9. When you are finished, click Cancel to return to the Library Manager.

## Managing Cells

You can manage cells by creating, copying, moving, and deleting them.

This topic describes the following:

- Creating New Cells
- Creating New and Reusing Cell Hierarchies
- Copying a Hierarchy of Cells
- Moving Cells

- Deleting Cells
- Enabling Rotation and Scaling

## Creating New Cells

You can create a cell in a library to define a logically separate component or device in a design. Creating a cell creates a cell container within the given library. A single cell describes an individual building block of a chip or system.

Use the Library Manager to create cells.

## To create a cell:

1. In the Library Manager, start to create the cell using one of these methods.
- From any location in the Cells list, right-click the mouse, and choose New .
- From the File menu, choose New &gt; Cell .
2. In the New Cell dialog box that opens:
- Confirm that the selected library is the correct target library to hold this cell, or select a different library.
- Select an existing cell on which to base the new cell.
- Specify a cell name by editing the name shown or by entering a new name.

If you specify the exact name of an existing cell, this operation deletes the contents of the existing cell, and creates an empty cell. Additionally, if there are any open designs in that cell, the tool closes them.

<!-- image -->

3. (Optional) To add the new cell to a category as you create it, choose from the Cell Categories list.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

4. When you are finished, click Apply to create the new cell in the destination library.
5. Click OK to close the dialog box.

## Creating New and Reusing Cell Hierarchies

You can copy an existing hierarchy of cells, and rename the copy to create a new hierarchy of cells.

You can use the Edit &gt; Copy &gt; Unique command to:

- Create a copy of a target cell (or leaf cell) and all cells that reference it.
- Rename the copied leaf cell and all cells that reference it so that they can be modified without affecting the originals.
- Retain references to all other cells in the original hierarchy, thus reducing the number of duplication cells in the system.

In the following example, the target cell and the top cell are identified for the Copy &gt; Unique operation. During the copy operation, the Top cell, target cell, and all cells that reference the target cell are copied and renamed so that they can be modified without affecting the originals. References to all other cells in the original hierarchy are retained.

If you were to open the original Top cell, you will see the original target cell, and all the original cells that reference the target cell. If you were to open the Top\_new cell, you will see targ\_new, blkb\_new, and blkc\_new. You will also see blka, blkb, blkc, and the other cells that were not copied.

<!-- image -->

If you want to duplicate the entire cell hierarchy, use the Edit &gt; Copy &gt; Cell command. See Copying a Hierarchy of Cells.

## To create new and reuse cell hierarchies:

1. In the Library Manager, choose Edit &gt; Copy &gt; Unique . The Copy Unique dialog box opens.
2. In the Top of the Design Hierarchy to Uniquify area, specify the top-level cell you want to copy by choosing the Library , Cell , and View .
3. In the Leaf Cell to Uniquify area, specify the referenced cell in the hierarchy that you want to copy by choosing the Library , Cell , and View of the referenced cell.
4. In the Copy Destination area, set the following:

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Setting         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|-----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Destination Lib | The target library that will contain all the renamed cells in the uniquified hierarchy.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Rename Pattern  | The prefix or suffix to append to the existing cell name. %C is the existing cell name. To append a suffix to the existing cell's name, type %C_<suffix> . For example, suppose the existing cell name is MyCell. If you type %C_copy1 in the Rename Pattern box, the top cell and all leaf cell names will have the _copy1 suffix. |

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Setting   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Overwrite | The option to overwrite existing cell copies if name conflicts are encountered during the copy operation. Clear the check box if you want to skip the copy operation when a conflict is encountered. |

5. When you are finished, click OK to create the copy and close the Copy Unique dialog box.

## Copying a Hierarchy of Cells

You can copy a cell and its hierarchy to create a duplicate version of it. You can copy cells from one library to another with or without changing their names. You use the Library Manager to copy cells.

<!-- image -->

This topic describes the following:

- Copying One or More Cells Without Changes
- Copying Individual Cells With Changes

See also Creating New and Reusing Cell Hierarchies.

## Copying One or More Cells Without Changes

You can copy cells without changes to create duplicate versions in a different library.

The new versions retains their names, maintain their positions within any cell categories, and update their references. (To change these aspects of a cell while copying it, see instead Copying Individual Cells With Changes).

To copy cells without changes:

1. In the Library Manager Cells list, press Ctrl, and use the mouse to select one or more cell names.
2. Drag the name or names toward the destination library.
3. At the destination, drop the names in place, and release Ctrl.

If you do not use the Ctrl key, the system moves the cells instead of copying them.

If the system detects cells with duplicate names in the destination library, the Conflicts dialog box opens. See Managing Duplicate Name Conflicts.

## The Lib Name Field's Dependency from Source and Destination library Selection Change

When no direct edits have been made to the Destination frame's Cell Name field, since the dialog box was first shown, then the Cell Name field track changes to the selection in the source Cellslistview as follows:

- If the new selection is a single cell, then the selected cell name is entered into the Cell Name field.
- If the new selection has multiple cells then the Cell Name field is cleared, and disabled.
- After edits are made to the Cell Name field, this tracking stops.
- Tracking resumes, if the Cell Name field value is emptied, or matches to a cell name from source selector by selecting a cell from destination cells list, or by changing Cell Name filed value manually

If the value in Cell Name field doesn't match to any cell in destination cells list, the selection in destination cells list is cleared.

The Lib Name field is initially seeded from source library selector's selection. If the field is not empty a selection change of source library is not set. Any selection change in destination library selector is reflected on Lib Name field.

The value of Lib Name field can be entered also manually. If the value in Lib Name field does not match to any library in destination libraries list (note that read-only libraries are not listed in the list,and they also should not be possible to use as destination), the selection in destination libraries list is cleared.

The following prompt is to show if the destination library doesn't exist: 'The destination library '%s' doesn't exist. Do you want to create it and continue?', where the Create button will create the library and continue copy process, and Cancel will cancel the operation, by returning the control to parent dialog box.

<!-- image -->

## Copying Individual Cells With Changes

You can copy an individual cell with changes to create an additional version of it while changing some cell aspects. As you create the new version, you can choose to change the cell name, its position in cell categories, and its references.

To copy an individual cell with changes:

1. In the Library Manager, specify the cell to copy using one of these methods:
- From the Cells list, select the cell name, right-click the mouse, and choose Copy .
- From the Edit menu, choose Copy &gt; Cell , and filter the list to select it.
- Make sure the cell name is selected in the Cells list. From the Toolbar , click Copy .

The Copy Cell dialog box opens.

<!-- image -->

## 2. In the Copy Cell dialog box that opens, specify the following settings:

<!-- image -->

## Setting

Source

## Description

The source cell to copy. Filter the list to specify the source cell, or directly select the cell name. To view cell categories during this procedure, choose Show Cell Categories .

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Setting     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|-------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Destination | Cell Name The name for the copied cell at its destination. Filter the list to select a base name or directly enter one. If the new selection has multiple cells then the Cell Name field is cleared, and disabled. Maintain Cell Categories inserts copied cells into corresponding categories at their destination, creating categories if necessary. Alternatively, you can place the cell in a new category by deselecting this option, and choosing a category from the list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Options     | Update References lets you choose to update references to only Copied Cells , all cells in the Destination Library , or all cells in All Writable Libraries . Skip Update for PCell Instances excludes PCells in the update process. You can choose how to resolve destination conflicts during the copy operation: ◦ Handle conflicts with rename : Opens the Cell Conflicts dialog box to let you rename the selected cells. ◦ Handle conflicts by selecting best cell : Opens the Cell Selection dialog box and lets you choose the cells to copy to the destination, and skip the cells if conflicts exist. Copy Hierarchical References copies the hierarchy underneath the cell by descending the hierarchy, and copying the master of each instance. To control where descent stops, enter a list of library names in the Exclude Libraries text box. (Descent stops at a reference to any cellView within any of these libraries). To copy only certain views, enter them in the Include Views text box. To copy cellview based on the view type name, select the cell view type name from the View Types list. To exclude the specified cell view type name, select Exclude . The default is Select All . The view type filtering applies to the copied cellviews and to the cellview references from the copied hierarchy. Rename All Cells lets you use new names for the copied cells in the library. Specify the new name for the cells in the box. You can use name patterns to rename the cells in the library. The name patterns you can use include %L (original library name), %C (original cell name), %N (a unique number in the system), and %<character> (one or more characters). For example, %C_a uses the original cell name ( %C ) and adds the _a suffix. |

3. When you are finished, click Apply .

<!-- image -->

If the system detects cells with duplicate names in the destination library, the Conflicts dialog box opens. See Managing Duplicate Name Conflicts.

4. Click OK to close the Copy Cell dialog box.

The destination library now contains the copied cells with changes.

## Moving Cells

You can use the Library Manager to rename a cell or move it to a different library. You can move cells from one library to another with or without changing their names and other details.

This topic describes the following:

- Moving One or More Cells Without Changes
- Moving Individual Cells With Changes

## Moving One or More Cells Without Changes

You can move one or more cells to relocate them while maintaining cell categories and references. The moved cells retain their names during the process.

To move one or more cells without changes:

- In the Library Manager, select the cell names, and drag them onto the destination library name in the Libraries list.

If the system detects cells with duplicate names in the destination library, the Conflicts dialog box opens. See Managing Duplicate Name Conflicts.

## Moving Individual Cells With Changes

You can move individual cells to relocate them while adjusting category positions, and references. In the process, you can rename the cells.

## To move individual cells with changes:

1. In the Library Manager, specify the cell to move using one of the following methods:
- From the Libraries list, select the cell name, right-click the mouse, and choose Move .
- From the Edit menu, choose Move &gt; Cell , and filter the list to select the cell.
- Make sure the cell name is selected in the Cells list. From the Toolbar , click the Move button.
2. In the Move Cell dialog box that opens, specify the following settings:

<!-- image -->

| Setting     | Description                                                                                                                                                                            |
|-------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Source      | The source cell to move. Filter the list to specify the source cell, or directly select the cell by name. To view cell categories during this procedure, choose Show Cell Categories . |
| Destination | Cell Name The name for the moved cell at its destination. Filter the list to select a base name or directly enter one.                                                                 |

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Setting   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Options   | Maintain Cell Categories inserts moved cells into their original categories at their destination, creating categories if necessary. To place the moved cells in a new category, clear the check box, and choose a different Category . ◦ Update References : Updates references to only Moved Cells , all cells in the Destination Library , or all cells in All Writable Libraries . ◦ Skip Updates for PCell Instances : Does not update PCell instances during the move process. ◦ Rename All Cells : Renames the moved cells to the specified name. You can add prefixes and suffixes to the original cell names. For example, to add a prefix to the original cell name, type <prefix>_%C . |

3. When you are finished, click Apply to start the move operation.

If the system detects cells with duplicate names in the destination library, the Conflicts dialog box opens. See Managing Duplicate Name Conflicts.

4. Click OK to close the Move Cell dialog box.

## Deleting Cells

You can delete a cell to completely remove it from the disk.

## Caution:

You cannot undo this operation. After deleting the selected cells, you cannot retrieve the cell contents.

## To delete a cell:

- In the Library Manager, delete the cell using one of the following methods:
- Select the cell by name, right-click the mouse, and choose Delete .
- Select the cell by name, and choose Edit &gt; Delete .
- Make sure the cell name is selected in the Cells list. From the Toolbar , click Delete .

The destination library no longer contains the cell and its files are deleted.

## Enabling Rotation and Scaling

Some OpenAccess designs, such as flat panel designs, require rotation (by an angle of any integer value) and magnification of instance masters. The Library Manager tool can enable rotation by any integer value and scaling (magnification) by extending a static instance into an extended instance.

<!-- image -->

To enable rotation and scaling:

- In the Library Manager tool, enable rotation and scaling using one of these methods:
- Select the cell by name, right-click the mouse, and choose Enable Rotation and Scaling .
- Select the cell by name, select layout from the CellViews list, right-click the mouse, and choose Enable Rotation and Scaling .

<!-- image -->

## Managing Cellviews

You can manage cellviews by creating, copying, moving, and deleting them.

This topic describes the following:

- Creating Cellviews
- Copying Cellviews
- Moving Cellviews
- Deleting Cellviews

## Creating Cellviews

You can create a cellview to hold one design representation of an individual cell. Creating a cellview creates a container for a single representation of the cell.

Use the Library Manager to create cellviews.

## To create a cellview:

1. In the Library Manager, create the cellview using one of these methods.
- From any location in the cellviews list, right-click and choose New .
- From the File menu, choose New &gt; CellView .
- From the Toolbar, choose Create CellView

<!-- image -->

.

2. In the New CellView dialog box that opens, specify cellview creation details for its library, optional cell category, cell, and view. Select each item directly or filter the lists.
3. Enter a Cell Name for the new cellview.

<!-- image -->

To overwrite the cellview shown, accept the name shown.

4. (Optional) To use a different view, select or enter the View Name .
5. (Optional) To associate a different editor from the ones shown, choose it from the Editor list.
6. (Optional) If you want to start creating the design using the new cellview now, click Open on Create .
7. When you are finished, click Apply to create the new cellview in the specified library.
8. Click OK to close the New Cellview dialog box.

## Copying Cellviews

You can copy a cellview to create an additional version of it in another library. You can copy cellviews from one library to another with or without changing their names, and other details.

<!-- image -->

This topic describes the following:

- Copying One or More Cellviews Without Changes
- Copying Individual Cellviews With Changes

## Copying One or More Cellviews Without Changes

You can copy cellviews without changes to create additional versions in a different library. New versions retain their names, maintain their positions within cell categories, and update their references. To change a cellview while copying it instead, see Copying Individual Cellviews With Changes.

To copy cellviews without changes:

1. In the Library Manager CellViews list, press Ctrl and use the mouse to select one or more cellview names.
2. Drag the name or names toward the destination cell.
3. At the destination, drop the names in place, and release the Ctrl key.

If you do not use the Ctrl key, the system moves the cellviews instead of copying them.

If the system detects cellviews with duplicate names in the destination library, the Conflicts dialog box opens. See Managing Duplicate Name Conflicts.

To copy an individual cellview with changes:

- Make sure the cellview is selected in the Views list. From the Toolbar , click the Copy button.

To control where descent stops, enter a list of library names in the Exclude Libraries text box. (Descent stops at a reference to any cellview within any of these libraries). To copy only certain views, enter them in the Include Views text box. To copy cellview based on the view type name, select the cell view type name from the View Types list. This list is available only when you select Copy Hierarchical References . To exclude the specified cell view type name, select Exclude . The default is Select All . The view type filtering applies to the copied cellviews and to the cellview references from the copied hierarchy. Rename All Cells lets you use new names for the copied cellviews in the library. Specify the new name for the cells in the box. You can use name patterns to rename the cells in the library. The name patterns you can use include %L (original library name), %C (original cell name), %N (a unique number in the system), and %<character> (one or more characters). For example, %C_a uses the original cell name ( %C ) and adds the _a suffix. Open on Copy opens the copied cellview when you click OK . Copy Cell Data copies properties assigned to the cell from the source cellview to the destination cellview, and overwrites any |

3. When you are finished, click Apply .

If the system detects a cellview with a duplicate name in the destination library, the Conflicts dialog box opens. See Managing Duplicate Name Conflicts.

4. Click OK to close the Copy CellView dialog box.

## Moving Cellviews

You can use the Library Manager to rename a cellview or move it to another library with or without changing cellview details.

This topic describes the following:

- Moving One or More Cellviews Without Changes
- Moving Individual Cellviews With Changes

## Moving One or More Cellviews Without Changes

You can move one or more cellviews without changes to automatically maintain categories, and update cellview references during the operation.

To move cellviews without changes:

- In the Library Manager, select one or more cellviews by name, and drag them onto a different cell in the Cells list.

If the system detects cellviews with duplicate names in the destination library, the Conflicts dialog box opens. See Managing Duplicate Name Conflicts.

## Moving Individual Cellviews With Changes

You can move individual cellviews to rename them or relocate them to new cells while adjusting category positions, and references.

To move a cellview with changes:

1. In the Library Manager, specify the cellview to move using one of these methods:
- From the Libraries list, select and right-click the cellview, and choose Move .
- Choose Edit &gt; Move &gt; Cellview , and filter the list to select the cellview.
- Make sure the cellview is selected in the Views list. From the Toolbar , click Move .

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## 2. In the Move Cellview dialog box, specify the settings:

<!-- image -->

## Settings Description

Source The source cellview to move. Filter the list to specify the source cellview or directly select the cellview by name. To view cell categories during this procedure, choose Show Cell Categories .

Destination Cell Name : The cell name for the moved cellview at its destination. Filter the list to select a base name or directly enter one.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Settings   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|            | View Name : The view name for the moved cellview at its destination.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Options    | ◦ Update References within Copied CellViews : Causes all design references to be instantiated cellviews to point to the new cellview location. Only references within the moved cellviews are updated. ◦ Copy Cell Data copies properties assigned to the cell from the source cellview to the destination cellview, and overwrites any conflicting data that exists in the destination cellview. ◦ Skip Updates for Pcell Instances : Does not update PCell instances during the move process. ◦ Rename All Cells : Renames the moved cells to the specified name. You can add prefixes and suffixes to the original cell names. For example, to add a prefix to the original cell name, type <prefix>_%C . ◦ Open on Move : Opens the moved cellview when you click OK . |

If the system detects a cellview with a duplicate name in the destination library, the Conflicts dialog box opens. See Managing Duplicate Name Conflicts.

## Deleting Cellviews

You can delete cellviews by deleting them from a library or deleting them from the disk.

This topic describes the following:

- Deleting Cellviews from a Library
- Deleting Cellviews From Disk

## Deleting Cellviews from a Library

You can delete a cellview from a library by deleting its view list name.

To delete a cellview from a library:

1. In the Library Manager, choose Edit &gt; Delete Views by Name .
2. Specify the libraries from which to delete the view or views.

<!-- image -->

Use the check boxes to specify libraries. You can optionally filter the list.

3. At the bottom of the dialog box, enter the exact names for views to designate for deletion from all selected libraries.

Separate each name with a space. In order to prevent inadvertent deletions, partial names, and wildcard characters, are not accepted here.

4. (Optional) Click Preview .
5. Click Delete .

The system deletes all designated views, closing them first if they are open, and reports the results of the operation.

## Deleting Cellviews From Disk

You can delete a cellview from disk to completely remove it from the system.

## Caution:

Select with care. You cannot undo this operation.

After this operation completes there is no method within this environment to retrieve the contents of the deleted cellview.

<!-- image -->

To delete a cellview from disk:

- In the Library Manager, delete the cellview using one of the following methods:
- Select the cellview by name, right-click the mouse, and choose Delete .
- Select the cellview by name, and choose Edit &gt; Delete .
- Select the cellview by name, and click Delete .

The cellview files are no longer on the disk.

## Managing Duplicate Name Conflicts

You can manage duplicate name conflicts when copying or moving cells, and cellViews, by refining and confirming your selections.

Destination conflicts can occur when a cell or view with the same name already exists in the destination.

Source conflicts can occur when you have chosen to copy hierarchical references, and the system finds multiple source cells or cellViews with the same name.

When name conflicts occur, the Cell Conflict dialog box opens and lets you decide how to resolve them.

To manage duplicate name conflicts:

1. View the list of duplicate items identified by the system.
2. Refine, and confirm, your selections.
- If you are moving or copying cells, and you want to select individual cellViews for the operation, click Manage Views .
- To continue to copy or move all items, click Check All .
- To copy or move only those items without duplicate names in the destination location, where applicable, click Check Not in Dest .
- To deselect all items, click Check None .
3. In the Conflicts dialog box, click Copy , Move , or Overwrite to confirm your selections, and complete the operation.

## Opening a File in the File Browser

Library Manager now supports opening any dmDMFile, through file browser, including files that do not belong to a cellview. Whenever a file does not have a default application associated with it, the operating system's default application is used for the file type.

## Using Cell Categories

## Viewing Cell Categories and Subcategories

You can view categories to see the way cells are classified. Libraries group cells in one category. Custom categories offer an additional level of cell classification.

Use the Library Manager to view cell categories and subcategories.

To view cell categories:

1. In the Library Manager, choose View &gt; Show Cell Categories .
2. To display cells in their parent categories, make sure View &gt; Show Cells in Parent Category is selected (default).

<!-- image -->

Clear the Show Cells In Parent Category check box if you want to display cells under their direct parent category only. This mode is useful when you are trying to organize cells in cell categories. After organizing the cells into their subcatgories, you can select Show Cells In Parent Category to view the results.

3. Select a library.

The Cell Categories column shows custom categories created by designers and their CAD support group. The categories with all cells, and uncategorized cells, are maintained by the Custom Compiler environment.

## Creating New Cell Categories

You can create new cell categories when you want to organize a group of cells.

Use the Library Manager to create new cell categories.

After you create the category by name, you can add cells to the category by Managing Cell Categories.

<!-- image -->

## To create cell categories:

1. In the Library Manager, choose View &gt; Show Cell Categories .

<!-- image -->

## 2. Begin to create the category.

- To create a top-level category for this library, position the cursor on the white space at the bottom of the category list.
- To create a subcategory, position the cursor over the name of the parent category.
3. Right-click and choose New .
4. Enter a unique name for this category. Duplicate names generate a warning message.
5. Click OK.

## Managing Cell Categories

You can manage cell categories to organize, and classify, cells.

Use the Library Manager to manage cell categories.

To manage cell categories:

1. In the Library Manager, choose View &gt; Show Cell Categories .

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## 2. Manage categories:

- To rename a category, position your cursor on the name of the category, right-click, choose Rename , enter a new name, and click Rename .
- To move a category under another category, select its name, and drag and drop it onto the name of the target category.
- To move cells from one category to another, expand the source category so that its contents are visible in the Cells column. From the Cells column, drag cells you want to move to their new category in the Cell Categories column.
- To delete a category, select its name, right-click, and choose Delete .
- To move a cell out of any category, you can optionally move it to the Uncategorized category.

## Post-processing MCells

You can import, export, and refresh MCells with the Library Manager.

These sections cover:

- Importing MCells
- Exporting MCells
- Refreshing MCells

## Importing MCells

You can import MCells by parsing a specified MCell definition file into the MCell superMaster design.

1. Begin by opening the Library Manager. From the Console tab or any open design window, choose Tools &gt; Library Manager .
2. In the Library Manager, choose to Edit &gt; MCell &gt; Import .

The Import MCell dialog box appears.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

3. Choose the target library from the Libraries pane.
4. Specify the MCell definition file in the MCell File text field or click the Browse button to choose the file. The default file extension is *.mcdef . This is controlled by the Tcl preference dbImportMCellFileName .

In the definition file, multiple MCells can be defined at the same time. For information, see Custom Compiler Application Notes.

5. (Optional) Enable the Overwrite Existing Cellviews option to overwrite any existing cellview with the new-defined cellview if any new-defined superMaster's cell name and view name are in conflict with the existing cellview.
6. (Optional) Enable the Load CDF option to load the CDF parameters of defined MCells.

To load the CDF parameters defined in files stored in a particular directory, specify the directory name.

To load the CDF parameters defined in a particular file (with the naming format, library name -cell name .tcl), specify the file name.

## Exporting MCells

You can export all MCell superMasters in the specified library to an output file through an Export MCell dialog box. This output file can be used as the MCell definition file when importing MCells.

1. Begin by opening the Library Manager. From the Console tab or any open design window, choose Tools &gt; Library Manager .
2. In the Library Manager, choose to Edit &gt; MCell &gt; Export .

The Export MCell dialog box appears.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

3. Choose the required library from the Libraries pane.
4. In the MCell File text field, specify a file name for the MCell definition file to be exported, or click the Browse button to choose the file. The default file extension is *.mcdef . This is controlled by the Tcl preference dbExportMCellFileName .

If the specified file name already exists, you will be prompted to confirm overwriting the existing file.

To export the CDF parameters of all the MCells defined in the selected library to a directory, select Export CDF and specify the directory name. The CDF parameters for each MCell are exported as a file with the naming format, library name -cell name.tcl .

In the output file, the sequence of MCell superMasters, layer definitions, and the rules might be changed and might be different from the imported MCell definitions file.

For information, see MCell Definition File in Custom Compiler Layout Editor User Guide for Creating and Editing Objects .

## Refreshing MCells

You can use the Edit &gt; MCell &gt; Refresh command to get the latest subMaster layout with the up-to-date superMaster and evaluator.

In the Refresh MCell dialog box, you can specify the superMasters of MCells and editable PCells and the target design libraries. The tool refreshes the recovery and version parameters for MCells and editable PCells, and saves the MCell instance and editable PCell instances and vias in the target design libraries with specified superMasters.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

When multiple users work on the same design, the Custom Compiler tool checks whether MCell SuperMasterSignature is changed and reports an error message if it fails to create or edit the edited MCells when reloading MCell definitions.

You can use the leMGRDefaultParam Tcl preference to calculate the default parameters for MCell guard rings when importing MCell definitions.

When you update MCell definitions locally, use Edit &gt; MCell &gt; Refresh to update the layout of MCells.

When other users update the MCell definitions, load the new MCell definitions from disk to update the content in memory using one of the following methods:

- Use the following Tcl command to reload: db::loadMCells -libName $mcellSuperMasterLibName
- Exit Custom Compiler and restart the tool.
