## Parameter Definition Editor Tool

You can use the Parameter Definition Editor to display, define, and set values for parameters.

Parameters are metadata associated with instance objects. Parameters differ from properties in that they can only be associated with instance objects. Additionally, the definition of the parameter cannot be created directly on an instance. Instead, the parameter definitions are inherited from data stored in the instance master's associated cell and library.

CAD support personnel and library developers can define parameters to serve the requirements of output tools.

This topic describes the following:

- Displaying the Parameter Definition Editor Tool
- Viewing Parameters
- Adding Parameters
- Adjusting Parameters
- Editing Components Parameters
- Viewing CDF Overlay Parameters
- Editing CDF Overlay Parameters
- Parameter Definition Editor Menus
- Parameter Definition Editor Toolbar

## Displaying the Parameter Definition Editor Tool

To display the Parameter Definition Editor, use one of the following methods:

- From the Custom Compiler Home tab, choose Tools &gt; Parameter Definition Editor .
- From the Library Manager, choose Edit &gt; Parameter Definitions .
- In the Library Manager, right-click a selected library or cell and choose Edit Parameter Definitions .
- In the Schematic Editor, press Q or choose Edit &gt; Properties &gt; Assistant or Window &gt; Assistants &gt; Property Editor to bring up the Property Editor, from which you choose Parameter Definitions from the toolbar menu .

<!-- image -->

## Viewing Parameters

You can view parameters in the Parameter Definition Editor to begin to work with them.

To view parameters:

1. In the Parameter Definition Editor, choose Library or Cell .
2. The table view contains the Parameters tab and other tabs of the propList section ( SimInfo , ViewInfo , and Display ). Switch tabs to view the parameter information. Cell Value is provided to display the value of selected column.

<!-- image -->

To edit and view the details of lxComponentType, see Editing Components Parameters.

3. The table view can be switched to tree mode by setting the dbEnableTableBasedParamDefEditor preference. For example: db::setPrefValue dbEnableTableBasedParamDefEditor -value false

<!-- image -->

Scroll to view the parameters.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

4. To find a parameter, enter the parameter name in the Find box, and click Next or Previous .

If the Find box is not shown, choose Edit &gt; Find to display it.

## Adding Parameters

You can add a parameter to an object by defining its type, and optionally setting its value.

To add a parameter:

<!-- image -->

1. In the Parameter Definition Editor, choose Edit &gt; Add Parameter . Alternatively, click .
2. Type the name of the parameter and press Enter . The new parameter is added to the list.
3. Define each parameter aspect by left-clicking next to the notation. Define the type, prompt, callback, units, default value, display, whether editable, use,

parseAsPEL, parseAsNumber, storeDefault, and propList.

4. Choose File &gt; Save .

## Adjusting Parameters

You can adjust parameters to change values set for them.

To adjust parameters:

1. In the Parameter Definition Editor, view the tree display.
2. To rearrange the order of the parameters, drag a parameter to its new position in the list.
3. To rename a parameter, double-click the parameter name, and type the new name.

To modify parameters using Component Description Format (CDF) overlays, see Modifying Component Description Format (CDF) Overlays.

## Editing Components Parameters

You can view and edit the values of the lxComponentType parameters in the Edit Components dialog box.

To view and edit the values of the lxComponentType parameters:

1. Click the Default Value column from lxComponentType.
2. The button appears next to the Cell Value field. ..
3. Click the button to enable Edit Components dialog box. The table is categorized the components information by Device Type . The Check button parses and checks the components from the library into the Components Report dialog box.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Viewing CDF Overlay Parameters

If a Component Description Format (CDF) overlay library exists, the Parameter Definition Editor automatically displays the Overlay option. If more than one CDF overlay is available, the list of CDF overlays is displayed. The order of the overlays is determined by the ASSIGN dbOverlayPath statements in the lib.defs file. See Modifying Component Description Format (CDF) Overlays.

<!-- image -->

To view overlay library parameters:

- In the Parameter Definition Editor, select Overlay .

Selecting Overlay displays the available overlays in the Parameter Definition Editor. The overlays are ordered from the highest to the lowest priority. The default active overlay is the overlay with the highest priority.

If you select Base , only the base CDF is displayed in the editor.

If you select Effective , parameters of effective level, all overlays, and the base CDF level are displayed in the read-only mode. Effective is in the highest precedence level, supersedes Base and Overlay . The tool allows to change CDF data dynamically in the Effective level. All the Effective level information is cleared after closing the tool.

When overlays are displayed in the Parameter Definition Editor:

- Italicized text indicates the base parameter values.
- Non-italicized text indicates overlays that override base parameter values.
- Bold text indicates edited parameter values.

The following example shows an overlay in use. The w parameters are italicized to indicate that they are values from the base library. The model parameters, which are not italicized, contain overlay values that override the w parameters. The defValue model parameter is in bold font because it has been edited.

<!-- image -->

## Chapter 8: Tools for Designing Parameter Definition Editor Tool

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Editing CDF Overlay Parameters

You can use the Parameter Definition Editor to edit the parameters of one or more Component Description Format (CDF) overlays.

To edit overlay library parameters:

1. In the Parameter Definition Editor, select Overlay .

Selecting Overlay displays the available overlays in the Parameter Definition Editor. The overlays are ordered from the highest to the lowest priority. The default active overlay is the overlay with the highest priority.

SingleCDFOverlay MultipleCDFOverlays

<!-- image -->

If you select Base , only the base CDF is displayed in the editor.

If you select Effective , parameters of effective level, all overlays, and the base CDF level are displayed in the read-only mode. You can use the db::getParamDefs and db::setNetlistInfo commands to edit the CDF data under the Effective level. For examples:

## Example 4

## Example 5

```
[db::getParamDefs $param_name -of $cell -level memory] db::setAttr param.defvalue -value $new_value db::setNetlistInfo termOrder -data $lib -info simInfo -netlister hspiceD -level memory -value $new_value
```

2. (Multiple overlays only) In the Overlay list, select the overlay you want to edit.

The CDF data for the selected overlay and all overlays with lower priority appear in the editor. Data of overlays with higher priority are not displayed.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

For example, if Overlay1 has the highest priority and Overly3 has the lowest priority, then:

- If you select Overlay, parameters of all overlays and the base CDF are displayed in priority order.
- If you select Overlay2, parameters of Overlay2, Overlay3, and the base CDF are displayed in priority order.
- If you select Overlay3, parameters of Overlay3 and the base CDF are displayed in priority order.
3. Edit the overlay parameters.

When Overlay is selected, you can edit the parameters of the selected overlays. When Base is selected, you can edit the base CDF data only.

## Displaying the Search and Replace Tool

To display the Search and Replace tool, use one of the following methods:

- From the Console, choose Tools &gt; Search and Replace .
- From the Library Manager, choose Edit &gt; Search and Replace .
- From the Layout Editor, choose Query &gt; Search and Replace .
- From the Schematic Editor, choose Edit &gt; Search and Replace .
- From the Symbol Editor, choose Edit &gt; Search and Replace .
- From the Text Editor, click Search and Replace on the Standard toolbar.

The Search and Replace dialog box displays. The content of tabs in the dialog box are the same.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The default search scope depends on where you displayed the Search and Replace tool. To change the scope, see Setting the Design Root.

## Setting Search and Replace Options

There are two general search and replace options. You can make replacement processes ignore properties that cannot be edited. You can make all searches case-sensitive.

<!-- image -->

To set general search and replace options:

- In the Search and Replace tab or dialog box, choose one of the following Options commands:
- Honor Property Editability ignores properties that are not editable in a search and replace operation. By default, this option is enabled, and properties that are not editable are ignored.
- Case Sensitive performs all searches in a case-sensitive manner. This option does not affect replacement values, which are applied exactly as you enter them. By default, this option is enabled, and case is evaluated in a search operation.
- Save Changes with Replace All is disabled by default, and when enabled, saves changes made by the Replace All operation.
- Replace All is disabled by default, and when enabled, selects the Replace All option in the Search and Replace dialog box.
- Show Delete , Show Replace , and Show Clear are enabled by default, and when disabled, hides the Delete , Replace , and Clear buttons in the Search and Replace dialog box.
- Match Pattern Type determines if the search operation should use Exact matching, glob-style Wildcard matching, or if the input should be interpreted as a regular expression ( Reg Expr ). See Searching for Design Components.
- Partial Match Type determines if the pattern matching should be partial or full. When disabled, the pattern match is considered to have succeeded only if the pattern matches the entire target string. when enabled, the pattern match is

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

considered to have succeeded if it matches any substring of the target string. See Searching for Design Components.

- Search root of EIP mode determines which cellview, either Edit (default) or View , to use from the parent design editor window as a search root cellview.

## Setting the Design Root

When you display the Search and Replace tool from the Console tab, the search scope defaults to the library level. You can set a design root to limit the scope to a single design or design hierarchy for search and replace operations.

If you opened the Search and Replace tool from a design editor, the search scope defaults to the design level. To use a different top design for search and replace operations, set a design root.

To display the Search and Replace window with no design root set automatically, from the Console tab choose Tools &gt; Search and Replace . From here, you can independently set any scope and search options. You do not need to open a design first.

To set the design root:

1. In the Search and Replace window, choose File &gt; Design Root . The Set Design Root dialog box opens.
2. Enter the top design (for a new design root) by its library, cell, and view.
3. Enter traversal options to determine the extent of any searches from this top design.
4. Click OK .

<!-- image -->

## Setting Search Criteria for Attributes and Properties

When searching instances and vias, you can filter objects based on attributes, properties, and value comparisons. All value comparisons are done on the value stored in the database.

To set the search criteria:

1. On the Attributes tab, click to add an attribute in the Attribute Name column. You can chose an attribute from one of the following: Area, Array, Columns, Delta X, Delta Y, Depth Limit, Fixed, Frozen, Height, Orientation, Origin, Physical Only, Placement Status, Rows, Soft Macro, Usage, or Width.

Alternatively, on the Properties tab, click to add a property in the Property Name column.

(Optional) Use the Tab key to navigator the entries in a row.

2. Enter the operator in the Operator column.

For example, to check to see if a parameter exists on an object, you can use the =~ operator with a value of ".*" .

The following table lists operators for objects evaluated in attribute and property searches.

| Name                  | Symbol   | Finds design objects where the attribute or property value ...                                                                            |
|-----------------------|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Equality              | ==       | Is equal to the specified value. By default, when you select an attribute or a property, the operator is set to the default value of == . |
| Inequality            | !=       | Is not equal to the specified value.                                                                                                      |
| Less Than             | <        | Is less than the specified value.                                                                                                         |
| Greater Than          | >        | Value is greater than the specified value.                                                                                                |
| Less Than or Equal    | <=       | Value is less than or equal to the specified value.                                                                                       |
| Greater Than or Equal | >=       | Value is greater than or equal to the specified value.                                                                                    |
| Pattern Match         | =~       | ( Properties tab only) Matches the specified regular expression. The pattern matching style is controlled by the preference .             |

dbRegexp

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Name                                 | Symbol       | Finds design objects where the attribute or property value ...                                                                                                                                      |
|--------------------------------------|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Pattern does not match               | !~           | ( Properties tab only) Does not match the specified regular expression. The pattern matching style is controlled by the preference dbRegexp .                                                       |
| Value does not have a local override | isDefault    | ( Properties tab only) Value is the default value: returns true . Note that this returns false if the effective value is set by a local value, regardless of whether the value matches the default. |
| Value does have a local override     | isNotDefault | ( Properties tab only) Effective value is set by a local override: returns true .                                                                                                                   |

3. Enter the current attribute or property value you want to find in the Value column.
4. (Optional) In the New Value column, enter the replacement value if you want this attribute or property value to be replaced.

Alternatively, you can enter &lt;Delete&gt; in this column to delete the found attribute or property value and reset it to the default value.

5. (Optional) Select one or more rows in the attributes or properties table, right-click and choose Delete to remove the selected rows from the table.

<!-- image -->

## Searching for Design Components

You use the Search and Replace tool to find design components. The tool recognizes design components as OpenAccess objects. Therefore, when you perform a search, you are searching for OpenAccess objects.

Using the search results, you can replace attribute values, properties, and parameters associated with objects either individually or as a batch operation.

To search for design components:

1. On the Standard toolbar in the Search and Replace dialog box, choose the Match type.

<!-- image -->

| Match Type     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Exact          | Finds exact matches only.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Reg Expr       | Finds patterns that are regular expressions.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Wildcard       | Uses wildcard matching that conforms to IEEE standard 1003.1-2001 sections 2.13.1 and 2.13.2 describing patterns to match a single character and multiple characters. The symbol $ accepts a single character wildcard match. |
| Partial        | Additionally finds any subset of a complete string.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Case Sensitive | Performs all searches in a case-sensitive manner. This option is a shortcut to Options > Case Sensitive described in Setting Search and Replace Options.                                                                      |
| Replace All    | This option is disabled by default. This option is a shortcut to Options > Replace All described in Setting Search and Replace Options.                                                                                       |

## 2. Choose Scope to control the extent of the search:

| Scope    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Design   | Searches all objects in the open design (offered when you open this feature from a design).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Viewport | Searches all objects in the viewport.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Region   | Searches a user-defined polygon or rectangle. When the search scope is Region , you choose Polygon or Rectangle from the toolbar. For polygons, you can select the Angle mode. You can also select the search Criteria from the toolbar: touch/intersect or enclose. For the intersect selection criteria type, the objects that intersect the specified region are also searched. For the enclose criteria type, only objects that are fully enclosed in the specified region are searched. |

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Scope                            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|----------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Design Hierarchy                 | Searches the design hierarchy for the open design (offered when you open this feature from a design). When the search scope is Design and the hierarchy depth is Levels , you have the option of enabling Show Occurrences (next to the Search button) to view results for hierarchical searches by their occurrences, and you can also set the start/stop levels. See Getting Total Number of Instances Used in a Design. |
| Selection                        | Searches the current selection set.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Library                          | Searches the library you specify here by choosing from the list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| All Libraries Writable Libraries | Searches all available writable libraries. Only writable libraries are selectable in the Search Scope list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

3. Choose Objects to specify the design component:
4. The object tab may vary depending on the object type you select from Objects . Set additional criteria to narrow the search, and provide replacement values.

<!-- image -->

| Search Object Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Instances            | In the Instance Criteria tab, finds instances by the instance criteria you specify: Library , Cell , View , or Instance Name . To search for instances where the Placed master is unbound (missing from the technology file) or where a Replacement master exists , choose Advanced Filters , and specify one or both of these options. |
|                      | To additionally search for vias by their attributes, see Step 5. To additionally search for vias by their properties, see Step 6.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

<!-- image -->

| Search Object Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Instance Arrays      | In the Instance Criteria tab, finds instance arrays by the Library , Cell , View , or Instance Name you specify. To optionally filter results based on object attributes of rows, columns, delta x, or delta y, choose one of these options, specify an operator, and choose a value. You can obtain the object attribute value to enter here by selecting an object, and viewing its attributes in the Property Editor. To include instance arrays where the Placed master is unbound , or where a Replacement master exists , choose Advanced Filters , and select one or both of these options. |
| Vias                 | In the Via Criteria tab, finds vias by their via definition names or net names. To search for unnetted vias, turn on Find only unnetted vias . Net Name is disabled when this option is turned on. To replace only vias where the given replacement via definition exists, choose the Advanced Filters tab, and                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

Net Name is disabled when this option is turned on.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Text                 | Finds text objects by text, LPP, font, rotation, justification, and height.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Connection Defs      | Finds connection definitions by their names, or the names of the associated default nets.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

5. In the Attributes tab (for instances and vias only), specify attributes for instances, instance arrays, and vias, and provide replacement values. See Setting Search Criteria for Attributes and Properties about operators for objects evaluated in property searches.
6. In the Properties tab, specify properties for instances, instance arrays, and vias, and provide replacement values. See Setting Search Criteria for Attributes and Properties about operators for objects evaluated in property searches.
7. (Optional) In the Advanced Filters tab, select one or both of the following criteria:
- Placed master is unbound
- Replacement master exists
8. Do one of the following to start the search:
- To search without making replacements, click the Search button.
8. (The Find Objects button on the toolbar also performs this operation).
- To search and automatically replace found values, on the toolbar click Find and replace all objects .
9. View process status on the Status bar (at the lower window edge).

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

(Optional) To halt the search process and retain results found up to this point, press Ctrl+C.

When the search process finishes, the results appear in the Results area.

## Browsing Component Search Results

To browse component search results:

1. In the Results browser, select the result you want to view.

Selecting a result highlights the component on the canvas and, in layouts, also applies the current Zoom to Fit setting. For schematics, single-click items to highlight them, and double-click to apply the current Zoom to Fit setting.

<!-- image -->

2. To view the previous result, click Prev . To view the next result, click Next .
3. (Optional) Set the following viewing options:

| Options      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Zoom to Fit  | Fills the viewport with the image of the selected item, adjusted by the zoom level you specify.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Replace      | Replaces existing values with new values for the currently selected items. The tool indicates successful replacement by changing item listings to italic type. For additional information, see Replacing Component Aspects Using Search Results.                                                                                    |
| Select All   | Selects all items in the results. You can use this option to select all objects for batch replacement of any specified attribute values, properties, or parameters. If you set the dbFindAutoSelectInEditor Tcl preference to true , Select All also adds the selected result components to the selection set in the design editor. |
| Deselect All | Deselects all items in the results.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Delete       | Deletes the selected object from the design.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Options                                        | Description                                                                                          |
|------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Clear                                          | Removes the selected item or items from the search results.                                          |
| From the Actions menu, choose Add to Selection | Adds all items in the search results to the selected set, and shows the selection set on the canvas. |

## Refining Component Search Results

You can refine component search results to find a subset of items within an existing set of search results.

To refine search results:

1. Obtain search results by Searching for Design Components.
2. At the top of the Search and Results tab or dialog box, adjust search criteria values for searching within these results.

For example, you can refine a search you made previously for text labels on LPPs (see Searching for Design Components) to now locate individual LPPs in the search results by layout shape. To do this, change the search type to Shapes , select Any LPP from the list, and choose text as the Object Type .

3. On the toolbar, click the Refine Current Result button, or choose Actions &gt; Refine Result .

The tool performs a new search within the existing search results, and lists a new set of results.

## Checking Whether a Property Exists on an Instance

You can use the Search and Replace tool to determine whether a property exists on an instance.

The example that follows illustrates this process.

Assume that you have a design that contains instances with the model property, and you want to find all the instances having that property.

1. In the Properties tab, define the Property Name as model .
2. Define the Operator as =~ . (Setting Search Criteria for Attributes and Properties lists operators for objects evaluated in property searches).
3. Use .* for the Value .
4. Click Search .
5. In the Results browser, review the list of found instances.

## Finding Instances With the Default Value of a Given Property

You can use the Search and Replace tool to find instances that have the given property set at its default value.

The example that follows illustrates this process.

Assume that you have a design that contains instances with the wtot property, and you want to find all the instances having the default value of that property.

<!-- image -->

1. In the Properties tab, define the Property Name as wtot .
2. Define the Operator as isDefault . (Setting Search Criteria for Attributes and Properties lists operators for objects evaluated in property searches).

Alternatively, if you want to search for instances having a non-default value of a given property, define the Operator as isNotDefault .

3. Click Search .
4. In the Results browser, review the list of found instances.

## Finding Instances With a Specific Property Value

You can use the Search and Replace tool to find instances that have the given property set at a specific value, or greater than or less than a specific value.

The example that follows illustrates this process.

Assume that you want to find all instances named n\_4t2 from the library ref9 that have a w property greater than 1u.

1. In the Instance Criteria tab, define the Library Name as ref9 and the Cell Name as n\_4t2 .
2. In the Properties tab, define the Property Name as w .
3. Define the Operator as &gt;= . (Setting Search Criteria for Attributes and Properties lists operators for objects evaluated in property searches).
4. Use 1u for the Value .
5. Click Search .
6. In the Results browser, review the list of found instances.

## Finding Instances With a Property Not Equal to a Specific Value

You can use the Search and Replace tool to find instances with a property that is not set at a specific value.

The example that follows illustrates this process.

Assume that you want to find all instances named n\_4t2 from the library ref9 that have a w property not equal to 3u.

1. In the Instance Criteria tab, define the Library Name as ref9 and the Cell Name as n\_4t2 .
2. In the Properties tab, define the Property Name as w .

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

3. Define the Operator as != . (Setting Search Criteria for Attributes and Properties lists operators for objects evaluated in property searches).
4. Use 3u for the Value .
5. Click Search .
6. In the Results browser, review the list of found instances.

## Finding Instances With a Property Value in a Given Range

You can use the Search and Replace tool to find instances that have the given property within a range of values by defining more than one search criteria for that property.

The example that follows illustrates this process.

Assume that you want to find all instances named n\_4t2 from the library ref9 that have a w property between 0.5u and 3.5u.

1. In the Instance Criteria tab, define the Library Name as ref9 and the Cell Name as n\_4t2 .
2. In the Properties tab, define the Property Name as w .
3. Define the Operator as &gt;= . (Setting Search Criteria for Attributes and Properties lists operators for objects evaluated in property searches.)
4. Use 0.5u for the Value .
5. Click row 2 to add another search criteria.
6. Define the Property Name as w again.
7. Define the Operator as &lt;= .
8. Use 3.5u for the Value .
9. Click Search .
10. In the Results browser, review the list of found instances.

## Finding Via Vector Values

You can use the Search and Replace tool to find via vector values, and additionally replace them with new values. An example illustrates this process.

The example that follows illustrates this process.

Assume that you want to search for an oaVia with a cutSpacing value of (0.2, 0.3) and replace it with a cutSpacing value of (0.4, 0.5). For a successful search to find this twovalue search entry, the search criteria notation must include the parentheses.

When you use this process in practice, open the Property Editor to identify values for input criteria.

To search for, and replace, an oaVia vector value:

1. (Optional) Open the design. (You can perform search-and-replace operations with no design open).

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

2. Open the Search and Replace tool. From the Console, choose Tools &gt; Search and Replace . Alternatively, from the Library Manager, choose Edit &gt; Search and Replace .
3. Specify a search scope of Design .
4. Specify a search type of Vias .
5. On the Via Criteria tab, choose a via definition value of via12 .
6. On the Properties tab, enter search criteria.
- a. Enter the property name cutSpacing .
- b. Accept the default operator of ==.
- c. Enter a Value of (0.2, 0.3) , including the parentheses.
- d. Enter a New Value of (0.4, 0.5) , including the parentheses.
7. Click Search .
8. In the Results browser, select the via whose vector value you want to replace. (If you searched for only one oaVia, this is the only via listed).
9. Click Replace .

The tool replaces the cutSpacing value for this oaVia.

## Replacing Component Aspects Using Search Results

You can replace attribute values, properties, and parameters. You can make replacements while performing a search, or you can review the search results, and then make replacements.

To replace component aspects using search results:

1. Set up the search by Searching for Design Components.
2. In the Instance Criteria and Properties tabs, review the values available for replacement.

<!-- image -->

3. In the New Value column, enter the replacement values.
4. Perform replacement operations:
- To replace values for currently selected objects, click Replace .
- To replace values as a batch operation for all items in this scope, click Select All and then click Replace .

The tool indicates successful replacement by changing item listings to italic type.

5. (Optional) Save all designs modified by a replacement operation (including designs not currently shown) by choosing File &gt; Save .

## Replacing Scientific Notation With Equivalent Value

You can use the Search and Replace tool to replace regular expressions with Perl-style substitution formats. The grouping metacharacters () are supported, allowing for the extraction of the parts of a string that match. For each grouping, the part that matches inside the () goes into the special variables $1 , $2 , and so forth. For example, the pattern (\S+)Lib$ can be used to match analogLib or myLib . Using the substitution pattern $1Lib2 would produce analogLib2 and myLib2 respectively.

The example that follows illustrates this process.

Assume that you have a design that contains instances with the w property, and you want to find all the instances of that property having u at the end, and replace that value with 10e-6 .

1. In the Properties tab, define the Property Name as w .
2. Define the Operator as =~ . (Setting Search Criteria for Attributes and Properties lists operators for objects evaluated in property searches).
3. Use (.+)u for the Value .
4. Use $1e-6 for the New Value .
5. Click Search .
6. In the Results browser, review the list of found instances in which the value has been replaced as specified.

<!-- image -->

This topic describes the following:

## Replacing Values Within Search Results

You can enter multiple search criteria in each tab to specify what to search, and then what to replace in the results of that search.

The example that follows illustrates this process.

Assume that you want to find all instances named n\_4t2 from the library ref9 that have a w property greater than 2u. Then, within that group, you want to replace any instance of the nf property with the number 4.

1. In the Instance Criteria tab, define the Library Name as ref9 and the Cell Name as n\_4t2 .
2. In the Properties tab, define the Property Name as w .
3. Define the Operator as &gt;= (greater than or equal to). (Setting Search Criteria for Attributes and Properties lists operators for objects evaluated in property searches).
4. Enter 2u for the Value .
5. Click row 2 to add another search criteria.
6. Define the Property Name as nf .
7. Define the Operator as =~ .
8. Enter .* for the Value .
9. Enter 4 for the New Value .
10. Click Search .
11. In the Results browser, review the list of found instances.

## Replacing Values With Value Multiplied by a Constant

You can also replace the value of a property with its current value multiplied by a constant.

The example that follows illustrates this process.

Assume that you want to find all instances named p\_4t2 from the library ref9 that have a w property less than or equal to 3u, then replace that with the value multiplied by 4.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

1. In the Instance Criteria tab, define the Library Name as ref9 and the Cell Name as p\_4t2 .
2. In the Properties tab, define the Property Name as w .
3. Define the Operator as &lt;= .
4. Enter 3u for the Value .
5. Enter 3*$w for the New Value .
6. Click Search .
7. In the Results Browser , review the list of found instances.

## Technology Manager Tool

Manage technologies through the Custom Compiler Technology Manager. Use the Technology Manager to create design library access to the correct technology database for the current design objective. The technology database is located either inside the design library or referenced via inheritance through another library that has the technology you want to use. If referenced, the referenced library must exist first, otherwise, the technology is considered unbound.

This topic describes the following:

- Displaying the Technology Manager Tool
- Considering Technology Management Options
- Changing the Technology Referenced by a Design Library
- Importing Technology Data
- Exporting Technology Data
- Adding a Reference
- Deleting a Reference
- Saving a Modified Technology Database
- Reverting Changes to a Modified Technology Database

## Displaying the Technology Manager Tool

You can display the Technology Manager using one of the following methods:

- From the Console tab, choose Tools &gt; Technology Manager .
- From the Library Manager, choose Edit &gt; Technology .

The Technology Manager appears and displays the list of libraries.

<!-- image -->

The Technology Manager will also list read-only libraries. However, for read-only libraries:

- The File menu commands will be disabled to prevent you from importing, exporting, reverting, and saving changes.
- The Edit menu commands will be disabled to prevent you from adding references and deleting references. If only a parent reference is read-only, then the commands are disabled for the specific parent reference only.
- User-interface operations, such as drag-and-drop actions, will be disabled.
- The Attachment selection is disabled for the library.

## Considering Technology Management Options

Consider your options given these possible situations:

- If you have a technology file (without a techArray), you can create a library that uses this technology. In this case, use the Library Manager to create the library. Then use the Technology Manager to either compile the technology file into it, or to reference

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

another library with the technology you want to use. Alternatively, you can attach the available default technology file. For all technology options, use the Technology Manager. See Importing Technology Data.

- If you have a technology file that includes a techArray, the techArray defines the required technology libraries to reference and these libraries need to now exist. In this case, you can use the Technology Manager to import the technology from the technology file. See Importing Technology Data.
- If you have a library, you can import technology into it. Additionally, if you have manually edited a technology file, you can import it into a new or existing library, creating a technology database for that library that matches the technology described in the file. Use the Technology Manager. See Importing Technology Data.
- From any library with attached technology data, you can export the technology data for use in additional libraries or to edit for customizing. Use the Technology Manager. See Exporting Technology Data.

## Changing the Technology Referenced by a Design Library

You can change the technology referenced by a library to use a different technology for the library.

If the technology was compiled into the library, the referenced library name and the design library name are shown as matching in the Technology Manager.

1. Begin by opening the Technology Manager. From the Console tab, choose Tools &gt; Technology Manager . Alternatively, from the Library Manager, choose Edit &gt; Technology .
2. In the Technology Manager, locate the design library by name, click the technology library currently referenced, and choose a different library from the list.

If a referenced library is read-only, the list does not appear.

Libraries whose referenced technology has been changed appear in italic type. Libraries associated with incremental technology are identified by the "(i)" notation after the reference name.

To reverse this operation, repeat Step 2, and choose the previously used technology library.

## Importing Technology Data

You can import technology data to add a technology database where one did not exist before, or to overwrite or merge imported data by compiling it into an existing technology database.

## To import technology data:

1. Begin by opening the Technology Manager. From the Console tab, choose Tools &gt; Technology Manager . Alternatively, from the Library Manager, choose Edit &gt; Technology .
2. In the Technology Manager, choose File &gt; Import or click Import The Import Technology dialog box opens.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Note:

For read-only libraries, the File &gt; Import command is disabled to prevent you from modifying the library.

3. Verify that the correct technology Library is chosen. The imported technology data will be stored in the chosen technology library.
4. Browse to find the technology file whose technology you want to import.
5. Choose the import mode:

To replace the currently defined technology for this library (effectively purging the library's technology) with the technology in the file you are importing, choose Full Overwrite .

To partially replace the currently defined technology for this library with the technology in the file you are importing, choose Partial Replace and select the files to replace.

6. Click OK .

in the toolbar.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Libraries with names in bold letters signify those with changed technologies. You can choose File &gt; Revert to reverse any import operation not yet saved. This enables you to change technologies for this session only.

7. Click Save to save the imported technology file to disk.

## Exporting Technology Data

You can export technology data to transfer the data from a library to an existing or new technology file. You can use this process to back up your technology database or to give someone else a copy of the technology you use. You can also use this process when you want to manually edit the technology file for customizing.

1. Begin by opening the Technology Manager. From the Console tab, choose Tools &gt; Technology Manager . Alternatively, from the Library Manager, choose Edit &gt; Technology .
2. In the Technology Manager, choose File &gt; Export or click Export in the toolbar. The Export Technology dialog box opens.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Note:

For read-only libraries, the File &gt; Export command is disabled.

3. Choose the technology Library from which you want to export the technology data.
4. Enter a technology file name or browse to find the technology file to receive the exported technology.

<!-- image -->

5. Select Export Local Tech Only to limit the data exported from the library to newly created, incremental technology data. Do not select this option if you want to write all technology from the library to the file. See Export Incremental Technology Data.
6. Select Include Empty Sections if you want the exported file to contain comment lines that show the syntax of sections even if they do not contain any data. If you decide to use the sections later, you can type data directly in the file without researching the syntax.
7. Click OK .

## Adding a Reference

You can add a technology database reference into the selected technology database.

1. Begin by opening the Technology Manager. From the Console tab, choose Tools &gt; Technology Manager . Alternatively, from the Library Manager, choose Edit &gt; Technology .
2. In the Technology Manager, select a library item.
3. Click Add Reference in the toolbar. A drop-down list of valid technology databases appears under the selected library item.
4. Click a technology database in the list to add it as a reference.
5. Alternatively, you can drag library item from the Library list and drop it into another library item to create a new sub-item. The technology database of the dragged library will be referenced to the technology database of the dropped library.

<!-- image -->

## Deleting a Reference

You can delete a technology database reference from the selected technology database.

1. Begin by opening the Technology Manager. From the Console tab, choose Tools &gt; Technology Manager . Alternatively, from the Library Manager, choose Edit &gt; Technology .
2. In the Technology Manager, select a library item.
3. Click Delete Reference in the toolbar.

<!-- image -->

2. Add or delete references, as described in Adding a Reference and Deleting a Reference.
3. Click Revert

## Displaying the Text Viewer

The Text Viewer opens automatically for many processes. You can also open the Text Viewer any time you want to view process output that generates text, such as log files, and other text files.

## Viewing Job Process Text

You can view text output for all job processes with the Text Viewer.

In the Text Viewer, choose an option:

- To view different files currently opened in the text viewer, choose between the tabs by name.
- To open a text file for viewing, choose File &gt; Open , and browse to choose a file.
- To scroll to the end of a file, use the keyboard end key.
- To display line numbers in the text file, select View &gt; Line Number
- To save a text file with a different name, open it, and then choose File &gt; Save As .
- To enable searching, choose Edit &gt; Find , and enter text and search options at the bottom of the window.
- To switch off the polling function, choose View &gt; Poll .

xt::openTextViewer -text [gi::createBinding -help]

## About the Design Technology Co-optimization

The Design Technology Co-optimization (DTCO) is a feature to aim at a team of engineers who work on making technology and design choices to improve overall design metrics typically during modifications to a process, at the start of new node or a derivative of an existing node. The DTCO solution is a set of features that can be used to define a flow for evaluating choices in process technology, standard cell architecture, and their impact on design. This feature:

- Helps a team assess the impact of the choices on design by providing a unified environment for experimentation and validation.
- Smartly manages the preferences and settings for complex designs.
- Creates and manages multiple process splits for the design with the design collaterals and sample design data to compare the splits for designers.
- Examines individual purpose from full DTCO flow.

The Design Technology Co-optimization (DTCO) flow provides multiple tools to let you conducts repetitive process experiments in a semi-automated way.

<!-- image -->

## Workflow for Design Technology Co-optimization

Before you start the Design Technology Co-optimization (DTCO), see Preparing for Design Technology Co-optimization.

After the preparations, proceed as follows from the DTCO Setup and Run dialog box:

<!-- image -->

|   Step |                                                                                                              | See...                                             |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
|      1 | Specify Parameters .                                                                                         | Setting Up the DTCO Parameters                     |
|      2 | Specify and run Transistor Modeling for baseline computations.                                               | Running Transistor Modeling                        |
|      3 | Specify and run Interconnect Characterization for baseline computations.                                     | Running Interconnect Characterization              |
|      4 | Specify and run Cell Parasitic Extraction for baseline computations.                                         | Running Cell Parasitic Extraction                  |
|      5 | Specify and run Digital Implementation for baseline computations.                                            | Running Digital Implementation                     |
|      6 | After specifying the baseline computations, design new parameters from original data by using Create Split . | Creating a Split                                   |
|      7 | Perform computations in Step 2 to 5 for the split.                                                           | Perform computations in Step 2 to 5 for the split. |

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Step            | See...                  |
|-----------------|-------------------------|
| 8 After Compare | Comparing Split Results |

## Setting Up the DTCO Parameters

You can use the Parameters tab to display, define, import and export values for DTCO parameters.

All DTCO parameters are stored with the library in its data.dm file. If a parameter affects the layout of any cell in the library, then that becomes a CDF parameter. A DTCO parameter can be dependent on one or more DTCO parameters. This dependency is captured by a Tcl expression sting as the value and has a Type called expression . A DTCO parameter is independent if the value is not a Tcl expression string and a Type other than expression .

This topic describes the following:

- Displaying and Filtering the DTCO Parameters
- Adding and Editing DTCO Parameters
- Exporting and Importing DTCO Parameters
- Loading DTCO Parameters
- Saving DTCO Parameters

## Displaying and Filtering the DTCO Parameters

You can view the DTCO parameters in the Parameters tab to begin to work with them.

To view parameters:

1. In the Parameters tab, choose library in the Library selection field. In a DTCO flow, all the DTCO parameters are defined, created, and stored in the reference library.
2. Choose Import (Exporting and Importing DTCO Parameters) or Load (Loading DTCO Parameters) to import the stored parameters.
3. All the parameters associated with the library are displayed in the parameters table.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The parameters table shows the following parameter information: Prompt , Name , Category , Type , Value , Collection , Measure , Unit , SWB Name , Variability Type , Var Value , and Layout Parameter Name . To edit the parameter value, see Adding and Editing DTCO Parameters.

You can filter the parameters table by Category column. To filter the parameters table, specify the string in the Filter by Category text field. After specifying the string in the text field, the tool lists the DTCO parameters that match the filter criteria.

<!-- image -->

## Adding and Editing DTCO Parameters

To edit DTCO parameters in the parameters table:

1. Double-click any column in the parameter table to display the Edit Parameter dialog box. Or click the button to enable the Edit Parameter dialog box.
2. Edit the parameters in the Edit Parameter dialog box and click OK to implement the changes.

<!-- image -->

To add DTCO parameters in the parameters table:

1. Right-click the parameter table to display the menu as below.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Or click the button to enable the Add Parameter dialog box.

<!-- image -->

2. Specify the parameter information in the Add Parameter dialog box.
3. Click OK to add new parameters.

The parameters that have been changed and added appear in red with italic type.

<!-- image -->

4. Save the design after editing. See Saving DTCO Parameters.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

If switching the library without saving the changes, the Save Library dialog box is displayed to save or discard the changes.

<!-- image -->

## Parameters Toolbars

Parameters toolbars let you quick edit the parameter table. Performs add parameter, delete, move, and edit the parameters in the table.

<!-- image -->

## Exporting and Importing DTCO Parameters

You can export the DTCO parameters to a YAML file by choosing the Export option. The Export dialog box is displayed to specify the library.

<!-- image -->

The exported parameters information can be edited by text editor.

## Here is the example of YAML file:

```
#DTCO Parameters Version:0.0 Parameters: cellArchitecture: prompt:Cell Architecture type:string collection:list value:shortmedium tall layoutParameterName:cellStyle cellHeightMultiplier: prompt:CellHeightMultiplier type:float collection:list value:5.56.57.5 cellHeight: prompt:Cel1 Height type:expression collection:list value: -"[lindex$cellHeightMultiplier0]*$mOPitch" -"[lindex$cellHeightMultiplier1]*$mOPitch" -"[lindex$cellHeightMultiplier 2]*$mOPitch" measure:length unit:nm
```

When the YAML file is created in the associated library, you can import the parameters saved in the YAML file.

<!-- image -->

To import a YAML file:

1. Choose Import to display the Import dialog box.
2. Choose the YAML file in the associated library in the Import dialog box.
3. The parameters are displayed in the parameters table.

<!-- image -->

## Loading DTCO Parameters

To load the stored parameters:

1. Select a library in the Library selection field.
2. Choose Load to load the data.dm associated with the library from disk.
3. The stored parameters are displayed in the parameter table.

## Saving DTCO Parameters

You can save the edited or imported DTCO parameters by choosing the Save option. The parameters are saved in a data.dm file associated with the library. Running any computation flows from other DTCO tabs would only consume the saved parameters or values.

<!-- image -->

## Running Transistor Modeling

This feature creates a spice model using the TCAD tools. To generate a compact spice mode, you need IV CV data for the transistor geometry and its corresponding material description.

## Note:

The transistor modeling flow does not need any layout design.

In the transistor modeling flow, you can choose to run:

- Only the IV CV data generation.
- Or only the Compact Model generation.
- Or both IV CV data and Compact Model generations.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## To create transistor modeling:

1. Specify the directory in the Run Root Dir field where files related to IV CV curve and the Compact Model generation are stored.
2. Enable IV CV to select IV CV curve generation or disable IV CV to ignore the IV CV curve generation.

To run the IV CV curve generation, specify the following settings:

| Option             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Run Mode           | Specifies one of the following modes: ◦ gui: Select this option to launch the Sentaurus Workbench Graphical User Interface. The Transistor Modeling need to be run manually. ◦ batch: Select this option to run in the background and status can be checked in Job Monitor. |
| Queue              | To select the Queue name where the computation would be performed.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| DTCO Parameters    | Library : Specifies the library to load the DTCO parameters for the transistor modeling. Category : When the library of DTCO parameters is specified, the parameters in the transistor category are used.                                                                   |
| Template Directory | Specifies the directory contains the files for Sentaurus TCAD tool to run the transistor modeling.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Tech Type          | Specifies the technology name or label.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Variability        | The Nominal option is specified.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Threads            | Specifies the number of threads.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Project Name       | This filed is automatically populated by Tech Type and Variability .                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

3. Enable Compact Model to select Compact Model generation or disable Compact Model to ignore the Compact Model generation.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## To run the Compact Model generation, specify the following settings:

| Option             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Run Mode           | Specifies one of the following modes: ◦ gui: Select this option to launch the Sentaurus Workbench Graphical User Interface. The Transistor Modeling need to be run manually. ◦ batch: Select this option to run in the background and status can be checked in Job Monitor.                                     |
| Queue              | To select the Queue name where the computation would be performed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Path File          | This field is enabled when Compact Model is checked and IV CV is not checked. Specifies the file which contains information for IV CV run. If IV CV is checked, the path information is passed from IV CV run to Compact Model run.                                                                             |
| DTCO Parameters    | Library : Specifies the library to load the DTCO parameters for compact model generation. If IV CV is checked, the library of DTCO parameters is passed from IV CV run to Compact Model run. Category : When the library of DTCO parameters is specified, the parameters in the compactModel category are used. |
| Template Directory | Specifies the directory contains the files for Sentaurus TCAD tool to run the compact model generation.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Project Name       | The final spice file of Compact Model run is stored with the Project Name directory in the Run Root Directory.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Save in Library    | Enables the option to save a cell view of the final spice model in the DTCO Library with specified Cell Name .                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

4. Click Run to process the transistor modeling flow.

## Running Interconnect Characterization

The interconnect characterization flow builds an integration with the TCAD tools to create interconnect structures, simulate through the process flow, run field extraction and create an ITF file. The ITF is compiled with grdgenxo (StarRC) to prepare a NXTGRD file which can be used in the digital implementation flow.

<!-- image -->

To create or update a NXTGRD file for parasitic extraction in the implementation flow, specify the following options and fields:

<!-- image -->

| Option       | Description                                                                                       |
|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Run Root Dir | Specify the directory where files related to Interconnect Characterization generation are stored. |

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

| Option             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Run Mode           | Specify the Run Mode by selecting one of the following options: • gui : Select this option to manually run the Interconnect Characterization in the Sentaurus Workbench graphical user interface. • batch : Select this option to run the Interconnect Characterization in the background and check the result in Job Monitor. |
| DTCO Parameters    | Specify the Library to load the DTCO parameters for Interconnect characterization.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Project Name       | When specifying the Project Name , the directory with project name is created in Run Root Dir to run the Interconnect Characterization.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Template Directory | Specifies the directory contains the files for Sentaurus TCAD tool to run the Interconnect Characterization.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Flow File          | Specifies the file contains the layer information with correct layer order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Headers File       | Specifies the file contains the information (technology, foundry, process node, process version, process type, process corner, and temperature) regarding the ITF header.                                                                                                                                                      |
| Materials File     | Specifies the file contains information (dielectrics, conductors, bulk resistivity model parameters, bulk resistivity, and temperature dependence) about the physical properties specific to the material needs to be simulated in the Sentaurus Workbench.                                                                    |
| Processes          | Specifies the number of jobs to be launched to run the Interconnect Characterization.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Save in Library    | The output of Interconnect characterization (NXTGRD, ITF) files are placed in interconnect_results directory. If this option is enabled and Cell Name is provided, the tool creates cell views of NXTGRD and ITF files in the DTCO Parameters Library .                                                                        |

To generate the output of Interconnect characterization, click Run to process the implementation flow.

## Running Digital Implementation

The Digital Implementation defines a set of sample digital designs to be run through the implementation flow. The step abstracts the notion of implementation and lets you define scripts that achieve the result. You can specify the following information in this tab:

- Fusion Compiler Technology File
- NDM Libraries (timing, power and physical information related to standard cells)
- Parasitic Files (TLU+ or NXTGRD)

Two methods are provided for the optimization: a simplified but less flexible step or a fully customized script by using Custom Script option.

1. Simplified Digital Implementation Flow: In this flow, you specify the library and design name, directory path where all verilog files are available, a config file, a compile file, QoR directory, and QoR result file. The tool generates a simple script to run these into an 'fc\_shell', and then invoke the QoR script on the results generated by Fusion Compiler. It requires users to put specific setup and place and route tcl flows in the config file and compile file in exchange for simple flow.
2. Custom Script Flow: A production digital implementation flow relies on other automation elements, such as makefiles, grid management, environment variables. In this flow, you specify the library and design name, and a custom script. The script is an entry point for you to setup and manage the complexities of a production flow. The tool passes rest of the arguments filled in the Digital Implementation tab as a YAML file to this script. The script may parse and get values from this YAML file.

The output of Fusion Compiler is analyzed to generate a YAML file which contains relevant key-value pairs for comparing in Compare Split . See Comparing Split Results.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

To run the Digital Implementation, specify the following options and fields:

1. Specify the directory in the Run Root Dir field where files related to Digital Implementation are stored.
2. Specify a file contains technology-specific information such as names, characteristics for each metal layer, and design rules in the Tech File field. This information are required to route a design.
3. Specify NDM libraries that contain the timing, power and physical information related to standard cells in the Reference Libraries section. You can add the reference library by clicking Click to Add . You can enable the library in the Enable column to specify what libraries are reference.

<!-- image -->

You also can use the toolbars to adjust the Reference Libraries table. The table includes the following options:

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

|----------|------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|          | Check Selected   | Lets you enable the selected libraries to be reference libraries.                                                  |
|          | Uncheck Selected | Lets you disable the selected libraries to be reference libraries.                                                 |
|          | Add File         | Lets you add a new row and open the Select Library dialog box to specify the reference library in the created row. |
|          | Delete Selected  | Lets you delete the selected row.                                                                                  |
|          | Move Top         | Lets you move the selected row to the start of the table.                                                          |

|          | Move Down        | Lets you move the selected row down.                                                                               |

4. Specify the mapping file in the Layer Map File field. The mapping file contains physical layer mapping information between the input database and the specified NXTGRD file.

(Optional) Specify NXTGRD or TLU+ files that contain the modeled layers of a circuit. You can add the files by clicking Click to Add and enable the file in the Enable column to specify what files are used. You can use the toolbar to adjust the Parasitic Files table. See Table 108.

5. In the Designs section, enable the Custom Script option to specify the script which contains the information to run the Fusion Compiler in the Designs table. Or disable the Custom Script option to specify RTL, Config files, Compile files and output QOR(Result) directory in the Designs table.

6. Specify the directory in the QOR Exec field. The Quality of Result exec file parses the QOR result directory and constructs the QOR.yaml file (see Figure 55) used for Compare Split. See Comparing Split Results.
